[150] ﴿And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, so that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who do wrong. So do not fear them, but fear Me, and so that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided.﴾

﴿And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾ means: so that no one may argue against you concerning your turning to other than it, and so that their disputing with you may cease, like the saying of the Jews, for example: "He denies our religion and follows our qibla!" and the saying of others: "He claims the creed of Ibrahim and opposes his qibla!" So when you pray toward it, there will be no argument for them against you.

Al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani) said: By His saying, ﴿And indeed it is the truth from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 149], He pointed to the confirmation of what preceded. He made clear that since wisdom requires that every bearer of a law have a qibla specific to him, and you are a bearer of a law, then changing the qibla for you is a truth from your Lord. (Then he said): If it is said: Why did He repeat His saying: ﴿and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾? It is said: One of the two (statements) urges turning toward the qibla, with heart and body, in whatever place a person may be, whether far from it or near to it. This is the outcome of choice and ability. The other urges turning with the heart alone when the qibla is uncertain, and in voluntary prayer during ease, while riding and traveling.

﴿except those of them who do wrong﴾: for they display wickedness and obstinacy in this matter, through stubbornness. They are either the Jews, referred to earlier as the People of the Book, or the hypocrites, or the polytheists, as was recounted earlier regarding "the foolish ones." It was among the saying of the Jews, as related by Qatada: "The man longed for the house of his father and the religion of his people." And among the saying of the polytheists, as related by Mujahid: "He has returned to your qibla, so he will soon return to your religion." (p-٣٠٩) The saying of the hypocrites has already been mentioned. In sum, they all found fault and engaged in idle talk. ﴿So do not fear them﴾: do not fear their disputation. ﴿but fear Me﴾: so do not oppose My command. ﴿and so that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ by turning toward the most complete of directions, which encompasses the clear signs and security. ﴿and that you may be guided﴾ to the straight path by turning toward it, so that you may be guided by this qibla with complete guidance.

Al-Harrali (al-Harali) said: Within it is a glad tiding of the conquest of Makkah and his mastery over the whole Arabian Peninsula, and his empowerment thereby over the rest of the people of the earth, since Islam would engulf all the Arabs, through whom God would open for him the easts and wests of the earth, which the dominion of his community would reach.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[151] ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from among yourselves, reciting to you Our verses, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know.﴾

"As We have sent among you a messenger from among yourselves." His words "among you" (fikum) are meant to refer to the Arabs, and likewise His words "from among yourselves" (minkum).

In His sending him among them and from among them there are great blessings upon them, because of the honour they gain thereby. Moreover, it is well known of the Arabs that they have an intense disdain (al-anafa) for submitting to others. So God the Exalted sent him from among their own midst, so that they would be closer to accepting him. "Reciting to you Our verses": he reads the Qur'an to you, which is among the greatest of blessings, because it is a lasting miracle, and because it is recited, through which acts of worship are fulfilled, and from which all the sciences and the comprehensive praiseworthy morals are derived; thus through its recitation come all the good things of this world and the next. "Purifying you": that is, He cleanses you from polytheism (shirk), the deeds of the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyya), and base morals. "Teaching you the Book": this is the Qur'an. This is not a repetition, because reciting the Qur'an to them is other than teaching it to them. "And wisdom": this is knowledge of the whole of the Sharia, which the Qur'an contains in detail. For this reason al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said: "Wisdom (al-hikma) is the Sunnah of the Messenger." His words "and teaching you what you did not know" are a reminder that God the Exalted sent His Messenger at a time of hiatus (fatra) between the messengers and of ignorance among the nations, when people were bewildered and astray regarding their religions. So God the Exalted sent the Prophet with the truth, until he taught them what they needed in their religion, and they became the most profoundly knowledgeable of people, the most righteous in heart, the least affected, and the most truthful in speech. This is among the greatest kinds of blessings. God the Exalted said: ﴿Certainly God conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164], and so on. He censured those who did not recognise the value of this blessing, saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By the blessing of God he means Muhammad ﷺ." For this reason God urged the believers to acknowledge this blessing and to requite it by remembering Him and giving thanks to Him. And He said:

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[152] ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me, and do not deny Me.﴾

﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me, and do not deny Me.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, "Remember Me, O believers, by your obedience to Me in what I command you and in what I forbid you. I will remember you with My mercy toward you and My forgiveness of you." Some scholars interpreted it as meaning remembrance through praise and commendation. Al-Qashani said: "Remember Me through response and obedience; I will remember you with increase and continuous favor." This has the same meaning as what precedes it. As for His words, "and be grateful to Me," Ibn Jarir said: That is, "be grateful to Me for what I have bestowed upon you of Islam and of guidance to the religion that I have legislated." His words, "and do not deny Me," mean: do not conceal My kindness to you, lest I take away from you the blessing that I have bestowed upon you.

Al-Samarqandi said: That is, "be grateful for My blessing: that I sent among you a Messenger from among you, who recites to you Our verses, purifies you, and teaches you the Book and wisdom. Do not deny this blessing." It is also said: the true blessing is knowledge. Everything else is merely a shift from one comfort to another, and is not a blessing. And the seeker of knowledge never tires of it; rather, he seeks more of it. So God's command to give thanks for this blessing is the blessing of sending a Messenger who teaches them the Book and wisdom, as al-Harrali related. Since the Arabs had a passion for mentioning their forefathers and their battles, God made His remembrance of them a substitute for what they used to mention, just as He made His Book a substitute for their poetry, and He stirred their resolve toward this by what would please them: His mention of them.

Imam Ahmad related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: I am with My servant when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in his self, I remember him in My Self; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs. If he draws near to Me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit; and if he draws near to Me by a cubit, I draw near to him by a fathom. And if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running." Its isnad (chain of narration) is sound (sahih), and al-Bukhari also narrated it.

Muslim related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah that they both testified concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No people sit remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them to those who are with Him."

The narrations concerning the virtue of remembrance are abundant, and this noble verse suffices in this regard.

(Note) Al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Know that the excellence of remembrance is not limited to glorification (tasbih), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), praise (tahmid), magnification (takbir), and the like. Rather, every person who performs an act of obedience to Allah is a person who remembers Allah.

This was also said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, and other scholars. 'Ata', may Allah have mercy on him, said: The gatherings of remembrance are the gatherings of what is lawful and unlawful: How do you buy and sell? How do you pray and fast? How do you marry and divorce? And the like of these. Al-Nawawi also said: The prescribed invocations (adhkar) in prayer and other than it, whether obligatory or recommended, are not counted nor considered valid unless one pronounces them audibly enough that one hears oneself, if one's hearing is sound and there is no impediment. Groups of the imams have composed precious books on the daily and nightly acts of worship. Among the most comprehensive for later scholars is the Book of Invocations (Kitab al-Adhkar) by al-Nawawi. And among those who gathered the essence of what was narrated in this subject was Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in Zad al-Ma'ad. He said at the beginning of that: The Prophet (ﷺ) was the most complete of creation in remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, all of his speech was in the remembrance of Allah and what is related to it. His commands, prohibitions, and legislation for the community were a remembrance of Allah from him. His reports about the names, attributes, rulings, actions, promise, and threat of the Lord were a remembrance of Him from him. His praise of Him for His bounties, His glorification, and His extolling of Him were a remembrance of Him from him. His asking, supplicating to Him, desiring Him, and fearing Him were a remembrance of Him from him. His stillness and silence were a remembrance of Him in his heart. Thus the remembrance of Allah was in all his times and in all his states. His remembrance of Allah flowed with his breaths, standing, sitting, lying on his side, in his walking and riding, his travel and descent, his departure and his settling. End of quote.

As for the innovated invocations and the blameworthy practices of listening (sama'), such as listening with clapping of hands and drums, the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un) who followed them in goodness, and the other great imams of the religion, did not make this a means of drawing near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. They did not count it among the acts of devotion and obedience; rather, they counted it among the reprehensible innovations (bid'ah). To the point that al-Shafi'i said: "In Baghdad I left behind something that the heretics (zanadiqa) invented, which they call al-taghbir, by which they divert people from the Qur'an." The righteous friends of Allah, who know Him, recognize this and know that Shaytan has a great share in it. For this reason, the best of those who attended it repented from it, and whoever was further from knowledge and from the perfection of Allah's friendship, Shaytan's share in it was greater. Listening to singing and frivolous entertainment is among the greatest things that strengthen satanic states, and it is the listening of the polytheists. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping﴾ [al-Anfal: 35]. Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and others among the early generations said: al-tasdiyah is clapping with the hands, and al-muka' is like whistling. The polytheists used to take this as worship. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), his worship was what Allah commanded: prayer, recitation, remembrance, and the like, and lawful gatherings. The Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions never gathered to listen to singing at all, neither with clapping of hands, nor with drums, nor with ecstatic movement (tawajud). When the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered, they would order one of them to recite, and the rest would listen. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: "Remind us of our Lord," and he would recite while they listened. The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari while he was reciting, and said to him: "I passed by you last night while you were reciting, and I began listening to your recitation." He said: "If I had known that you were listening, I would have embellished it (habbartuhu) for you embellishment." That is, I would have beautified it for you. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices." And he (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more attentive (ashadd udhunan, i.e., more attentive in listening) to a man with a beautiful voice reciting the Qur'an aloud than the owner of a singing girl is to his singing girl."

From 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes." So I recited Surah al-Nisa' until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41]. He said: "That is enough for now." I turned and saw that his eyes were shedding tears.

Such listening is the listening of the Prophets and their followers, as Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in His Book, saying: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping﴾ [Maryam: 58]. And Allah, the Exalted, said concerning the people of knowledge: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83]. And He, glorified is He, praised the people of this listening for what they attain of increased faith, the trembling of the skin, and the flow of tears. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeating. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2]. So the opposite of this listening is from the falsehood which He forbade. For this reason, the three generations which the Prophet (ﷺ) praised did not do it, nor did the great shaykhs do it. So let whoever is among the lowest group in the path of his poverty (before Allah) awaken, and let him accompany one who is among the highest companions up to the resting of his grave; and let him heal the wounds caused by his innovation by following the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ) and adhering to his Sunnah.

Know that the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, sometimes occurs for His greatness, from which arises awe and reverence. Sometimes it occurs for His power, from which arises fear and sorrow. Sometimes for His blessing, from which arises gratitude; and for this it has been said: "Remembering a blessing is its thanks." And sometimes for His dazzling acts, from which arises lessons. So it is the duty of the believer never to be separated from the remembrance of Him, the Exalted, in one of these aspects.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And be grateful to Me, and do not deny Me﴾, it contains a command to thank Him for His blessings and not to deny them. (Here kufr means concealing the blessing, not disbelief in the sense of denial.) He, the Exalted, has promised increase of good in return for gratitude, saying: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you deny, indeed My punishment is severe﴾ [Ibrahim: 7]. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "Ushkuru li and ushkuruni have one meaning. But 'li' is more eloquent and more common with shukr (gratitude)."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 153:

(p-316) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[153] ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾ Exalted is He guided the believers, following the command to give thanks in the previous verse, to seek help through patience and prayer. This is because the servant is either in a blessing, so he gives thanks for it, or in a calamity, so he is patient with it. As has come in the hadith: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for no decree is decreed for him except that it is good for him. If prosperity befalls him and he gives thanks, it is good for him; and if adversity befalls him and he is patient, it is good for him." And Exalted is He made clear that the best things one can seek help with in bearing calamities in the way of Allah are patience and prayer, as has preceded in His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45]. And in the hadith: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever a matter distressed him, would pray." Then, patience is of two kinds: patience in abstaining from what is forbidden and sinful, and patience in performing acts of obedience and devotion. The second is greater in reward, because it is the intended goal. As for the third kind of patience, which is patience over calamities and misfortunes, it too is obligatory, like seeking forgiveness for faults.

(p-317) The Imam Ibn Taymiyyah said in his book (al-Siyasah al-Shar'iyyah): The greatest aid for the ruler in particular, and for others in general, is three matters. The first is sincerity to Allah, and placing trust in Him through supplication and other means; and the root of this is guarding the prayer with the heart and the body. The second is kindness to creation through benefit and wealth, which is zakah. The third is patience over harm from people and other calamities. For this reason Allah often combines prayer and patience, as in His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], and His saying: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early part of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud: 114], ﴿And be patient, for indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ [Hud: 115], and His saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. As for His linking prayer and zakah in the Qur'an, it is very frequent. Thus, by upholding prayer, zakah and patience, the condition of the ruler and the ruled is set right. When a person understands what enters into these comprehensive terms, he enters into prayer the remembrance of Allah, supplicating to Him, reciting His Book, sincerity of religion to Him, and trust in Him; and into zakah, kindness to creation with wealth and benefit: from supporting the oppressed, aiding the distressed, and meeting the needs of the needy. And into patience: bearing harm, restraining anger, pardoning people, opposing desire, and abandoning evil and insolence. End.

﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ Imam Ibn Taymiyyah said in (Sharh Hadith al-Nuzul): The term "being with" (ma'iyyah) in the Book of Allah comes in a general sense, as in His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid: 4], and in His saying (p-318) ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7], up to His saying: ﴿but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7]. And it comes in a specific sense, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl: 128], His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46], and His saying: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40]. If the intended meaning were His essence being with everything, the generality would contradict the specification. For it is known that His saying: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40] intended by it the specification of Himself and Abu Bakr, to the exclusion of their enemies among the disbelievers. Likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl: 128]; He specified them with this to the exclusion of the wrongdoers and the wicked.

Also, the term "being with" is not used in the language of the Arabs, nor in any part of the Qur'an, to mean the mixing of one essence (p-319) with the other, as in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ [al-Fath: 29], His saying: ﴿Then those are with the believers﴾ [al-Nisa: 146], His saying: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 119], and His saying: ﴿and strive with your wealth﴾ [al-Anfal: 75]; and the like of this is abundant. Thus it is impossible that His saying "and He is with you" indicates that His essence is mixed with the essences of the creation.

He has expounded this matter elsewhere and clarified that the term "being with" in the language, although it implies association, companionship and accompaniment, when it is with the servants, does not contradict His being above His Throne. Its ruling in every situation is according to what suits it: He is with all creation by knowledge, power and dominion, and He specifies some of them with aid, support and strengthening. End, abridged.

[p. 320]

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the exegetical explanation) of His statement, Exalted is He:

[154] ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.﴾ [154]

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.﴾ forbids His believing servants from calling the martyrs "dead," meaning those whose souls have perished, who have lost life, whose pleasures have ceased, and who have become like inert objects, as the meaning of "dead" suggests. He, glorified is He, commands them to say to them: "The living," because they are alive in the presence of their Lord, being provided for, as He, Exalted is He, said in Al 'Imran: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169] ﴿rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty and receiving good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Al 'Imran: 170] ﴿They receive good tidings of a favor from Allah and bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 171]. So His statement in this verse, "with their Lord," explains the intended meaning of their life: that is, it is for their souls, in His presence, Exalted is He. His statement "but you do not perceive" means you do not perceive their life of the barzakh (the intermediate state) after their death, since nothing of it appears in their bodies, although it preserves some of them from decay, just as you see sleepers motionless and not moving. There is no greater pride than this in this world, nor a more pleasant life than it in the Hereafter.

Al-Harrali said: "It is as if He, Exalted is He, negates from the warrior (*mujahid*) the experience of what is disliked in every respect, even to the point that he be called 'dead.' So He protects him from the speech which, to them, is among the most grievous things to their selves, because their selves are bound to a beautiful remembrance." End of quotation.

For this reason al-Asamm said: "That is, do not name them 'the dead.' Say to them: 'The martyrs, the living.'" Al-Raghib al-Isfahani said: "Life has several aspects, and each of them is opposed by a death. (The first) is the growing power (*al-quwwah al-namiyah*) by which nourishment and the desire for it occur. This exists in plants, animals and humans. For this reason it is said: 'a living plant.'

(The second) is the sensory power (*al-quwwah al-hassah*) by which spatial movement occurs. It is found in animals but not in plants.

(The third) is the active, rational power (*al-quwwah al-'amilah al-'aqilah*). It is found in humans but not in animals or plants. By it obligation (*taklif*) is connected. It may also be said of acquired knowledge and righteous action that they are 'life.' On this basis is His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. It has also been said: 'The one who does good is alive, even if he is in the abode of the dead, and the one who does evil is dead, even if he is in the abode of the living.'"

(He) said: "Let us return to the meaning of the verse and say: They have agreed that there is not established for them the life by which growth and nourishment occur, nor the life by which sensation occurs, for the absence of these two in the dead is perceptible and intelligible. Some exegetes considered the life specific to the human being and said: This life is specific to the power called at times the spirit (*ruh*) and at times the soul (*nafs*). He said: The death that is witnessed is the separation of this power, which is the spirit, from the body. So whenever the person is good, he is blessed with his spirit, rejoicing in his place until the Day of Resurrection. If he is evil, he is punished through it. To this the wise have gone and they have demonstrated it with proofs and evidences. This is the position of the people of hadith (*ashab al-hadith*). The reports and verses transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) confirm its soundness. Indeed, all the religious communities (*milal*) have gone to it."

Among what indicates its soundness is the report: "The spirits are armies mobilized; whatever among them recognizes one another becomes harmonious, and whatever among them does not recognize one another differs." And what is narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (ʿAli ibn Abi Talib), may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah created the spirits two thousand years before the bodies." And it is narrated that "when those among the chieftains of Quraysh who were killed on the day of Badr were killed and gathered into a well, the Prophet (ﷺ) came and addressed them, saying: 'Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Do you address corpses?' He said: 'You are not more hearing than them, but if they were able, they would answer.'" And other reports besides these.

And He, Exalted is He, said concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿They are exposed to the Fire morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. This refers to the time before the Day of Resurrection, because He said at the end of the verse: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46] End of quotation.

In al-Baydawi and its glosses: "The affirmation of life for the martyrs at a time when the body has perished and the structure has decayed, together with the negation of their perception of it, is evidence that their life is not the body, nor of the kind of animal life, for that is through soundness of the structure and balance of temperament. Rather, it is a matter known through revelation, not through reason." End of quotation.

Revelation has indeed come with an explanation of their life, as we have mentioned. Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah, Exalted is He, have mercy on him, said in *Kitab al-Ruh* (The Book of the Spirit): "Allah, glorified is He, has informed about the martyrs that they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. This is the life of their spirits, and their provision for it is continuous, for otherwise the bodies have been torn apart. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained this life: that their spirits are in the bellies of green birds which have lamps suspended beneath the Throne, roaming the Garden wherever they wish, then returning to those lamps. Their Lord looked upon them with a look and said: 'Do you desire anything?' They said: 'What is it that we could desire, while we roam the Garden wherever we wish?' He did this with them three times. When they saw that they would not be left alone unless they were asked, they said: 'O Lord! We wish that our spirits be returned to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your way once more!' When He saw that they had no need, they were left alone." And it is authentically reported from him (ﷺ): "The spirits of the martyrs are in green birds that feed on the fruit of the Garden" (and *taʻlaqu* is with a *damma* on the *lam*, that is, they eat the *ʻalaqah*, the tree-fruit). This is clear about their eating, drinking, movement, transfer, and speech. End of quotation.

Al-Tibi said: The Prophet's (ﷺ) statement, "Their spirits are in the bellies of green birds," means that after their spirits have separated from their bodies, Allah creates for their spirits forms in that appearance which are attached to them and serve as substitutes for their bodies, so that they reach what they desire of sensual pleasures.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Kitab al-Ruh*: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made the abodes three: the abode of this world, the abode of the barzakh, and the abode of permanence. He made for each abode rulings specific to it. He composed this human being of a body and a soul, and made the rulings of the abode of this world apply to the bodies, with the spirits following them. For this reason He made His legal rulings dependent upon what appears of the movements of the tongue and the limbs, even if the souls conceal something contrary to it.

He made the rulings of the barzakh apply to the spirits, and the bodies follow them. Just as the spirits followed the bodies in the rulings of this world, so they were pained by its pain and delighted by its comfort, and it was they who directly experienced the causes of bliss and punishment, so the bodies follow the spirits in their bliss and punishment. In that state, the spirits are the ones who directly experience punishment and bliss, so the bodies there are apparent and the spirits are hidden. The bodies are like graves for them. There, the spirits are apparent and the bodies are hidden in their graves. Thus the rulings of the barzakh apply to the spirits, and you see their bodies receiving bliss and punishment, just as the rulings of this world applied to the bodies, and you see their spirits receiving bliss and punishment. So comprehend this matter with knowledge and understand it as it should be understood, and every doubt that arises for you from within or without will go away. Allah, glorified is He, has shown us through His kindness, mercy and guidance an example of this in this world in the state of the sleeper. What he is blessed with or punished with in his sleep applies to his spirit primarily, and the body follows it. It may grow strong until it affects the body in a visible way, so the sleeper sees that he was struck in his sleep, and in the morning the marks of the blow are on his body. He sees that he has eaten and drunk, and he wakes to find the trace of food and drink in his mouth, and his hunger and thirst are gone.

Even more wondrous is that you see the sleeper rise from his sleep and strike, seize and defend himself, as though he were awake, while he is asleep and has no awareness of any of that. Because the ruling, once applied to the spirit, seeks the help of the body from outside it; if it had entered it, he would have awakened and felt it.

If the spirit suffers and enjoys, and this reaches its body by way of following, then likewise in the barzakh, and even more so. For the spirit's separateness there is more complete and stronger, and it is attached to its body, not severed from it entirely. When the day of the gathering of bodies comes, and people rise from their graves, the ruling, the bliss and the punishment upon spirits and bodies become manifest and clear. When you give this matter its due, it will become clear to you that what the Messenger reported of the punishment of the grave and its bliss, its narrowness and its spaciousness, its squeezing, and that it is a pit from the pits of the Fire or a garden from the gardens of Paradise, is consistent with reason, and that it is true without any doubt. And whoever finds this difficult to understand, it is due to the poorness of his understanding and the scarcity of his knowledge." End of quotation.

(p-325) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[155] ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits. And give good tidings to the patient.﴾ [156] ﴿Who, when disaster strikes them, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 156]

His saying, exalted is He, "And We will surely test you with something," is addressed to those who believed along with the Prophet (ﷺ). They were singled out for it, although it includes those like them, because they are the ones directly engaged in the call (da'wah) and in jihad (striving in the way of Allah), and in confronting the wicked. Every person who stands upright for the truth and calls to it is exposed to being tested with what has been mentioned, all of it or part of it. The tanwin here indicates diminution: that is, with a little of each of these trials and a portion of it. He mentioned it as little so as to inform that every trial that befalls a person, however great it is, has beyond it something smaller than it. It also serves to lighten the matter for them and to show them that His mercy is with them in every state and never leaves them. He informed them of it before it occurred so that they would prepare their souls for it and their certainty would increase when they witnessed it, just as they were told, and so that they would know that it is a small matter with a praiseworthy outcome. "Of fear" means the fear of the enemy and the spreading of rumours about it. "And hunger" means poverty, due to being occupied with jihad, or the loss of provisions, when you are in a detachment (sariyyah) striving in the way of Allah. This used to happen to them for days, when they would sustain themselves with a single date. "And loss of wealth" means that, because they were cut off from tending their orchards by jihad, or because some of it was lost through the emigration (hijrah) and some of it was left behind in the city from which they emigrated. "And lives" means by their being killed as martyrs in the way of Allah, or by losing limbs in it. "And fruits" means that the gardens would not yield as they customarily did, due to their absence from them in the way of Allah and the loss of the one who would tend them. It was singled out for mention because it is the greatest of the wealth of the Ansar, who are the people most specifically intended by this mention, especially at the time these verses were revealed, which was the earliest period of the hijrah. So all of this and the like is that by which Allah tests His servants, as He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are steadfast﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. Al-Raghib said: this verse encompasses all the trials of this world; that is, if one looks at the generality of each individual item mentioned in it, and sets aside the specifics of the addressees within it, by what its preceding context indicates.

Then He explained what the patient have with Him by His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the patient﴾ ﴿Who, when disaster [musibah] strikes them,﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 156]. Musibah: an active participle from "asabahu shiddah," meaning it overtook him; that is, like these trials. "They say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah'," meaning in ownership and creation, so we should not fear anyone other than Him, since He prevails over all; or we should not be concerned about hunger, because the servant's provision is upon his master, so if it is withheld for a time, it must return to him. Our wealth, our lives and our fruits are His possession, so He may dispose of them as He wills. "And indeed to Him we will return" in the Hereafter. Thus we obtain with Him what He has deprived us of, for He does not waste the reward of the good-doers. The one afflicted finds his calamity easier when he consoles himself with this saying, and conceives of what he was created for and that he returns to his Lord, recalls Allah's blessings upon him, and sees that what He has left him is many times what He has taken back. Al-Raghib said: By "saying" he does not mean the utterance alone, for uttering it while in ugly distress and rejecting the decree is of no benefit at all. Rather, he means conceiving of what man was created for, intending it, and belittling what stands in the path of reaching it. So He commanded that good tidings be given to those who acquire the true sciences, conceive of them, intend this aim, and prepare their souls for it.

(Then he said) If it is said: Why did you say that the command to patience requires knowledge? It is said: patience in reality only occurs for one who knows the excellence of what he seeks.

**(p. 327)** The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[157] ﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy. And those are the ones who are guided.﴾

"Those" (أُولَئِكَ) refers to the patient, in view of their having the qualities that were mentioned. "Upon them are blessings from their Lord" (عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِن رَبِّهِمْ).

Al-Raghib said: *Salah* (blessing), although in origin it means supplication, is from God in one sense blessing and in another sense forgiveness. Al-Razi said: *Salah* from God is praise, commendation, and exaltation. Al-Raghib said: He said "*salawat*" in the plural to draw attention to its abundance from Him, and that it is found in this world as divine success and guidance, and in the Hereafter as reward and forgiveness. "And mercy" (وَرَحْمَةٌ) is great in this world, as a recompense for their affliction. "And those are the ones who are guided" (وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ), that is, to fulfilling the right of *rububiyya* (lordship, God's sovereignty as Lord) and *ubudiyya* (servanthood). So God must bestow upon them His blessings and His mercy.

**(Note.)** Many hadiths have been related concerning the reward for *istirja'* (saying "Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return" at calamities) and for the reward of the patient. Among them is what is in Sahih Muslim from Umm Salamah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "No servant who is struck by a calamity and says, 'Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return. O God, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,' except that God will reward him in his calamity and replace it for him with something better." She said: When Abu Salamah died, I said: "Who is better than Abu Salamah, the companion of the Messenger of God?" Then God inclined me to say it. She said: Then I married the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad related from al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No Muslim man or Muslim woman is afflicted by a calamity and then remembers it, even if its time has passed, and so does *istirja'* for it, except that God renews for him at that moment and gives him the like of its reward on the day he was afflicted by it."

**(p. 328)** Imam Ahmad also related with his chain from Abu Sinan, who said: "I buried a son of mine, and while I was in the grave, Abu Talhah (meaning al-Khawlani) took hold of my hand and brought me out and said: 'Shall I not give you good news?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: Al-Dahhak ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Arzab related to me from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'God, exalted is He, says: O Angel of Death, you have taken the child of My servant, you have taken the coolness of his eye and the fruit of his heart?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What did he say?' He said: 'He praised You and said *istirja'*.' He said: 'Build for him a house in Paradise, and name it the House of Praise.'" Al-Tirmidhi related it and said: "Hasan gharib."

Al-Bukhari related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whomever God wills good for, He afflicts with trials."

Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Nothing afflicts the Muslim of fatigue, nor sickness, nor anxiety, nor grief, nor harm, nor distress, not even a thorn that pricks him, except that God expiates by it some of his sins."

Both of them also related from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim is afflicted by harm from illness **(p. 329)** or otherwise, except that God removes by it some of his misdeeds, as a tree sheds its leaves."

The hadiths on this are abundant and well known in the books of the Sunnah.

For Imam Izz al-Din Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam, may God have mercy on him, there is a discourse on the benefits of trials and calamities, which is fitting to cite here. He, may mercy be upon him, said: For calamities, afflictions, trials, and misfortunes there are benefits that differ according to the ranks of people:

First: knowledge of the might of Lordship and its subjugation.

Second: knowledge of the humility of servanthood and its breaking. To this is the allusion in His words: ﴿Those who, when a calamity afflicts them, say: Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 156]. They acknowledge that they are His possession and His servants, and that they return to His judgment, His governance, His decree, and His measure; there is no escape for them from it and no deviation from it for them.

Third: sincerity to God, exalted is He; for there is no refuge in removing hardships except to Him, and no reliance in relieving them except upon Him: ﴿And if God touches you with harm, there is no remover of it but He﴾ [Al-An'am: 17]. ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 65].

**(p. 330)** Fourth: turning in repentance to God, exalted is He, and attending to Him: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾ [Al-Zumar: 8].

Fifth: humble supplication and invocation: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us﴾ [Yunus: 12]. ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon go astray except Him﴾ [Al-Isra': 67]. ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon, and He removes what you call upon Him for, if He wills, and you forget what you associate﴾ [Al-An'am: 41]. ﴿Say: Who delivers you from the darknesses of land and sea, which you call upon in humility and secretly: "If He delivers us from this, we will surely be among the grateful"﴾ [Al-An'am: 63].

Sixth: forbearance toward the one from whom the calamity came: ﴿Indeed Abraham was tender-hearted and forbearing﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 114]. **(p. 331)** ﴿Indeed We give you good news of a knowing boy﴾ [Al-Hijr: 53]. [And from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ashaj of Abd al-Qays: "Indeed in you are two traits that God, exalted is He, loves: forbearance and deliberation."] The degrees of forbearance differ according to the greatness or smallness of the calamities; forbearance at the greatest calamities is more excellent than any forbearance.

Seventh: pardoning the one who inflicted it: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people﴾ [Al Imran: 134]. ﴿Whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God﴾ [Al-Shura: 40]. Pardoning the greatest of them is more excellent than any pardon.

Eighth: patience with them, which necessitates God's love and abundant reward: ﴿And God loves the patient﴾ [Al Imran: 146]. ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [Al-Zumar: 10]. No one has been given a gift better and more expansive than patience.

**(p. 332)** Ninth: rejoicing in them for the sake of their benefits. He, upon whom be prayer and peace, said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul! Indeed they rejoice in trial as you rejoice in ease." Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, said: "How excellent are the two disliked things: death and poverty." They rejoiced in them because the harshness and bitterness of their hardship has no weight compared to their fruit and benefit, just as one whose illness is grave rejoices in drinking the decisive medicines that cure it, despite gulping down their bitterness.

Tenth: gratitude for them for what they contain of benefits, just as the patient thanks the physician who cuts off his limbs and prevents him from his desires, because of the recovery and healing he expects from that.

Eleventh: their purifying of sins and misdeeds: ﴿And whatever calamity befalls you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Al-Shura: 30]. "No Muslim is afflicted by fatigue or sickness, not even the worry that troubles him **(p. 333)** or the thorn that pricks him, except that God expiates by it some of his misdeeds."

Twelfth: mercy toward the people of trial and helping them in their affliction. People are either healthy or afflicted, so have mercy on the people of trial and thank God, exalted is He, for well-being. Only the one who loves is moved to pity lovers.

Thirteenth: knowing the value of the blessing of well-being and being grateful for it, for blessings are not known in their worth except after their loss.

Fourteenth: what God, exalted is He, has prepared for these benefits of Hereafter reward, according to its different ranks.

Fifteenth: the hidden benefits contained within them: ﴿Perhaps you dislike a thing while God makes in it much good﴾ [Al-Nisa': 19]. ﴿Perhaps you dislike a thing while it is good for you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 216]. **(p. 334)** ﴿Indeed those who brought the slander are a band among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather it is good for you﴾ [Al-Nur: 11].

When the tyrant seized Sarah from Abraham, it was contained within that trial that she gave him Hagar as a servant. She bore Ishmael to Abraham, peace be upon them both, and from the descendants of Ishmael came the Seal of the Prophets. How great is that news that was contained within that trial! And it has been said:

*How many a blessing is folded for you within the folds of calamities.*

**(p. 335)** Another said:

*Many a hated, detested thing has within it subtle gifts of God.*

Sixteenth: that calamities and hardships prevent arrogance, insolence, pride, vanity, haughtiness, and tyranny. For Nimrod, had he been poor, sickly, and lacking hearing and sight, would not have disputed with Abraham about his Lord. Rather, the insolence of kingship drove him to that. God, glorified is He, has attributed his disputation to his possession of kingship. Had Pharaoh been tested with the like of that, he would not have said: ﴿I am your Lord, the most high﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 24]. ﴿And they resented only that God and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 74]. ﴿Indeed, man transgresses﴾ [Al-Alaq: 6]. ﴿When he sees himself as self-sufficient﴾ [Al-Alaq: 7]. ﴿And if God extended provision to His servants, they would surely transgress upon the earth﴾ [Al-Shura: 27]. ﴿And the wrongdoers followed what they were given in luxury﴾ [Hud: 116]. ﴿Surely We would give them abundant water﴾ [Al-Jinn: 16]. ﴿That We might test them therein﴾ [Al-Jinn: 17]. ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but its affluent ones said: "Indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with"﴾ [Saba': 34].

**(p. 336)** The poor and the weak are the friends of God and the followers of the prophets. For the sake of these great benefits, the people most severely tested were the prophets, then the most excellent after them, one after another. They were called madmen, sorcerers, and soothsayers; they were mocked and ridiculed. ﴿So they were patient over what they were denied and harmed﴾ [Al-An'am: 34]. And it was said to us: ﴿Or did you think you would enter Paradise while the example of those who passed before you has not reached you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?" Unquestionably, the help of God is near﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 214]. **(p. 337)** ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 155]. ﴿You will surely be tested in your wealth and your selves, and you will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God﴾ [Al Imran: 186]. Like those who were expelled from their homes and their wealth and were exiled from their homelands, whose hardship increased, whose trial intensified, and whose enemies multiplied. They were overcome in some places, and some of them were killed at Uhud and at Bi'r Ma'una. The face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was wounded, his front tooth was broken, the helmet on his head was smashed, and his dear ones were killed and mutilated. His enemies rejoiced and his allies were grieved. They were tested on the day of the Trench; they were shaken with a severe shaking, their eyes turned, their hearts reached their throats, and they were in constant fear, persistent nakedness, and extreme poverty, until they tied stones to their stomachs from hunger. The master of the first and the last did not eat wheat bread two times in one day. He was harmed with various kinds of harm until they slandered the dearest of his family to him.

**(p. 338)** Then, at the end of matters, he was tested with Musaylimah, Tulayhah, and al-Ansi, and he and his companions met in the Army of Hardship what they met, and he died while his armor was with a Jew for thirty *sa'* of barley. The prophets and the righteous were continually tested, one time after another. "A man is tested according to the measure of his religion; if he is firm in his religion, his trial is intensified." "Indeed one of them would have a saw placed on his head, and that would not turn him from his religion." The Prophet, upon whom be prayer and peace, said: **(p. 339)** "The likeness of the believer is the likeness of a plant: the wind does not cease to bend it, and the believer does not cease to be struck by trial." He, upon whom be prayer and peace, also said: "The likeness of the believer is like the tender stalk of grain, which the wind bends: it knocks it down one time and straightens it another time, until it ripens." The state of hardship and trial draws the servant toward God, mighty and majestic is He, while the state of well-being and blessing turns the servant away from God, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us about a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12]. For this reason they lived sparingly in food, drink, marriage, gatherings, mounts, and other things, so that they would be in a state that necessitates their returning to God, mighty and majestic is He, and turning to Him.

Seventeenth: contentment, which necessitates the good pleasure of God, exalted is He. Calamities descend upon the righteous and the wicked alike. Whoever resents them will have resentment and the loss of this world and the Hereafter; whoever is content with them will have contentment. Contentment is more excellent than Paradise and what is in it, because of His words: ﴿And the pleasure of God is greater﴾ [Al-Tawbah: 72], that is, than the gardens of Eden and its good dwellings.

This is a brief summary of what has come to mind of the benefits of trial, and we ask Allah, exalted is He, for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. We are not among the people of trial. May Allah, exalted is He, grant us success in what He loves and is pleased with, and protect us from afflictions and calamities by His grace and generosity. Amin.

[p. 343]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[158] ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs Hajj to the House or ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for going around between them. And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs Hajj to the House or ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for going around between them﴾. ﴿Al-Safa and al-Marwah﴾ are proper names for two hills in Makkah. The meaning of their being among the symbols of Allah is that they are among the markers of His rites and acts of worship.

Al-Razi said: Everything that is made a marker of obedience to Allah is among the symbols of Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the symbols of Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 36], meaning a sign of closeness to Allah. And He said: ﴿That, and whoever honours the symbols of Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 32]. The symbols of Hajj are the landmarks of its rites. From this comes al-Mashʿar al-Haram (the sacred landmark), and from it comes ishʿar al-sanam, which is marking the hump (of the sacrificial camel) with a blade, so that this becomes a sign of the pilgrim's state of ihram and of his having designated it as an offering to the House of Allah. And (al-shaʿāʾir, الشَّعَائِرُ) is the plural of (shaʿīrah, شَعِيرَةٌ), meaning a sign. It is derived from ishʿar (إشْعَار), which is informing, and from it comes your saying: "I felt (shaʿartu) something," meaning "I knew." End of quote.

[p. 344] Al-Hajj, linguistically, means intention and purpose. Al-ʿItimar (ʿumrah) means visitation. In the Sharʿiah (sacred law) both terms came to be used specifically for intending the House and visiting it, in the two well-known forms of worship. Al-junah (الجُنَاحُ), with a dammah, means sin, constriction, and blame. The original meaning of al-tawaf (الطَّوَافُ) is walking around something. The intended meaning here is the sa'y (السَّعْي), the going between the two hills.

Several narrations have been reported concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

The wording of al-Bukhari, from ʿUrwah, who said: "I asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and I said to her: 'Tell me about the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs Hajj to the House or ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for going around between them﴾. By Allah, there is no blame upon anyone for not going around between al-Safa and al-Marwah!' She said: 'What an evil thing you have said, O son of my sister! If this verse were as you have interpreted it, it would read: "There is no blame upon him for not going around between them." Rather, it was revealed concerning the Ansar. Before they embraced Islam, they used to pronounce the talbiyah for Manat, the idol they worshipped at al-Mushallal. Whoever pronounced it would feel uneasy about going around between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When they embraced Islam, they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to feel uneasy about going around between al-Safa and al-Marwah." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of﴾, the verse.'"

ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established the going around between them." Therefore, no one has the right to abandon going around between them.

Then I informed Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, and he said: "This is knowledge I had not heard before. I did hear men of knowledge mention that the people, except those whom ʿĀʾishah mentioned who used to pronounce the talbiyah for Manat, all used to go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned going around the House but did not mention al-Safa and al-Marwah in the Qur'an, they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we used to go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and Allah revealed going around the House but did not mention al-Safa.' So is there any discomfort upon us if we go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah?' Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾, the verse."

[p. 345] Abu Bakr said: "I think this verse was revealed concerning both groups: those who felt uneasy about going around al-Safa and al-Marwah in the Jahiliyyah, and those who used to go around them and then felt uneasy about it in Islam. This is because Allah, exalted is He, commanded circumambulation of the House without mentioning al-Safa, until He mentioned it after mentioning the circumambulation of the House."

In the narration of Maʿmar from al-Zuhri: "We used not to go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah out of reverence for Manat." Al-Bukhari reported it in suspended form (taʿlīq), and Ahmad and others connected it.

Muslim also reported, in the narration of Yunus from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, that ʿĀʾishah informed him: "The Ansar, before they embraced Islam, along with Ghassan, used to pronounce the talbiyah for Manat. So they felt uneasy about going around between al-Safa and al-Marwah. This was a custom among their forefathers: whoever entered ihram for Manat did not go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When they embraced Islam, they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that. So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed concerning that: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs Hajj to the House or ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for going around between them. And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing﴾."

Al-Fakihi narrated from al-Zuhri that ʿAmr ibn Luhayy set up Manat on the seashore near Qudayd. The Azd and Ghassan used to make Hajj to it and honour it. When they had circumambulated the House, departed from ʿArafat, and finished at Mina, they came to Manat and pronounced the talbiyah for it. Whoever pronounced the talbiyah for it did not go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: Manat belonged to the Aws, the Khazraj, and the Azd of Ghassan, and to those of Yathrib who followed their religion.

Al-Nasai narrated with a strong chain from Zayd ibn Harithah, who said: "On al-Safa and al-Marwah there were two idols of copper, called Isaf and Nailah. When the polytheists went around, they would touch them..." The hadith continues.

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir narrated with a good chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: [p. 346] "The Ansar said: 'Going between al-Safa and al-Marwah is a matter of the Jahiliyyah.' So Allah, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah﴾, the verse."

Al-Fakihi and Isma'il al-Qadi in al-Ahkam narrated with an authentic chain from al-Shaʿbi, who said: "There was an idol on al-Safa called 'Isaf,' and an idol on al-Marwah called 'Nailah.' The people of the Jahiliyyah used to run between them. When Islam came, it threw them away, and they said: 'That was done by the people of the Jahiliyyah on account of their idols.' So they refrained from going between them." He said: "Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah﴾, the verse."

From the totality of these narrations it is derived that groups felt uneasy about going between al-Safa and al-Marwah for various reasons, and so the verse was revealed concerning all of them. And Allah knows best.

ʿĀʾishah's answer to ʿUrwah, may Allah be pleased with her, reflects her subtle knowledge, her penetrating understanding, and her great insight into the fine points of wording. This is because the wording of the noble verse only indicates the removal of blame from one who goes around between them. It contains no indication either that going between them is not obligatory or that it is obligatory.

﴿And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing﴾: that is, whoever does good, Allah will show appreciation for it and reward him for it. The meaning of (taṭawwaʿa, تَطَوَّعَ) is that he did what was within his willingness, or did an act of obedience. Its application to what is not obligatory is a jurisprudential (fiqhī) usage, not a linguistic one. Appreciation (shukr, الشُّكْرُ) from Allah, exalted is He, means recompense and good praise.

Al-Raghib said: Appreciation, as it occurs by speech, occurs also by action, and on this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾ [Saba': 13]. He said: The appreciation of the exalted toward the lowly is nothing but bestowing favour upon him and accepting praise from him.

[p. 347] Notes:

First: Some people hold to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾ as evidence that the sa'y is a sunnah (recommended practice), and that whoever abandons it bears no liability. If their basis for this is that taṭawwuʿ means voluntarily giving what is not required, we have already noted that this is a jurisprudential usage and not a linguistic one, so there is no proof in it. And if their basis is the negation of blame, you know what is intended by it.

Among those who held that it is a sunnah, such that no compensation is required for abandoning it, is Anas, as transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir, and ʿAtaʾ. Ibn Hajar transmitted this in al-Fath.

Al-Razi said: It was reported from Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and ʿAtaʾ that whoever abandons it bears no liability. As for the hadith: "Run (between them), for Allah has prescribed for you the sa'y," narrated by Ahmad and others, its chain includes ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Muʾammal, in whom there is weakness. For this reason Ibn al-Mundhir said: If it is established, then it is a proof for obligation. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned this in al-Fath.

Second: It is authentically established that "the Prophet (ﷺ) went around between al-Safa and al-Marwah seven times." Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated it from Ibn ʿUmar. [p. 348] Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his circumambulation, he came to al-Safa and ascended it until he saw the House. He raised his hands and began to praise Allah and supplicate with whatever he wished to supplicate." Muslim also narrated from the hadith of Jabir: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) drew near to al-Safa, he recited: 'Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. I begin with what Allah began with,' and he began with al-Safa and climbed it until he saw the House. He faced the qiblah, declared Allah's oneness and glorified Him, and said: 'There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things capable. There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone.' Then he supplicated between these, saying the same three times. Then he descended toward al-Marwah until, when his feet were placed in the bottom of the valley, and when they ascended, he walked until he reached al-Marwah. He did on al-Marwah as he had done on al-Safa." End quote. The apparent meaning of this is that he was walking.

Muslim, in his Sahih, narrated from Abu al-Zubayr that he heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: "The Prophet (ﷺ) circumambulated the House on his mount during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and between al-Safa and al-Marwah, so that people could see him, and so that he could be seen and asked, for the people had surrounded him."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions did not go around between al-Safa and al-Marwah except for one circuit.

Ibn Hazm said: There is no contradiction between them, for when a rider's camel stumbles and falls, all of it falls, and his feet fall along with the rest of his body.

[p. 349] In my view, there is another way of reconciling them, better than this, which is that he performed the sa'y on foot at first, then completed his sa'y while riding. This has been stated explicitly. In Sahih Muslim, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: "I said to Ibn ʿAbbas: 'Tell me about going around between al-Safa and al-Marwah while riding. Is it a sunnah? For your people claim that it is a sunnah!' He said: 'They spoke truly and they lied!' I said: 'What do you mean by "they spoke truly and they lied"?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was crowded by people who kept saying, "This is Muhammad!" until the young women came out of the houses to see him.' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not like people to strike with their hands in front of him. So when the crowd pressed upon him, he rode. But walking and the sa'y are better.'"

In the two Sahihs, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only performed the sa'y around the House and between al-Safa and al-Marwah in order to show the polytheists his strength!"

From Kurayb, the mawla of Ibn ʿAbbas: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Running through the valley bed between al-Safa and al-Marwah is not a sunnah. It was only that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to run there, saying: 'We do not permit the valley (al-Batha') except by running!'" Al-Bukhari narrated it in suspended form, and Abu Nuʿaym connected it in his Mustakhraj. The commentators on the Sahih said: What is negated by the sa'y here is the intense walking and running. He, may Allah be pleased with him, did not negate the sunnah of the plain sa'y, but rather the crossing of the valley with force and rapid running, since the origin of the sa'y is the practice of the Prophet (ﷺ). And Allah knows best.

[p. 350] Third: In al-Bukhari, from Ibn ʿAbbas, in the story of Hajar, the mother of Isma'il: the going between them is derived from her circling and her hastening in search of water. His wording is: "The mother of Isma'il began nursing Isma'il and drinking from that water, until the water in the waterskin ran out, and she and her son became thirsty. She began to look at him writhing, or he said: thrashing. So she set off, out of distress at looking at him. She found al-Safa the nearest mountain to her on the earth, so she stood upon it. Then she faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone. But she saw no one. So she descended from al-Safa, and when she reached the valley, she lifted the edge of her garment and then ran the run of a exhausted person until she crossed the valley. Then she came to al-Marwah and stood upon it and looked to see whether she could see anyone. But she saw no one. She did this seven times."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That is the sa'y of the people between them. When she reached al-Marwah, she heard a voice..." The hadith continues.

Ibn Kathir said: When Hajar wandered in this blessed place between al-Safa and al-Marwa, seeking relief from Allah, the Exalted, humbled, fearful, distressed, and poor before Allah, Azza wa Jall, Allah removed her distress, eased her loneliness, relieved her hardship, and caused Zamzam to gush forth for her, the water that is food for the hungry and a cure for the sick. Thus the one who goes back and forth between them should bring to mind his poverty, his humility, and his need for Allah to guide his heart, set right his condition, and forgive his sin, and that he should seek refuge with Allah, Azza wa Jall, to relieve what he has of deficiencies and faults, to guide him to the straight path, to keep him firm upon it until his death, and to transform him from his state of sins and disobedience into a state of perfection, forgiveness, rectitude, and steadfastness, just as He did for Hajar, peace be upon her.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 159:

(p-351) The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[159] ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear for the people in the Book—those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear for the people in the Book—those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse.﴾

Since it was previously stated that some of the People of the Book conceal this truth which they know, and He concluded what followed it with the two attributes of gratitude and knowledge, as encouragement and warning, that He is grateful to whoever does what He has prescribed for him, and knows whoever hides it, however subtle his action and however much he exaggerates in concealing it, the discourse turned to rebuking the hypocrites among them and cursing them for concealing the truth they know. All of this, in reality, concerns their stories, and moving on to other matters is merely a digression in the wise and clear style, because this Book is guidance. The context indicated that the implied sense after ﴿Grateful, Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158] is "and whoever commits evil, then indeed Allah is Knowing, Powerful." So He connected to it, as a new statement, in a manner that encompasses them and others: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down﴾, up to the end of the verse, as an explanation of their recompense. Thus this verse, in its conclusion of this address, is coherent with what came at its beginning in His saying: ﴿And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 42]. So the beginning was specific and the conclusion general, so that what is in the Book of Allah would be a command applying—in the manner that the command of Muhammad (ﷺ) and those before him of the messengers applied to creation—so that the command applies to creation uniformly at the beginning and the end, thus including every concealer among the earlier and later generations. Transmitted by al-Biqa'i.

And al-La'n (cursing): expulsion and distancing from good. From Allah, the Exalted, it is this; from creatures, it is reviling, insulting, invoking evil upon the cursed, opposing and contesting him, and opposing him, along with anger toward him and disassociation from him. By His saying ﴿al-La'inun﴾ (those who curse) is meant everyone from whom cursing is valid, and He clarified it after His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161]. (p-352) The verse indicates that this concealment is among the major sins, because He, exalted is He, made cursing obligatory for it; what relates to the religion and which the responsible person needs may not be concealed, and whoever conceals it has greatly erred and reached, through his cursing, the extreme of wretchedness and loss whose reality cannot be grasped! Numerous hadiths have been related prohibiting the concealment of knowledge. In the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Were it not for two verses that Allah revealed in His Book, I would never have narrated anything ever: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal﴾, up to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those given the Book, that you shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 187], up to the end of the verse."

Then He, exalted is He, excepted from these those who repent to Him, saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[160] ﴿Except for those who repent, amend, and make clear. Those, I accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿Except for those who repent﴾ - that is, from concealment -: ﴿and amend﴾ - that is, they do righteous deeds -: ﴿and make clear﴾ - what they had concealed, so that their repentance becomes manifest through giving it up -: ﴿Those, I accept their repentance﴾ - that is, I accept their repentance by pouring forth forgiveness and mercy upon them -: ﴿and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Then, exalted is He, informed about those who disbelieved in Him and whose state continued in disbelief, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verses 161–162:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162] — i.e., in the curse, or in the Fire, the pronoun being left unexpressed without mention in order to magnify its matter and to emphasise its gravity — ﴿the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]. This may be from al-indhar (inẓār) in the sense of delay and respite: i.e., they will not be granted respite from the punishment, nor will it be deferred from them for an hour, but it is continuous and perpetual. Or it may be from al-naẓar (naẓar) in the sense of sight: i.e., He will not look upon them with a look of mercy, as in His saying: ﴿nor will He look upon them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 77].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verses 161–162:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162] — i.e., in the curse, or in the Fire, the pronoun being left unexpressed without mention in order to magnify its matter and to emphasise its gravity — ﴿the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]. This may be from al-indhar (inẓār) in the sense of delay and respite: i.e., they will not be granted respite from the punishment, nor will it be deferred from them for an hour, but it is continuous and perpetual. Or it may be from al-naẓar (naẓar) in the sense of sight: i.e., He will not look upon them with a look of mercy, as in His saying: ﴿nor will He look upon them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 77].

(p-354)The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[163] ﴿And your God is One God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.﴾

﴿And your God is One God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.﴾ Exalted is He informs, by His address to all of mankind, of His singularity in divinity, and that He has no partner and no equal.

Al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani) said: It is permissible that His words ﴿And your God is One God﴾ be a general address, meaning: the one who deserves worship from you is one God, not more. It is also permissible that it be an address to the believers, and the meaning is: the One whom you worship is one God, as a warning that you are not like the disbelievers who worship idols as gods, and Satan, and desire, and other things. If it is asked: what is the benefit of combining "Your God is One God" with "there is no deity except Him," when one of them is built upon the other? It is answered: when He clarified by His words ﴿And your God is One God﴾ that He is the one intended for worship, or the one deserving of it, and it might be imagined that there exists another deity besides Him, but one that is not worshipped and does not deserve worship, He reinforced this with His words ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾. It is right for this meaning that it be an emphasis, and that the expressions be repeated, since He is the beginning and the ultimate end of the object of worship. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: God, glorified and exalted is He, specifically placed these two attributes in this position because mentioning divinity and uniqueness conveys dominance and exaltedness, so He followed them with the mention of this intensity of mercy, to refresh hearts from the awe of divinity and the might of uniqueness, and to indicate that His mercy precedes His wrath, and that He created creation only for mercy and benevolence. End of quotation.

Since the station of oneness cannot be valid except with complete knowledge and perfect power, God, exalted is He, set forth the proofs, from the heavenly and earthly things, their accidents and the intermediate things, upon that, as an insight for the ignorant and a reminder for the scholars, with His words:

(p-355) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[164] ﴿Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ship that runs in the sea with what benefits mankind, and what God sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and dispersing in it every kind of creature, and the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between heaven and earth, are signs for a people who use their reason.﴾

﴿Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ — in the height of the first, its subtlety and vastness, its planets and fixed stars, and the rotation of their spheres; and in the lowness of the second, its density, its mountains, seas, deserts, valleys, its inhabited places, and what is in them of benefits. ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾ — i.e., their succession, each of them being a replacement for the other: one comes and then goes, and the other replaces it and follows it without lagging behind it for a moment. Like His words: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day to succeed one another﴾ [al-Furqan: 62]. Or the alternation of each of them in itself, in increase and decrease, as He said: ﴿He causes the night to pass into the day, and causes the day to pass into the night﴾ [al-Hadid: 6], i.e., one increases from this into that and from that into this. ﴿And the ship that runs in the sea with what benefits mankind﴾ — i.e., in the subjection of the sea by carrying ships from one side to another, for the livelihoods of people and for benefiting from what is in one region for another.
