Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 131]. Islam was named Islam only for this meaning. The name al-silm came to be applied to reconciliation and the abandonment of war. This too goes back to this meaning, since at reconciliation each party submits to its companion and does not contend with him over it.

The meaning of the verse: enter into submission and obedience, i.e., submit to Allah and obey Him, and do not depart from any part of His laws. ﴿Completely⦅kaffah⦆﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in "enter." ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan⦅khutuwat⦆﴾, i.e., his paths to which he calls you. For ﴿He only commands you to evil and immorality, and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 169], and ﴿He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 6]. The vowelling of the ta' in khutuwat, as a damma or as a sukun, are two dialects: Hijazi and Tamimi. Both have been read in the seven canonical readings. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy⦅mubin⦆﴾ — manifestly hostile, or one who makes it manifest. That is, by what We have informed you concerning the matter of your father Adam, peace be upon him, and others, whose evidences are evident.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[209] ﴿And if you slip after the clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

﴿And if you slip﴾ i.e., from entering into peace (al-silm). ﴿after the clear proofs have come to you﴾ i.e., the manifest signs that what you have been called to enter is the truth. ﴿then know that Allah is Exalted in Might﴾ — Victorious, whom the exacting of retribution from those who slip does not overcome, and from whom those who go astray cannot escape. ﴿Wise﴾ — He does not exact retribution except with right. His saying ﴿then know﴾ and so on is an utmost form of warning, because it combines kinds of fear that a threat by mention of punishment does not combine. A father may say to his son: "If you disobey me, then you know me, and you know my power over you and the severity of my might." This speech, in rebuke, is more eloquent than mentioning beating or otherwise. Thus it becomes clear that the answer of the conditional in the verse is caused by what it signals of rebuke and threat, upon the condition that points to their sin and transgression.

Furthermore, among the probable meanings of the verse is that the "peace" mentioned in it means reconciliation, making peace, and abandoning dispute and disagreement. So the meaning of ﴿Enter into peace﴾ [al-Baqarah: 208] is: be in agreement and united in supporting the religion, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan by having him drive you to pursue worldly gain and to quarrel with people. In that case the verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart﴾ [al-Anfal: 46], and His saying: ﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah, and do not separate﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 103], and His saying: ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [al-Shura: 13]. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 210 (part 1 of 2)**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[210] ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, with the angels, and the matter be decided? And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

﴿Do they await﴾ means: do they wait. *Nazara* (to look) is like *intazara* (to wait). It is said: "I looked at him" and "I waited for him" when you anticipate his presence. This interrogative is one of denial, in the sense of negation. That is: they await nothing, despite their obstinacy and opposition in what they do, in not complying with what they were commanded and not refraining from what they were forbidden, after a long period of forbearance towards them: ﴿except that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾. *Zulal* is the plural of *zullah* (a canopy), like *qulal* is the plural of *qullah* (a peak). That is, in a canopy within a canopy. It is that which shields from the sun, so it is at the extreme of darkness, terror and awe, because of its density, which covers over the one who sees what is within it. ﴿And the angels﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161] is a conjunction with the Glorious Name, meaning: and His hosts will come, whose number none knows but Him. This is according to the reading of the majority. According to the reading of Abu Ja'far, in the genitive case, it is a conjunction with *zulal* or *al-ghamam* (the clouds). ﴿And the matter is decided﴾ means: the affair of their destruction is completed and finished. Al-Raghib said: by this he draws attention to the fact that what has passed cannot be remedied. It is a conjunction with ﴿He comes to them﴾, falling within the scope of the waiting. He turned to the past tense form to indicate its certainty, as if it had already occurred. Or it is an independent sentence, brought to report that its content will certainly take place. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ means: those who were possessors of authority and disposal in the world, their dominion and their disposal will be taken back from them on the Day of Resurrection, and will return to Him, exalted is He. It is said: "the matter returned to the ruler", meaning he reclaimed what he had delegated to them. Or by ﴿the matters﴾ he meant the spirits and souls, not the bodies, and he called them "matters" because they are originations referred to by His saying: ﴿Surely to Him belong the creation and the command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. They are of the origination that humans cannot conceive, so he drew attention to the fact that all spirits are returned to Him and come back to Him. In a similar manner He said: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾ [al-A'raf: 29]. Their return will be either with gain and joy, or with regret and anguish. This was said by the Imam al-Raghib.

Abu Muslim said: Indeed, He, exalted is He, has given everyone dominion over matters in the abode of trial and affliction, as a test. When the affair of this abode ends and we arrive at the abode of reward and punishment, the entire affair will belong to Allah alone. Since this is so, He is worthy to be feared, obeyed, and to be entered into peace, as He commanded, and to guard against the footsteps of Satan, as He forbade.

It has been read in the seven canonical readings as *turja'u* with a *damma* on the *ta'* (to be returned), meaning "are returned", and with a *fatha* on it, meaning "become", as in His saying: ﴿Surely to Allah all matters come to their end﴾ [al-Shura: 53].

Al-Qaffal said: The meaning of the two readings is close, because they return to Him, exalted is He, and He, glory be to Him, returns them to Himself by the annihilation of the world and the establishment of the Resurrection.

Two points of note:

The first: This verse has similar and parallel passages which indicate that this threat is of the Hereafter.

For this reason Ibn Kathir said regarding the meaning of the verse: Exalted is He says, threatening the disbelievers who opposed Muhammad (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, with the angels﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, for the decisive judgement between the first and the last, so that every doer is recompensed according to his deed: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil...! For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the matter is decided, and to Allah all matters are returned﴾.

As He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿No! When the earth is ground to powder, grinding to powder﴾ [al-Fajr: 21]; ﴿and your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [al-Fajr: 22]; ﴿And on that day Hell is brought near; on that day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ [al-Fajr: 23].

And He said: ﴿Do they await only that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come?﴾ [al-An'am: 158], to the end of the verse.

(p-518) The second: His describing Himself with coming in canopies of clouds is like His description of Himself with coming in other verses and the like, of what He described Himself with in His Book, or what has been authentically related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The discussion concerning all of this is of one kind.

This is the way of the Salaf (early generations) of the Community and its Imams: they describe Him, glory be to Him, with what He described Himself with, and with what His Messenger (ﷺ) described Him with, without *tahrif* (distortion), *ta'til* (negation), *takyif* (asking "how"), or *tamthil* (likening). The discussion of His attributes is like the discussion of His essence. Allah, exalted is He, ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾, neither in His essence, nor in His attributes, nor in His actions. So if a questioner asks: How does He, glory be to Him, come, or how does He come...? Then it should be said to him: How is He in Himself? If he says: I do not know the modality of His essence! Then it should be said to him: Likewise you do not know the modality of His attributes...! For knowledge of the modality of an attribute follows knowledge of the modality of the one described. Many who related the consensus of the Salaf, including al-Khattabi, have stated: the way of the Salaf is that His attributes, exalted is He, are taken according to their apparent meaning, with the negation of modality and resemblance from them. Some people say: the way of the Salaf is that the apparent meaning is not intended. And they say: We are agreed that the apparent meaning is not intended. This expression is an error, either in wording and meaning, or in wording without meaning. For the word "apparent" contains ambiguity and homonymy. If the speaker believes that the apparent meaning of these texts is the likening to the attributes of created beings or what is among their particular characteristics, then there is no doubt that this is not intended. But the Salaf and the Imams did not call this their apparent meaning. This speaker erred in thinking that this corrupt meaning is the apparent sense of the wording, to the point that he considered it in need of *ta'wil* (interpretation), and in that he related of the Salaf what they did not intend. If the speaker believes that the apparent meaning of the texts whose meaning is disputed is of the same kind as the apparent meaning of the texts whose meaning is agreed upon, and the apparent meaning is what is intended in all of them: since Allah has informed that He is knowing of all things, and that He is powerful over all things, and the People of the Sunnah and the Imams of the Muslims are agreed that this is upon its apparent meaning, that the apparent meaning of that is intended, it is known that they did not intend by this apparent meaning that His knowledge be like our knowledge or His power like our power.

Likewise, since they agreed that He is living, knowing, and powerful in reality, they did not mean that He is like the created being who is living, knowing and powerful. If the listener thinks that the apparent meaning of the attributes resembles the attributes of created beings, it would necessitate that none of that apparent meaning is intended (p-519). If he believes that its apparent meaning is what befits the Creator and is specific to Him, it is not permissible for him to negate this apparent meaning, or to negate that it is intended, except by a proof which indicates the negation. There is nothing in reason or revelation that negates this except of the same kind as that by which all the attributes are negated, so the discussion regarding all of them is one.

Therefore it is not permissible to say: the apparent meaning is not intended by this explanation. In sum, whoever says: the apparent meaning is not intended, in the sense that the attributes of created beings are not intended, we say to him: You are right in meaning, but you erred in wording, and you gave rise to innovation, and made a path for the Jahmiyyah to their goal. You could have said: they pass as they came, upon their apparent meaning, with the knowledge that the attributes of Allah are not like the attributes of created beings, and that He is exalted and sanctified above everything that would entail His being originated or deficient. Whoever says: the apparent meaning is not intended, by the second explanation, which is the intention of the Jahmiyyah and those who follow them, has erred. Those who erred were only led to it because they imagine, regarding some attributes or many of them or most of them or all of them, that they resemble the attributes of created beings. Then they want to negate what they understood, and so fall into four kinds of pitfalls:

The first: that he becomes like what he understood from the texts regarding the attributes of created beings, and thinks that the implication of the texts is likening.

The second: that when he makes that its meaning and then nullifies it, the texts remain nullified from what they indicate of affirming attributes befitting Allah. So, along with his offence against the texts and his bad opinion of Allah and His Messenger, in thinking that what is understood from their speech is the false likening, he has nullified what Allah and His Messenger placed in their speech of affirming attributes for Allah and the divine meanings befitting the majesty of Allah, exalted is He.

The third: that he negates those attributes from Allah, mighty and majestic, without knowledge, and so he is a nullifier of what the Lord deserves.

The fourth: that he describes the Lord with the opposite of those attributes, from the attributes of the dead and the inanimate or the attributes of the non-existent, and so he has nullified through it the attributes of perfection which the Lord deserves, and likened Him (p-520) to the deficient and the non-existent, and nullified the texts from what they indicate of attributes, and made their implication the likening to created things. So he combines in the speech of Allah and regarding Allah both nullification and likening, and so he is a deviator regarding the names of Allah and His signs.

The summary of the discussion: these attributes are the attributes of Allah, glory be to Him, according to what befits His majesty, their attribution to His sanctified essence being like the attribution of the attributes of everything to its essence.

This is the summary of what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah be pleased with him, established in his two treatises *al-Tadmuriyyah* and *al-Madaniyyah*.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: The People of the Sunnah are agreed on affirming all the attributes that occur in the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and believing in them, and taking them in their literal sense, not in their figurative sense. However, they do not give any of them a modality, nor do they limit any attribute to a restricted description. As for the People of Innovation, the Jahmiyyah, the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij, they all deny them and do not take any of them in their literal sense, and claim that whoever affirms them is a likener. And they, in the view of those who affirm them, are negators of the One who is worshipped. The truth is in what was said by those who spoke according to what the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger uttered, and they are the Imams of the community.

Qadi Abu Ya'la said in his book *Ibtal al-Ta'wil* (The Nullification of Interpretation): It is not permissible to reject these reports, nor to occupy oneself with interpreting them; what is obligatory is to take them according to their apparent meaning, and that they are the attributes of Allah which are not to be likened to the other beings described by them from among the creation, and no likening is to be believed in them.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: When the Book speaks of something, we say it; and when reports come with something, we proceed upon it. Know that there is nothing in sound reason or clear transmission that requires opposing the Salafi method. Those who oppose the Book, the Sunnah and the Salaf of the Community, among the interpreters of this subject, are in a confused matter. Glory be to Allah! By what intellect is the Book and the Sunnah weighed?

May Allah be pleased with the Imam Malik when he said: Whenever a man comes to us who is more skilled in disputation than another man, shall we abandon what Jibril brought to Muhammad (ﷺ), for the sake of this disputation? Each of these is refuted by the same argument with which the other was refuted. And this is on several grounds:

(p-521) The first: the proof that reason does not render that impossible.

The second: that the texts which have come do not admit of interpretation.

The third: that the generality of these matters is known to have been brought by the Messenger by necessity, just as he brought the five daily prayers and the fasting of the month of Ramadan. So the interpretation that diverts them from this is like the interpretations of the Qaramita and the Batiniyyah regarding the Hajj, the fast, the prayer, and the rest of what the prophethoods brought. Moreover, the leading figures among these champions acknowledge that reason has no path to certainty in the generality of divine matters. Since this is so, it is obligatory to receive the knowledge of this from the prophethoods as it is, and Allah speaks the truth and He guides to the path.

Al-Biqa'i said: The manifestation of the angels in canopies of clouds is a familiar matter. Among it is what is in the authentic collection from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A man was reciting Surah al-Kahf, and beside him was a horse tied with two ropes. A cloud overshadowed him and began to draw nearer and nearer, and his horse began to bolt. When he awoke in the morning, he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. He said: 'That was the tranquillity (*sakinah*) which descended with the Qur'an.'"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 210 (part 2 of 2):

"It is narrated from Usayd ibn Hudayr that he said: 'While he was reciting Surat al-Baqarah at night, and his horse was tethered beside him, the horse began to move about. He fell silent, and the horse fell silent. He recited again, and the horse moved about. He fell silent, and the horse fell silent. Then he recited again, and the horse moved about. So he left off [reciting]. His son Yahya was close to the horse, and he feared that it would trample him. When he dragged him away, he raised his head toward the sky until he could no longer see it. In the morning he told the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: "Keep reciting, Ibn Hudayr, keep reciting, Ibn Hudayr." He said: "I feared, O Messenger of Allah, that it would trample Yahya, who was close to it, so I raised my head and went to him. Then I raised my head to the sky and saw something like a canopy in which were the likenesses of lamps, and I went out until I could no longer see it." (p-522) He said: "Do you know what that was?" He said: "No." He said: "Those were the angels who drew near for the sake of your voice. Had you continued reciting, the people would have seen them in the morning, and they would not have hidden themselves from them."'"

Al-Baqa'i also said: "Since the Children of Israel were the people most knowledgeable about the manifestation of the glory of Allah in the clouds, because of what their forefathers witnessed from it when they left Egypt, and at Mount Sinai, and in the Tent of Meeting (qubbat al-zaman), and what was in that—as was transmitted to them—of immense majesty and exalted greatness, Allah the Exalted said, in answer to one who had said: 'How can this be?'"

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them. And whoever substitutes the blessing of Allah after it has come to him, indeed Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ [2:211]

﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them.﴾ The purpose of this question is to rebuke and reproach the Children of Israel for their transgression and their denial of the truth after the signs had become manifest. It is not that they would answer, so that something might be learned from their answer. It is like when one of us wants to reprimand someone, and he says to those present: "Ask him how much I have bestowed upon him?" That is, ask them how many manifest miracles (mu'jizat, miracles) they witnessed at the hands of their prophets, which decisively proved the truthfulness of those prophets (peace be upon them) in what they brought to them: such as the staff of Moses, his splitting of the sea, his striking of the rock, the shade of the clouds over them in the intense heat, the sending down of the manna and the quail (al-man wa al-salwa), and other signs that point to His oneness, the Exalted, and to the truthfulness of the one through whose hands these extraordinary events occurred. Despite this, many of them turned away from them, and they exchanged the blessing of Allah upon them with them for disbelief, as indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever substitutes the blessing of Allah after it has come to him, indeed Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ So the blessing of Allah here means His signs. This is an instance of placing the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun (wad' al-zahir mawdi' al-mudmar, placing an explicit noun where a pronoun would be expected) without a preceding explicit mention, in order to magnify the signs. And there is no doubt that they are among the greatest kinds of Allah's blessings, because they are the means of guidance and of salvation from misguidance. Their substitution of them means exchanging belief in them for disbelief in them and turning away from them. As the Exalted said, reporting about the disbelievers of Quraysh: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28] ﴿Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the settling place.﴾ [Ibrahim: 29]

And His saying: ﴿after it has come to him﴾ means: after it has reached him and he was able to recognize it, or he recognized it. The explicit statement of this, even though substitution is not conceivable before its coming, is to indicate that they substituted it after they had come to know its details. In this there is a great censure of them, a condemnation of the monstrousness of their state, and an argument for their deserving the severe punishment, since they substituted it after knowledge.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 212:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[212] ﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe. But those who have taortaken taqwa (God-consciousness) will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.﴾

﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾ until they exchanged the blessing. ﴿The life of this world﴾ because of its presence, so it distracted them from the unseen Hereafter.

Al-Harali said: Within it is an indication that admiring the splendour of this world is a kind of disbelief, insofar as the sight of reason and faith perceives its inner reality and witnesses its carrion nature, so one is not deceived by its adornment. It is the bane of creation in their detachment from the truth. Thus, the Exalted made the one who adorns unspecified in this verse, so that it includes the lightest adornment that occurs by the tongue of Satan and the most hidden adornment that comes from Allah's gradual leading astray, as in His words: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every community their deeds﴾ [Al-An'am: 108].

In his words there is also an indication of the answer to the occurrence of adornment, attributed sometimes to Allah, Exalted is He, and sometimes to others, in several verses of the Noble Revelation. (p. 524)

Al-Raghib has a wonderful statement by which such a problem is resolved, and it is his words:

Indeed, an act is attributed to its direct agent, and it is also attributed to that which is its cause and facilitator. On this basis, it is valid for a single act to be attributed at times to Allah, Exalted is He, and at times to other than Him, such as His words: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death will take you﴾ [As-Sajdah: 11], and in another place: ﴿Allah takes the souls﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42]. So in the first He attributed the act to its direct agent, and in the second to the one who commands it. And thus, what has been mentioned can be conceived, and the doubt disappears regarding those acts seen as attributed to Allah, Exalted is He, and also negated from Allah, Exalted is He, such as His words: ﴿So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them﴾ [Al-Anfal: 17], His words: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ [Al-Anfal: 17], and His words: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾ [An-Nisa: 79].

﴿And they mock﴾, i.e., they ridicule: ﴿those who believe﴾. This is as He, Exalted is He, said: (p. 525) ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 29], ﴿and when they passed by them, they winked to one another﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 30], and the verses that follow. ﴿And those who have taken taqwa﴾, and they are the believers, and they were mentioned by the title of taqwa only to urge them toward it and to announce that the ruling is based upon it. ﴿Above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because they are in the ʿIlliyyin (the highest heights), while those (the disbelievers) are in the lowest of the low. Or because they will exalt themselves over them in the Hereafter and will mock them, just as they mocked them in this world, as He said: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 34], ﴿upon couches, looking on﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 35].

For this reason al-Raghib said: His words ﴿above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ may bear two meanings:

The first: that the state of the believers in the Hereafter is higher than the state of the disbelievers in this world.

The second: that the believers in the Hereafter are in the lofty chambers, and the disbelievers in the lowest level of the Fire. End of quotation.

Subtleties:

Al-Sialkuti said: Know that His words ﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾ and so on form a clause giving the reason for what preceded concerning the states of the disbelievers, from among the hypocrites and the People of the Book. That is to say, all the blameworthy attributes that have been mentioned of them are due to their wholehearted pursuit of love for the life of this world and their turning away from anything else. The adornment was expressed in the past tense because it is settled, fixed in their nature. It was joined to it by the present tense verb, namely {they mock}, to indicate continuity. And His words ﴿those who have taken taqwa﴾ were joined in order to console the believers.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾ mean: what Allah gives these (p. 526) God-conscious ones of reward without account, that is, abundant and pleasant provision that has no end and no cessation, like His words, glorified is He: ﴿Those enter Paradise, being provided therein without account﴾ [Ghafir: 40]. For everything that falls under reckoning, limitation, and measure is finite, so what is not finite is necessarily outside of reckoning.

Al-Raghib has thoroughly examined what the verse may bear of its meanings, and that is a wide scope. His expression: "He gave him without account" means: when He gives him more than he deserves, or less than he deserves. The first is what is intended, and it is what is pointed to by the term "beneficence." He has interpreted that in several ways because the wording is general and ambiguous.

The first: He gives him a gift that the limitation of the servants cannot contain, like the words of the poet:

؎His gifts are counted before the rain is counted.

The second: He gives him more than he deserves.

The third: He gives him without reproach.

The fourth: He gives him without restriction, from their saying: "he called him to account."

The fifth: He gives him more than he thinks will suffice for him. All these meanings may be in this world, and they may be in the Hereafter.

The sixth: that this is an indication of His expanding (provision) upon the disbelievers and the wicked, concerning whom He said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 33], and as an alert that there is no virtue in wealth for the one upon whom it is expanded (p. 527) so long as he does not seek help with it in reaching what is sought from it. For this reason He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they think that We extend to them﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 55], the verse.

The seventh: He gives His friends without consequence or reckoning against them regarding what they are given. That is because the believer takes from the goods of this world only what is obligatory, from the place it is obligatory, in the manner it is obligatory, and spends it only in that way. So he takes account, and thus is not called to account. For this reason it was narrated: "Whoever takes account of himself in this world will be safe from reckoning in the Hereafter." On this basis He, Exalted is He, said to Solomon: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾ [Sad: 39].

The eighth: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, deals with the believers on the Day of Resurrection not according to the measure of their deserving, but with more than that, as He said: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245], the verse.

The ninth, which is close to that: that this is an indication of what has been narrated, that the people of Paradise have no prohibition upon them, and upon this is His words: ﴿And therein is what the souls desire﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 71], the verse, and His words: ﴿They enter Paradise﴾, the verse.

As for its connection to what preceded, then according to some of these interpretations, it is connected to ﴿those who disbelieve﴾, and according to some it is connected to ﴿those who believe﴾.

(p. 528)

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[213] ﴿Mankind were one community; then Allah sent forth the Prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book with truth, that it might judge between people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed concerning it except those who were given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Then Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

﴿Mankind were one community﴾ means: they were brought into existence as one community, their aims, objectives and direction united, so that they would do good and not corrupt, do well and not do evil, act justly and not oppress. That is, they were created only to be such. As He said in another verse: ﴿And mankind were not but one community, then they differed﴾ [Yunus: 19]. That is, they deviated from unity and agreement, which produce for them every good and happiness, into disagreement and discord, which entail corruption and the ruin of tilth and progeny. Since they were not created in vain, Allah bestowed upon them what would show them the path of right guidance in unity upon the truth, through the sending of the Prophets and the decisive Book that was sent down with them, as the continuation of the verse indicates: ﴿Then Allah sent forth the Prophets﴾, whom He raised above the rest of His creation, informing them of what He wills of His command, and sending them to His creation: ﴿as bearers of good news﴾ to whoever believes and obeys, ﴿and warners﴾ to whoever disbelieves and disobeys. ﴿And He sent down with them the Book﴾, that is, His speech, comprehensive of what they need in matters of religion, for uprightness and complete guidance, being ﴿with truth﴾ in every respect, ﴿that it might judge between people concerning that over which they differed﴾ regarding the beliefs and deeds in which they had been before that, being one community. Then they (the people) followed the Prophets' path with effort, then they went astray despite knowledge after the death of the Messengers, and so differed in religion because of their differing over the Book. ﴿And none differed concerning it﴾, that is, concerning the Book, the guiding Book (p. 529) which is free of any confusion, sent down to remove disagreement: ﴿except those who were given it﴾, that is, who knew it, yet they ﴿changed the blessing of Allah﴾ by causing dispute over what was sent down to remove dispute. Their disagreement was not due to any confusion on its part; rather, it arose ﴿after clear proofs had come to them﴾, that is, manifest evidences, ﴿out of rivalry among themselves﴾, that is, envy that arose among them. ﴿Then Allah guided those who believed﴾ through the Book ﴿to the truth concerning that over which they (the people of misguidance) had differed﴾, that is, to the truth about which they had disputed. In the mention of it in an ambiguous way first, and then explaining it second, there is an emphasis of its grandeur that is not hidden. ﴿By His permission﴾, that is, by His facilitation and kindness. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ is a confirmation of what preceded.

In Sahih Muslim, from ʿAʾishah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he rose at night to pray, would say: 'O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed! You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth concerning that over which they have differed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path...!'"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 214:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[214] ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Hardship and adversity touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.﴾

﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you﴾ That is, of the prophets and those who believed with them. The meaning is: while their example has not yet come to you, and you have not been tested with what they were tested with of tremendous circumstances, which are an example of horror and severity. This is the sunnah (way, or established custom) of Allah, which does not change. ﴿Touched them﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) that came as an answer to what the mind is led to ask, as if it were said: "How was their example?" (p. 530) Then it was said: ﴿hardship and adversity touched them﴾, that is, the hardships and pains. ﴿And they were shaken﴾, that is, they were disturbed, by what overwhelmed them of terrors and being poured out upon, a severe disturbance resembling the earthquake that nearly levels the earth and crushes the mountains. ﴿Until the Messenger﴾, that is, their affair reached the point of hardship to where their impatience compelled them to say, the Messenger, who is the most knowledgeable of people about the affairs of Allah, the Exalted, the most certain of His help, and the one who calls them to patience, ﴿and those who believed with him﴾, who are the most steadfast after him, resolved upon patience, certain of the promise of help, ﴿said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾, seeking it late and feeling that the period of hardship and toil was prolonged. Then it is said to them: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 5] ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 6], that is: be patient as they were patient, and you will be victorious!

A great portion of this trial occurred for the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, on the day of the Confederates, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you were thinking about Allah different thoughts﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10] ﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11] ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us only delusion"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12], and the verses.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was reclining on a cloak of his in the shade of the Ka'bah, and we said: 'Will you not seek help for us? Will you not supplicate for us?' He said: 'Among those before you, a man would be taken and a pit would be dug for him in the earth, and he would be placed in it. Then a saw would be brought and placed upon his head, and he would be split in two. And iron combs would be used on him, on what lies beneath his flesh and bone, yet that would not turn him from his religion. By Allah! Allah will surely complete this affair until a rider travels from Sana'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah and the wolf over his sheep, but you are hasty.'"

(p. 531) And in another narration: "While he was reclining on a cloak, and we had encountered severe hardship from the polytheists..."

When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan: "Did you fight him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How was the war between you?" He said: "Sijal (alternating), he gains over us and we gain over him." He said: "Thus are the messengers tested, and then the final outcome is theirs!"

This verse is like the verse: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 1] ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2] ﴿And We had already tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 3].

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[215] ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever wealth you spend that is good is for parents and near relatives, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.﴾

﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾ means: what kinds of wealth should they spend? ﴿Say: Whatever wealth you spend that is good is for parents﴾, who are mentioned first, before others, in order to fulfil the right of their upbringing, and because it is both an act of kinship and a charity. ﴿And the near relatives﴾ come after them, so that it is an act of kinship and a charity. ﴿Orphans﴾ come after them, because they combine poverty with incapacity. ﴿The needy﴾ come after them, because of their need. ﴿The wayfarer﴾ comes after them, because he is like the poor man, since his wealth is absent.

If it is said: how does the answer correspond to the question, when they asked about what they should spend, and were answered with a statement of the recipients? The answer is: His saying ﴿whatever wealth you spend that is good﴾ already includes an explanation of what they spend, which is every wealth they regard as good, and the speech was built upon what is more important, namely the explanation of the recipients, because spending is not counted unless it is placed where it belongs. The poet said:

*Indeed, a favour is not a favour until it reaches the path of the one who is made to benefit from it.*

*So when you do a favour, direct it to Allah, or to those of kin, or leave it.*

Thus the speech is of the wise method of address (al-uslub al-hakim, a rhetorical technique of answering a question with what the questioner should have asked), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189], as has preceded in this sūrah.

Al-Qaffal said: although the question came in the general wording "what", the intended question is about the manner, because they knew that what they were commanded to do was to spend wealth which would be an act of drawing near to Allah, exalted is He. When this is known, the mind does not turn to asking what that wealth is. When this is excluded from being the intended meaning, it becomes determined that what the question sought was: what is its recipient? Then the answer corresponds to the question. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is, for the cow has become confused to us, and indeed, if Allah wills, we will be guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 70], ﴿He said: He says it is a cow neither broken to work nor...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 71]. This answer corresponded to that question only because it was known that the cow is the animal whose nature and attributes are such-and-such. So His saying "what is it" cannot be taken to mean a request for its essence, and it is determined that what is meant by it is a request for the attribute by which that cow is distinguished from others. By this method we said that this answer corresponds to that question. Likewise here: since we know that they knew what they were commanded to spend, it must be concluded that their intention in saying ﴿what should they spend?﴾ is not a request for the essence, but a request for the recipients. Therefore this answer is excellent...!

Al-Raghib answered with two responses:

The first: they asked about both, saying: What should we spend? And upon whom should we spend? But the reporting of one of the two questions was omitted for brevity, and it was indicated by the answer, his saying ﴿whatever wealth you spend that is good﴾, as if it was said: what is spent is the good, and those upon whom it is spent are these. So he folded one of the two answers into the other, and this is a known method in rhetoric.

The second response: questions are of two kinds: a question of contention, whose right is that its answer should correspond to it, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it; and a question of learning, where the right of the teacher is that he should be like the physician who seeks the cure of a sick person, so he prescribes what will cure him, whether the patient asked for it or not. Since their need for someone to spend wealth upon them is like their need for what they should spend of wealth, He made clear to them both matters together. If it is said: how did He specify these particular persons and not others? It is answered: those who were mentioned were mentioned by way of example of those upon whom spending is made, not by way of restriction and comprehensiveness, since the categories of those upon whom spending is made are as has been mentioned in other places.

When He, exalted is He, had made clear the direction of expenditure and detailed it in this excellent and complete manner, He followed it with a general statement, and said: ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾. That is: all good that you do, whether with those mentioned or with others, seeking Allah's reward and desiring His abundant recompense, and fleeing from His painful punishment, indeed Allah is Knowing of it. "Knowing" (al-'Alim) is an intensive form of His being a knower, meaning: not even an atom's weight escapes His knowledge, on earth or in heaven, so He will reward you with the best of reward for it, as He said: ﴿Indeed I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female﴾ [Al 'Imran: 195], and He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7].

(p-534) The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[216] ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you. But perhaps you dislike a thing while it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing while it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾

﴿Prescribed﴾ means obligated. ﴿Fighting﴾ means fighting those who confront you in battle, as He said: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress﴾ [al-Baqarah: 190]. What is meant by fighting them is striving against them with that which annihilates them, subdues them, humiliates them, and weakens their strength.

Some of the wise have said: The sword of jihad and fighting is the sign of might. By it, cities were founded and towns were built up, doctrines and creeds spread, and laws and statutes were strengthened. By it, Islam was protected from being toyed with by the hands of meddlers in the past, and it is what protects it from the greed of the covetous in the present. By it, the dominion of Islam extended beyond the Ural Mountains to the north, the equator to the south, the Great Wall of China to the east, and the Pyrenees Mountains to the west..!

He said: Muslims must not evade the saying of some Europeans: "The Islamic religion spread by the sword!" For this saying does not harm the essence of the religion at all. Fair-minded Europeans know that it was established through preaching and persuasion, and that the sword was drawn only to protect the call. What harms the Muslims is evading it, for it keeps them from supporting the religion by the sword, leads them to submission and passivity, and makes them believe in abandoning the means, so they become weak, as is their condition today, and the powerful nations that have made the motto of their civilization "the sword or power" swallow them up..!

He said: Muslims must study the verses of jihad morning and evening, and reflect at length on His saying, exalted is He: (p-535) ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [al-Anfal: 60], perhaps they will be spurred to keep pace with the powerful, striving nations among the weak nations..!

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and it is hateful to you﴾, it derives from al-karh (dislike). The verbal noun has been placed in the position of the adjective for emphasis, like the saying of al-Khansa':

﴿For it is but advance and retreat﴾

As if it were itself dislike, because of the extreme dislike they had for it. Or it is a verb in the sense of a passive participle, like al-khubz (the bread) meaning al-makhbuz (the baked), i.e., "and it is disliked by you." This dislike arises from the aversion of the natural disposition toward fighting, because of its burden on wealth, the hardship on the soul, the danger to life, and fear. Therefore it does not contradict faith, for the dislike of natural disposition is innate and does not contradict contentment with what one is obligated to, like the sick person who drinks a foul-tasting medicine.

In al-Qamus and its commentary: al-karh, with a fatha or a damma, are two good dialects, meaning reluctance and hardship.

(p-536) Tha'lab said: Nafi' and the people of Medina recited in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿وهو كُرْهٌ لَكم﴾ with a damma on this word alone, and with a fatha throughout the rest of the Qur'an. ʿĀsim used to put a damma on this word and on the one in al-Ahqaf: ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا ووَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], and recited the rest with a fatha. Al-A'mash, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i used to put a damma on these three words, and on the one in al-Nisa': ﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكم أنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهًا﴾ [al-Nisa': 19], then they recited everything else with a fatha. Al-Azhari said: We choose what the people of the Hijaz hold: that everything in the Qur'an is with a fatha except the one in al-Baqarah specifically, for the readers have unanimously agreed upon it!. Tha'lab said: I know of no grammatical distinction between the words which these readers vocalized with a damma and those they vocalized with a fatha, nor any sunnah to be followed, and I do not see that people have agreed on the word in Surat al-Baqarah specifically, except that it is a noun while the rest of the Qur'an are verbal nouns.

Al-Azhari said: Many lexicographers have agreed that al-karah and al-kurh are two dialects, so whichever one occurs, it is permissible, except that al-Farra' distinguished between them, saying that al-kurh with a damma is what you compel yourself to, and with a fatha is what someone else compels you to. You say: "I came to you kurhan (unwillingly)" and "You made me enter kurhan (under compulsion)." Ibn Sidah said: al-karh is reluctance and hardship which you force upon yourself and so bear; with a damma, it is hardship you bear without having forced it upon yourself. One says: "He did that kurhan and ʿala kurhin." Ibn Barri said: (p-537) What supports the correctness of al-Farra''s view is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا﴾ [Al 'Imran: 83], and no one recited it with a damma on the kaf. And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ القِتالُ وهو كُرْهٌ لَكُمْ﴾, and no one recited it with a fatha on the kaf. Thus al-karh with a fatha becomes the act of one compelled, and al-kurh with a damma becomes the act of one who chooses.

﴿And perhaps you dislike a thing﴾ - such as jihad in the way of Allah, exalted is He - ﴿while it is good for you﴾, for in it is one of the two good outcomes: either victory and booty, or martyrdom and Paradise. ﴿And perhaps you love a thing﴾ - such as staying behind from the expedition - ﴿while it is bad for you﴾, because of the humiliation and poverty in it, and the deprivation of booty and reward. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what is good for you, ﴿while you know not﴾ that. So hasten to what He commands you, even if it is difficult for you, for He is Kind to the servants and commands them only with good.

Al-Harali said: The negation of knowledge from them with the word "lā" (not), which is for the future, so that it indicates the continuity of the state. ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85]. He said: This is in terms of the rank of this category of people, from among the Bedouins and others. As for the believers - that is, the firmly grounded - Allah has taught them from His knowledge what they knew: that fighting was good for them and that staying behind was bad for them.

Indeed, their knowledge of that overflowed onto their tongues in what brings tears and illuminates hearts, to the point that "the Prophet ﷺ consulted them about heading out to the Battle of Badr. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said well, (p-538) then ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said well. Then al-Miqdad ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, proceed with what Allah has commanded you, for we are with you. By Allah! We will not say to you what the children of Israel said to Moses: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24]. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight, and we are fighting with you! By Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to travel to Barak al-Ghimad, we would strive alongside you against whatever lies beyond it until you reach it..! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him good words and supplicated for him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Advise me, O people!" Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: By Allah! It is as if you mean us, O Messenger of Allah! He said: "Indeed." He said: We have believed in you and affirmed you, and testified that what you have brought is the truth, and we have given you upon that our covenants and pledges of hearing and obedience. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, with what you intend, for we are with you. By Him who sent you with the truth! If you were to lead us across this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you. Not one man among us would stay behind, and we do not dislike that you meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are steadfast in war, true in encounter; perhaps Allah will show you from us what will gladden your eye. So march with us in the blessing of Allah."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 217 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[217] ﴿They ask you about fighting in the Sacred Month. Say: Fighting therein is great, but averting from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, and (barring access to) the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it, is greater in the sight of Allah. And persecution is worse than killing. And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while a disbeliever - those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

(p-539) ﴿They ask you about fighting in the Sacred Month﴾. Al-Raghib said: The ones asking about this are said to be the polytheists, intending to reproach the Muslims for what they had transgressed of killing in the Sacred Month. And it is said: they are the people of Islam.

Al-Tabarani in "al-Kabir", al-Bayhaqi in his "Sunan", Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Jundub ibn Abdullah: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched a detachment and appointed over them Abdullah ibn Jahsh. They encountered Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, and they did not know that that day was of Rajab or of Jumada. The polytheists said to the Muslims: 'You have killed in the Sacred Month.' So Allah revealed this verse. Some of them said: 'If they did not commit a sin, then they have no reward.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated and strove in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 218] - the verse."

Ibn Mandah narrated it from the Companions, from Ibn Abbas.

The summary of what Imam Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned in "Zad al-Ma'ad" and Ibn Hisham in "al-Sirah" concerning this expedition and the revelation of this verse: "The Prophet ﷺ sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh al-Asadi to Nakhlah in Rajab, at the beginning of the seventeenth month after the Hijrah, with twelve men from the Emigrants, each two of them taking turns upon a camel. They arrived at Batn Nakhlah, watching for a caravan of Quraysh. In this expedition Abdullah ibn Jahsh was named Amir al-Mu'minin. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had written him a letter and commanded him not to look into it until he had travelled two days, and then to look into it. When he had travelled two days, he opened the letter and found in it: 'When you look into this letter of mine, proceed until you alight at Nakhlah - between Makkah and al-Ta'if - and watch there for a caravan of Quraysh, and bring us news of their affairs.' He said: 'Hearing and obeying!' He informed his companions of this, and that he would not compel them; whoever loves martyrdom, let him advance, and whoever dislikes death, let him return. As for me, I am advancing! So they all advanced. When they were on the way, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Utbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs which they were taking turns riding, so they stayed behind to search for it. Abdullah ibn Jahsh went on until he alighted at Nakhlah, and a caravan of Quraysh passed by him, carrying raisins, leather, and merchandise, among them Amr ibn al-Hadrami, Uthman and Nawfal, the two sons of Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, a freedman of Banu al-Mughirah. The Muslims consulted and said: 'We are on the last day of Rajab. If you leave these people this night, they will enter the Haram and be protected there from you; and if you kill them, you will be killing them in the Sacred Month!' The people hesitated and were reluctant to advance against them, then they encouraged themselves against them and resolved to fight them. One of them shot Amr ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, and they captured Uthman and al-Hakam, while Nawfal escaped and eluded them. Then Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions came with the caravan and the two captives until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, having set aside from it the fifth - which was the first fifth in Islam, the first person killed in Islam, and the first two captives in Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disapproved of what they had done, and Quraysh's reproach and denunciation grew intense; they claimed that they had found an argument, and said: 'Muhammad has made the Sacred Month lawful.' This weighed heavily on the Muslims until Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They ask you about fighting in the Sacred Month﴾ - the verse."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿fighting therein﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the month", a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion), because fighting occurs within the month.

Al-Kisa'i said: it is in the genitive case by repetition (al-takrir), meaning the estimated sense is: "about fighting therein". This is the meaning of al-Farra's statement: it is in the genitive by an implied "an" (about). This is very weak, because the preposition's governing function does not remain after its deletion in the usual usage...! Abu Ubaydah said: it is in the genitive by proximity (al-jiwar). This is further removed than their two views, because proximity belongs to the places of necessity and irregularity, and what can be avoided should not be interpreted by it. In this there is also the possibility that it is an attributive adjective (na't) to "fighting", and the possibility that it is connected to it as it is connected to "fighting" (qatil).

It has been read in the nominative in an irregular reading, and its basis is that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, together with the interrogative hamza, its estimated form being: "Is fighting therein permissible?"

(p-541) ﴿Say﴾ in answer to them: ﴿Fighting therein is great﴾, i.e., a grave matter that is condemned. The Arabs used not to shed blood nor raid an enemy in the sacred months, which are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab. We will mention, in a forthcoming note, the verification of whether the prohibition of fighting in them is muhkam (definitive) or mansukh (abrogated).

Al-Raghib said: If it is asked: why did it not say "fighting therein is great", since the rule for an indefinite noun mentioned, when it is repeated, is that it is repeated in the definite form, as in: "You asked me about a man, and the man is such and such?" It is said: mentioning it indefinitely is an indication that not all fighting in the Sacred Month has this ruling, for the Prophet's ﷺ fighting against the people of Makkah did not have this ruling, as he said: "An hour of a day was made lawful for me, and it was not lawful for anyone before me."

﴿And averting from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from His religion which leads to His good pleasure, or from the Sacred House, for the Prophet ﷺ called the Hajj "the way of Allah."

Al-Harali said: "Sadd" (averting) is turning away to a direction with aversion and dislike; and "sabil" (way) is the well-trodden main road whose path is evident to every traveller. "Sadd" is the subject (mubtada').

(p-542) ﴿And disbelief in Him﴾, i.e., in the way - meaning the religion - or in Allah; it is conjoined to it. ﴿And the Sacred Mosque﴾ is conjoined to ﴿the way of Allah﴾, i.e., "and averting from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque." Al-Farra claimed that it is conjoined to the pronoun in "bihi" (in Him), i.e., "disbelief in Him and in the Sacred Mosque." ﴿And expelling its people﴾, i.e., the people of the Sacred Mosque - namely the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers who are his allies - and it is conjoined also to "averting": ﴿from it﴾, from the Sacred Mosque. The predicate of the three nouns is: ﴿is greater in the sight of Allah﴾ in crime than what the detachment did, namely their killing of them in the Sacred Month, because expulsion is a persecution: ﴿and persecution is worse than killing﴾ in the Sacred Month, i.e., they have done to you in the Sacred Mosque what is greater than killing in it, and the sanctity of the Mosque is like the sanctity of the month...! This is one view; and it is said that the predicate of "sadd" and "kufr" is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

Al-Razi pointed to another grammatical analysis, namely that "sadd" and "kufr" are conjoined to "great" (kabir), i.e., "fighting therein, described by these attributes." In that case, "akbar" is the predicate of "ikhraj" alone.

Al-Mahayimi inclined to this view when he said in his "Tafsir":
﴿Say: fighting therein is great﴾ among the major sins; how much more so when it is: ﴿and averting from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from trade, which Allah made a path of sustenance for His servants; and if this killing were permitted, it would be: ﴿and disbelief in Him﴾ and averting from the Sacred Mosque when the pilgrims who go out are killed in the Sacred Month. This is the reason for the prohibition of fighting in this month. But: {expelling its people} - i.e., their expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque, who are the Prophet and the believers: ﴿from it is greater in the sight of Allah﴾ to the end. This mode of grammatical analysis is novel, while most scholars follow the first.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in "Zad al-Ma'ad" concerning the interpretation of this verse: Allah the Exalted says: "What you have denounced them for - though it is great - what you yourselves have committed of disbelief in Allah, averting from His way and from His House, expelling the Muslims - who are its people - from it, the shirk you are upon, and the persecution that arose (p-543) from you through it, is greater in the sight of Allah than their fighting in the Sacred Month." Among what has been attributed to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning this meaning are these verses, though it is said they belong to Abdullah ibn Jahsh:

You count killing in the sacred month a great thing, but greater than it, were the rightly-guided to see the right path, is
Your averting from what Muhammad says, and disbelief in it, while Allah is Seer and Witness,
And your expelling from the Mosque of Allah its people, lest Allah be worshipped with prostration in the House,
Even if you reproach us for killing him, while the revolter and the envious spread alarm about Islam,
We gave to drink from Ibn al-Hadrami our spears at Nakhlah when the inflamer of war, Waqid, kindled it,
Blood; and Ibn Abdullah, Uthman, is between us, struggling against the shackle of hide, the stubborn one.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in "Zad al-Ma'ad": Most of the early scholars interpreted "fitnah" here as shirk, as in His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193], and His saying supports this: ﴿Then their fitnah was only that they said: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], i.e., the outcome of their shirk, its consequence and final matter, was only that they disowned it and denied it. Its reality is the shirk which calls its adherent to it, fights for it, and punishes whoever is not seduced by it. For this reason they will be told at the time of their punishment with the Fire and their fitnah: ﴿Taste your fitnah﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 14]. Ibn Abbas said: your denial. Its reality: taste the end of your fitnah, its limit and the destination of its matter, as in His saying: ﴿Taste what you used to earn﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. Just as they persecuted His servants away from shirk, they are persecuted at the Fire and it is said to them: (p-544) ﴿Taste your fitnah﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 14]. From it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent﴾ [al-Buruj: 10]; the fitnah here has been explained as their torturing the believers and burning them with fire, though the wording is more general than that. Its reality: they tortured the believers in order to seduce them from their religion. This is the fitnah attributed to the polytheists. As for the fitnah which Allah attributes to Himself and which His Messenger attributes to Him, such as His saying: ﴿And thus We tried some of them by means of others﴾ [al-An'am: 53], and Musa's saying: ﴿It is only Your trial; You lead astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will﴾ [al-A'raf: 155], that is with another meaning, namely trial, testing and affliction from Allah upon His servants with good and evil, with blessings and calamities. So this is one kind; the fitnah of the polytheists is another kind; the fitnah of the believer in his wealth, his children and his neighbour is yet another kind. The fitnah which is caused among the people of Islam, like the fitnah which arose between the companions of Ali and Mu'awiyah, and between the people of the Camel and Siffin, and among the Muslims until they fight one another and abandon one another, is another kind; and it is the fitnah about which Muhammad ﷺ said: "There will be a fitnah in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running....", and the hadiths of fitnah - in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded withdrawal from the two groups - refer to this fitnah. Fitnah is sometimes used to mean sin, as in His saying: ﴿And among them is he who says: Grant me leave and do not tempt me﴾ [al-Tawbah: 49], said by al-Jadd ibn Qays when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him to Tabuk; he said: Grant me leave to stay behind and do not tempt me by exposing me to the yellow women of the Romans, for I cannot be patient (p-546) regarding them...!

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Surely into fitnah they have fallen﴾ [al-Tawbah: 49], i.e., they fell into the fitnah of hypocrisy and fled into it from the fitnah of the yellow women.

Its purpose: God, glory be to Him, judged between His friends and His enemies with justice and equity. He did not absolve His allies of committing sin by killing in the Sacred Month; rather, God declared that it is a grave matter, and that what His enemies, the polytheists, are engaged in is greater and more monstrous than the mere fighting in the Sacred Month. They are therefore more deserving of blame, reproach and punishment, especially His allies. [Those who fought] were either interpreting (their action) or were negligent in a minor way that God forgives them for, in light of what they did of monotheism, acts of obedience, emigration with His Messenger, and preferring what is with God. They are, as it has been said:

"When the beloved commits a single sin, his good deeds come with a thousand intercessors."

So how can he be compared with the hateful enemy who came with every ugliness and did not bring a single intercessor of good deeds?!

Reminder:

The majority agreed that the ruling of this verse is the prohibition of fighting in the Sacred Month. Then they differed as to whether that ruling remains or has been abrogated (naskh).

Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Zad al-Ma'ad*, in the chapter he devoted to what the Battle of Khaybar contains of legal rulings, the following text: "Among them is fighting and battling the disbelievers in the Sacred Months, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Hudaybiyyah in Dhu al-Hijjah, then he stayed there and then marched to Khaybar in Muharram, likewise. Al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Marwan and al-Miswar, and al-Waqidi likewise said: he set out at the beginning of the seventh year of the Hijrah. However, there is consideration in using this as evidence, for his departure was at the end of Muharram, not at its beginning, and its conquest was only in Safar. Stronger than this argument is the Prophet's (ﷺ) pledge of his companions under the tree, the Pledge of Ridwan, to fight and not to flee. It was in Dhu al-Qa'dah. But there is no proof in that, because he only pledged them to that when it reached him that they had killed Uthman while they intended to fight him; then he took the pledge of the Companions. There is no disagreement on the permissibility of fighting in the Sacred Month defensively, and the disagreement is only over whether fighting may be initiated in it. The majority permitted it and said: the prohibition of fighting in it has been abrogated, and this is the position of the four Imams, may God have mercy on them (p-547). 'Ata' and others went to the view that it is established and not abrogated; 'Ata' used to swear by God that fighting in the Sacred Month is not lawful, and nothing of its prohibition has been abrogated..! Stronger than these two arguments is the argument from the Prophet's (ﷺ) siege of al-Ta'if. He set out toward it at the end of Shawwal and besieged them for some twenty nights, and some of these were in Dhu al-Qa'dah. He conquered Makkah ten nights before the end of Ramadan, and stayed there after the conquest for nineteen days shortening the prayer, then went out toward Hawazin when twenty days of Shawwal remained, and God granted him victory over Hawazin and he divided their spoils. Then he went from there to al-Ta'if, and they besieged him for twenty nights. This necessarily implies that part of it was in Dhu al-Qa'dah without doubt. It has been said that he besieged them for some ten nights. Ibn Hazm said: this is the correct view without doubt. But this is strange from him: from where does he get this certainty and this firm judgment..? In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik regarding the story of al-Ta'if, he said: 'We besieged them for forty days, and they resisted and held out,' and he mentioned the hadith. This siege therefore undoubtedly occurred in Dhu al-Qa'dah. Yet even so, there is no proof in the story, because the campaign against al-Ta'if was part of the completion of the Battle of Hunayn. They had begun the fighting against the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When they were routed, their king, Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri, entered the fortress of al-Ta'if with Thaqif, and they waged war against the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Their fighting was therefore part of the completion of the campaign in which he had begun, and God knows best."

God, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Ma'idah, which is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed and contains nothing abrogated (p-548): ﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month or the offering or the garlands﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2]. And He said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting therein. Say: Fighting therein is great, but averting from the way of God...﴾. These are two Madani verses; between their revelation lies about eight years. There is nothing in the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger that abrogates their ruling, and the Ummah has not agreed on its abrogation. Whoever cites as evidence for abrogation His saying: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36] and similar general statements, has cited for abrogation what does not prove it. Whoever cites as evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abu 'Amir on a detachment to Awtas in Dhu al-Qa'dah, has argued without proof, because that was part of the battle in which the polytheists had initiated the fighting, and it was not an initiation on his part of fighting them in the Sacred Month.

﴿And they will not cease﴾ - meaning the people of Makkah -: ﴿fighting you﴾ - O believers -: ﴿until they turn you back from your religion﴾, that is, they return you from your religion of Islam to disbelief: ﴿if they are able﴾, that is, if they are capable of making you apostatize. In this there is a sense of improbability about their capability, like the saying of a man to his enemy: "If you overpower me, then do not spare me," while he is confident that he will not overpower him. The clause ﴿and they will not cease﴾ is either coordinated with ﴿they ask you﴾ or parenthetical. The purpose is to warn the believers against them and to disregard agreeing with them in some matters, because of the firmness of their enmity and their persistence in seducing (people) from the religion.

The verse implies that you are more entitled to not cease fighting them, because they are certain that you are upon the truth and that you will be victorious, and that they are upon falsehood and will be forsaken, and this is inevitable however long the period; because you rely on God and they rely on their own strength. Whoever is left to himself is lost. So the matter between you and them is more serious than mere speech. It is therefore fitting to prepare for it with its equipment and to get ready for it with its readiness, let alone to be swayed by their words, which the devils inspire to them as slander against the religion and as obstruction from the path. Al-Biqa'i pointed to this.

Then God warned against apostasy by saying: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion﴾, which is Islam. The form of the verb *ifti'al* from apostasy, which implies effort and deliberateness, indicates that whoever engages with the religion of truth is far from returning from it, and so he is one who strains himself in that matter: ﴿and dies while he is a disbeliever - those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾, that is, all their beneficial efforts have been nullified and rendered void: ﴿in this world﴾ - for the security over their wealth and families is lifted -: ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ - for their reward is forfeited, so they will not be recompensed there for their good deeds. {And} it is not restricted to this; rather: ﴿those are the companions of the Fire﴾, that is, its people: ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾, remaining, not dying nor leaving, like the rest of the disbelievers.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[218] ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of Allah — those hope for the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have believed﴾ — [believed] in the sanctity of the month in itself and the permissibility of fighting those who expelled the people of the Sacred Mosque from it. ﴿And those who have emigrated﴾ — they left Makkah and their kinsfolk when they were expelled from the Sacred Mosque. ﴿And have striven in the cause of Allah﴾ — even in the sacred month, for the purpose of defending themselves. ﴿Those﴾ — even though they engaged in fighting (p-550) in the sacred month. ﴿Hope for the mercy of Allah﴾ — that is, His Paradise, for their faith, their emigration and their striving. The hope is attributed to them without the attainment of what is hoped for, to indicate that they know that deeds do not necessitate the reward, which is rather by way of His bounty, glory be to Him, and not because there is any doubt in their attaining it. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ — for their violating the sanctity of the month. ﴿Merciful﴾ — by overlooking their fighting, despite the existence of an indication of its prohibition, so He did not punish them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[219] ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [some] benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses that you may give thought.﴾

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ This is the first verse revealed concerning wine, according to what Ibn 'Umar, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. Then the verse in Surat al-Nisa' was revealed, and then the verse in al-Ma'idah.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi related from 'Umar that he said, when the prohibition of wine was revealed: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification!" So this verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ to the end of the verse. 'Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification." Then the verse in al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:43]. So the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he called to prayer, would announce: "No intoxicated person is to approach the prayer." 'Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification." Then the verse in al-Ma'idah was revealed, and 'Umar was summoned and it was recited to him. When it reached ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:91], 'Umar said: "We have desisted, we have desisted."

The reality of wine (haqiqat al-khamr) is whatever intoxicates from any substance. Al-Shaykhan related from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks wine in this world and dies while persisting in it, without repenting of it, will not drink it in the Hereafter."

As for gambling (al-maysir): it is al-qimar (gambling), with a kasrah on the qaf, a verbal noun from yasara, like al-maw'id and al-marji' from their verbs. One says: "yasartuhu" when you gamble with him (qamartuhu). Its derivation is either from al-yusr (ease), because it is taking a man's wealth with ease and facility without toil or exertion, or from al-yasar (wealth), because it strips him of his wealth.

Its description: they had ten arrows called al-azlam and al-aqlam, and they are: al-Fadhdh, al-Tawam, al-Raqib, al-Hils (with a kasrah on the unpointed ha' and a sukun on the lam, and like kataf), al-Nafis, al-Musbil (like muhsin), al-Mu'alla (like mu'azzam), al-Manih (like amir), al-Safih (on the pattern of what precedes it), and al-Waghd. For each of them there is a known share of a slaughtered camel, which they slaughter and divide into ten parts, as Abu 'Umar said, or into twenty-eight parts, as al-Asma'i said, and this is the more common view, except three of them, which are al-Manih, al-Safih and al-Waghd, and these have no shares. The arrows are multiplied only out of dislike of suspicion. Someone among them said:

"I have in this world arrows, none of which has a gain,
and their names: Waghd, Safih and Manih."

So al-Fadhdh has one arrow, that is, one portion. al-Tawam has two, al-Raqib three, al-Hils four, al-Nafis five, al-Musbil six, and al-Mu'alla seven. They place them in al-Rababah, which is a bag, and place it in the hands of a trustworthy man. Then he shakes it and puts his hand in and brings out an arrow, [assigned to] man after man. If the arrow that comes out for him is one of those with shares, he takes the share marked with that arrow. If the arrow that comes out for him is one of those without a share, he takes nothing and must pay the full price of the camel. They would give those shares to the poor and not eat from them, and they took pride in that, and they reviled whoever did not take part in it, calling him al-Baram (with two fathahs). This is as stated in al-Kashshaf, with additions.

In al-Qamus and its commentary: al-maysir is playing with the arrows, or it is the camel over which they gambled. When they wanted to play for it, they bought a camel on credit, slaughtered it, and divided it into twenty-eight parts, or ten parts. Then, when one arrow came out for each man, the winning of those for whom the arrows with shares came out was manifest, and the one for whom the blank arrow came out bore the loss.
