The camel was called maysir only because it is divided into parts. Anything you divide into parts, you have made easy (yassarta); and you yassarta the she-camel when you divide its meat; and the people yassarū the camel, that is, they cut it up and shared out its parts. Suhaym ibn Wuthayl al-Yarbu'i said:

"I say to them at al-Sha'b when they make me a share,
Do you not know that I am the son of the knight Zahdam?"

He had been captured as a prisoner of war, and they cast arrows over him. His saying "yaysirunani" is from al-maysir, that is, they divide me up and share me out. And Labid said:

"Refrain from the women and give them your fat maysir [camel]."

Here he made the camel itself the maysir. Al-Saghani reported that al-maysir is backgammon. Mujahid said: everything in which there is gambling is from al-maysir, even the children's playing with nuts.

﴿In them is great sin﴾ That is, mighty. It is read also with a thaa (al-muthallathah). This is because of what it contains of evils that oppose the excellent qualities of the Shari'ah, such as lying, abuse, loss of intellect, and making lawful the property of others. ﴿and [some] benefit for people﴾ worldly benefits, such as pleasure, merriment, and trade in wine, and gaining wealth without toil in gambling. In the prior mention of its sin, its description as great, and the delaying of mention of its benefits together with restricting them to people, there are indications of the predominance of the former, which is not hidden from what His saying, Exalted is He, has expressed: ﴿but their sin is greater than their benefit﴾, that is, the corruptions that result from engaging in them are greater than the benefits that result from them. That is, their harm and their corruption, which are dominant, are not balanced, because they relate to the intellect and religion. In this there is a deterrence from them that is not hidden. For this reason this verse was a preparation for the absolute prohibition of wine, and it was not explicit but allusive. For this reason, 'Umar, when it was recited to him, said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a healing clarification!" until the explicit prohibition was revealed in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:90], ﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred between you through wine and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:91].

Note:

Many leading physicians and philosophers have composed works specifically on the harms of intoxicants.

In some lands of the Christians, international conferences have continually been held, to which representatives from all the major nations of the world are invited, to combat intoxicants, to denounce them, and to declare their effect on bodies, minds and spirits, and the financial losses that arise from them. Among what fifty physicians established are these statements:

1. Intoxicants do not quench thirst but increase it.
2. They are of no use at all in the performance of tasks.
3. They halt mental and physical growth in children.
4. They weaken the strength of will, leading to the commission of destructive acts, and drag people into poverty and misery.
5. They are among the sedatives, like henbane and ether.
6. They prepare the body for contagious diseases.
7. They prepare, in a particular way, for tuberculosis and consumption.
8. They harm more than they benefit in pneumonia and typhoid fever.
9. They hasten the sorrowful end in diseases that end in death, and prolong the period of recovery in diseases that end in health.
10. They prepare for sunstroke and heat exhaustion in the days of heat.
11. They hasten the dissipation of heat in the days of cold.
12. They alter the substance of the heart and the blood vessels.
13. They often cause inflammation of the nerves and severe pains.
14. They hasten the destruction of the body's cells.
15. The great quantity consumed by people of physical labour from their drinks is the cause of their misery, their poverty and the loss of their health.
16. Abstaining from them leads to the health and happiness of the human race.

﴿And they ask you what they should spend﴾ That is, what they should give in charity from their wealth. ﴿Say, "The excess"﴾ and it is what exceeds the expenditure, that is, the surplus that can be set aside because there is no need for it.

In the two Sahihs, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The best charity is that given from a surplus of wealth, and begin with those you support."

Muslim related from Jabir that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Begin with yourself and give charity to it. If there is surplus, then to your family. If there is surplus beyond your family, then to your relatives. If there is surplus beyond your relatives, then here and here (i.e., in every direction)."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related from Abu Hurayrah who said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'I have a dinar.' He said: 'Spend it on yourself.' He said: 'I have another.' He said: 'Spend it on your child.' He said: 'I have another.' He said: 'Spend it on your family.' He said: 'I have another.' He said: 'Spend it on your servant.' He said: 'I have another.' He said: 'You know best.'"

﴿Thus﴾ that is, as what has been mentioned was made clear to you: ﴿Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ that is, the command, the prohibition, and the worthlessness of this world: ﴿that you may give thought.﴾

"Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 220:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[220] ﴿In this world and the Hereafter. And they ask you concerning orphans. Say, "Improving their affairs is good. And if you mix your affairs with theirs, then they are your brothers. And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer. And if Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise."﴾

﴿In this world﴾ — that it is perishable — ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ — that it is everlasting. And [reflect] in their affairs so that you may reform them and not take on what corrupts them, so that you do not abandon the lasting pleasures for the perishing pleasures.

(p-556) ﴿And they ask you concerning orphans﴾. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When the saying of Allah, exalted is He, was revealed: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾ [al-An'am: 152], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will be burned in a Blaze﴾ [al-Nisa': 10], those who had orphans in their care separated their food from the orphan's food and their drink from the orphan's drink. They began to set aside some of the orphan's food and drink, and it was kept for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This became difficult for them. They mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And they ask you concerning orphans﴾ — the verse — so they mixed their food with his food and their drink with his drink."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Improving their affairs is good."﴾ That is: mixing with them in a manner of reform, for them and for their property, is better than keeping away from them. The ultimate purpose of mixing — I mean reform — has been placed in its stead, to alert that what is commanded is a mixing whose result of reform is evident, as if it were the very essence of reform. ﴿And if you mix with them﴾ — that is, you live with them and do not keep apart from them — ﴿then they are your brothers﴾ — they are your brothers in religion, which is stronger than the bond of lineage. And among the rights of brotherhood is mixing with them through reform and benefit.

Al-Isbahani said: If this is broad regarding the property of orphans, it is broader regarding others. This is a principle that supports what companions do on journeys: they bring out expenses equally, and they differ in the amount of food they eat.

(p-557) ﴿And Allah knows the corrupter﴾ of their property ﴿from the reformer﴾ of it, and He will recompense him according to the measure of his mixing. So beware of Him and do not seek anything other than reform. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty﴾ — He would have compelled you into ʿanat, which is hardship, and made you strait, so He would not have permitted you to mix with them, and nothing prevents Him from that. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might﴾ — that is, Dominant over what He wills. ﴿Wise﴾ — that is, the Doer of His acts according to what wisdom requires, the wisdom that calls for basing the obligations on the foundation of capacity.

Furthermore, al-Qadi interpreted His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Improving their affairs is good"﴾ as referring to the aspects of benefit and good returning to the guardian and the orphan. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This statement encompasses consideration of the welfare of the orphan's interests through correction, discipline and other means, so that he grows up with knowledge, good manners and virtue, because this conduct has a greater effect on him than improving his condition through trade. It also includes the improvement of his wealth, so that it is not consumed by expenditure through trade. Also included is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give the orphans their property and do not substitute the bad for the good﴾ [al-Nisa': 2]. And the meaning of His saying "good" encompasses the situation of the guardian, that is: this action is better for him than being negligent regarding the right of the orphan; and it also encompasses the situation of the orphan, that is: this action is better for the orphan in that it includes the reform of his self and the reform of his property. Thus this phrase comprehends all the interests of the orphan and the guardian.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I and the one who cares for an orphan will be in Paradise like this," and he pointed with his index and middle fingers and spread them apart. Muslim also narrated something similar in his Sahih."

(p-٥٥٨) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[221] ﴿And do not marry idolatresses until they believe. A believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even though she may please you. And do not marry idolaters until they believe. A believing slave is better than an idolater, even though he may please you. Those invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes His verses clear to the people that they may be reminded.﴾

﴿And do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾, i.e., do not marry worshippers of idols until they believe in Allah, exalted is He.

Ibn Kathir said: This is a prohibition from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the believers marrying idolatresses from among the worshippers of idols. Then, if its generality is intended, and every idolatress is included, whether a woman of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab) or an idolatress, then He has specified from this the women of the People of the Book by His saying: ﴿And [lawful to you are] the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5].

Al-Allamah al-Razi has extensively discussed here the question of whether the term "mushrik" (polytheist) encompasses disbelievers from among the People of the Book. Refer to him.

The verified position is that the term "mushrik" does not encompass the Kitabi (a person of the Scripture), because the verses of the Qur'an are explicit in distinguishing between them. One of them is joined to the other in such verses as: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 6]. The secret of that is that the mushrik is one who adheres to polytheism, i.e., the origin of his religion is association (of partners with Allah). The Kitabi, though polytheism may have entered his religion, was not so from its origin and essence.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress﴾ is a reason for the prohibition against associating with them, and an encouragement to associate with believing women; i.e., a believing slave woman, despite the lowliness of slavery and the lack of standing that accompanies it, is better than an idolatress, despite the nobility of freedom and the elevation of status she may have. For the deficiency of servitude in her is compensated by faith, which is the most sublime of human perfections. ﴿Even though she may please you﴾, i.e., the idolatress, by her beauty, lineage (p-٥٥٩) and other things. For the deficiency of disbelief is not compensated by them.

﴿And do not marry idolaters﴾, with the letter ta' pronounced with a damma, from the causative (inkah), which means marriage; i.e., do not marry off the disbelievers, of whatever disbelief they may be, to Muslim women: ﴿until they believe﴾ and abandon what they are in of disbelief. ﴿And a believing slave, despite the humiliation of servitude that he has, ﴿is better than an idolater, even though he may please you﴾ by the motive of worldly desire for him, for the loss of equal standing (kafa'ah) through disbelief is not compensated by anything of that. This implies, by way of greater emphasis, that a believing free woman and a believing free man are better, with great honour being given to them by omitting mention of them, to inform that their superiority is a certain matter, and that the comparison is only between those whom they used to consider lowly, whom faith has ennobled, and those whom they consider noble, whom disbelief has debased. Therefore the one described as believing is mentioned in both places, to show that he, though lowly, is the locus of preference because of the loftiness of his attribute. And the attribute of idolatry is affirmed in both places limited to it, because it is the locus of contempt, even if his described person is elevated by custom. So said al-Biqa'i.

Then He pointed to the reason for the prohibition by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., those mentioned, of the idolatresses and the idolaters: ﴿invite﴾ whoever associates with them and lives among them: ﴿to the Fire﴾, i.e., to that which leads to it, of disbelief and wickedness. For marriage is the reason for familiarity, affection and love, and all of that necessitates agreement in aims and purposes. So it is their due that one should not befriend them nor become related to them by marriage..!: ﴿But Allah invites﴾, i.e., by what He commands through the tongues of His messengers: ﴿to Paradise and forgiveness﴾, i.e., to the action that leads to them. The placing of Paradise here before forgiveness, though forgiveness precedes it, is for the sake of observing the contrast with the Fire at the outset: ﴿by His permission﴾, by His command: ﴿and He makes clear His verses﴾, His command and His prohibition regarding marriage: ﴿to the people that they may be reminded﴾, so that they may take heed and refrain from marrying the forbidden, and befriend the friends of Allah, who are the believers, through association and intermarriage, and thus attain what they have been called to, of Paradise and forgiveness.

That said, it has been said: the meaning of ﴿But Allah invites﴾ is "and the friends of Allah invite", who are the believers, by omitting the genitive term (al-mudaf) and placing the genitive complement (al-mudaf ilayh) in its position, in honour of them and magnification of their status, since He made their action as His own action in form; and its purpose is observing the contrast, as if it were said: "The enemies of Allah invite to the Fire, and the friends of Allah (p-٥٦٠) invite to Paradise and forgiveness." However, there is in this the loss of an observance suited to the pronouns, for the pronoun in the clause conjoined to the predicate, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He makes clear﴾, refers to Allah, exalted is He, so there would result a disjunction (tafkik).

Admonition:

Al-Raghib said: The reality of remembrance (tadhakkur) is recollection after forgetting or heedlessness, of what the heart has become confused about. He said: If it is asked, "To what did this remembrance refer?" It is said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has composed within us, by innate nature (fitrah), knowledge of Him and knowledge of His bounties. A person, by acquiring knowledge, remembers what is mentioned in it; this is the meaning of remembrance. Then he said: It has been said: hope from Allah is obligatory, in the sense that if we hope in Him, He fulfils our hope. He said: This is a matter whose reality cannot be conceived unless we attain it by engaging in these actions which Allah, exalted is He, has stipulated. Therefore its apprehension is difficult for us.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[222] ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they are purified. When they have purified themselves, go to them as Allah has commanded you. Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves.﴾

﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾ It is the blood that issues from the womb in a specific manner at a specific time. It is also called al-hayd (menstruation). That is, they asked whether it necessitates and requires avoiding touching the woman who has it. ﴿Say: It is a harm﴾ That is, menstruation is something that is considered repugnant and harms whoever approaches it, out of aversion to it and dislike of it. ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾ That is, avoid having intercourse with them during its period.

Al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani) said: In His words, ﴿It is a harm﴾, there is an indication that reason requires avoiding it, as if it were said: Menstruation is a harm, and every harm is shunned. Since a person may bear harm and not regard it as forbidden, He stated its prohibition explicitly by His words: ﴿so keep away from women﴾.

Imam Ahmad and Muslim narrated from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would not eat with her, nor would they have intercourse with them in the houses. The companions of the Prophet ﷺ asked the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harm﴾ to the end of the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do everything except intercourse.' This reached the Jews, and they said: 'This man does not want to leave any of our matters without opposing us in it!' Then Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr came and said: 'O Messenger! The Jews say such-and-such, so should we not have intercourse with them?' The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed until we thought he was displeased with them both. They went out, and a gift of milk was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, so he sent after them and gave them to drink, and they knew that he was not displeased with them."

﴿And do not approach them until they are purified﴾ This is an emphasis of the ruling of keeping away, and an indication that what is meant by it is not to approach them to intercourse, rather than not to be near them at all. He referred to approaching them, which is forbidden, as a metaphor for lying with them. Thus it indicates the permissibility of enjoying them at that time in what falls short of the private part.

In the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: "I used to comb the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was menstruating."

Also in both of them, from her as well, she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would lean on my lap while I was menstruating, and then he would recite the Qur'an."

Muslim also narrated from her, as well, she said: "I used to drink while I was menstruating, then I would hand it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been, and drink. And I would take a bone and gnaw the meat off it while I was menstruating, then I would hand it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he would place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been."

In the two Sahihs, and the wording is Muslim's, from Maymunah, she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would touch his wives above the waist-wrapper while they were menstruating."

In another wording of his: "He would lie down with me while I was menstruating, and between me and him there was a garment."

His words, ﴿until they are purified﴾, explain the limit of keeping away. It has been recited in the seven canonical readings (qira'at, the recognized recitations): with a fatha on the ta and the ha with shadda (tashdid, gemination), and with a sukun on the ta and a damma on the ha, unshadda (lightened). The first reading explicitly indicates that the limit of the prohibition of approaching is bathing, as His words indicate: ﴿When they have purified themselves﴾, etc. The second reading, although it indicates that the limit is the cessation of the blood, based on what has been said that purity (tuhr) is the cessation of blood and purification (tatahhur) is bathing, nevertheless, when His words ﴿When they have purified themselves﴾ are added to it, the whole becomes the limit. This is like a man saying: "Do not speak to so-and-so until he enters the house; then, when he has entered, if his soul is content, speak to him!" It is necessary that the permissibility of speaking to him depend on both matters together. Likewise, the verse, since it indicates the obligation of both matters, requires that this prohibition not end except when both matters are fulfilled. So the two readings return to one meaning, as we have explained.

Muslim narrated from Aisha that "Asma asked the Prophet ﷺ about bathing after menstruation. He said: (p-563) 'One of you takes her water and her lote-leaves and purifies herself, and does the purification well. Then she pours water over her head and rubs it vigorously until it reaches the roots of her hair. Then she pours water over herself. Then she takes a piece of cloth (fir'sa) and purifies herself with it.' The fir'sa, with a kasra, is a piece of wool or cotton or other material, which she uses to follow the trace of the blood."

Then Allah, Exalted is He, made known that purification is a condition for the permissibility of approaching them, which is not valid without it, by His words, glorified is He: ﴿When they have purified themselves, go to them as Allah has commanded you﴾. That is: have intercourse with them from the place that Allah commanded you to avoid during menstruation, which is the front passage, and do not go beyond it to anything else. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾ from sins; ﴿and loves those who purify themselves﴾, that is, those who keep themselves far from indecencies and filth, such as having intercourse with a menstruating woman and approaching the place that is forbidden. In the mention of repentance there is an indication of the pressing need for it, given that some people commit what they have been forbidden. The repetition of the verb is for greater emphasis on the matter of purification.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 223 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[223] ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish. And send ahead for yourselves, and fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers.﴾

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish.﴾ Al-Bukhari and Muslim related from Jabir, who said: "The Jews used to say: 'If a woman is approached from behind, in her vagina, and then conceives, her child will be squint-eyed (aḥwal).'" He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish.﴾

(p. 564) In Muslim, from al-Zuhri, there is the addition: "If he wishes, [she may be] prone (mujabbiyah), and if he wishes, not prone, except that this is in one opening (ṣimām wāḥid)."

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: This addition resembles being from the tafsir (explanatory interpretation) of al-Zuhri, since it is absent from the narrations of others among the companions of Ibn al-Munkadir, despite their number.

Al-mujabbiyah, like mulabbiyah, is the one lying face-down. The ṣimām wāḥid is the vagina (al-farj). As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿a tilth for you﴾: the tilth (ḥarth) is the casting of seed into the earth; this is its original sense. The statement is either by elision of a noun (i.e., "places of tilth"), or the verbal noun is used in the sense of the passive participle (i.e., "things tilled"). They were likened to this because of the resemblance between what is deposited in their wombs and seeds, in that each of them is the matter from which what results comes forth. And when He, exalted is He, expressed concerning them by "tilth," He expressed their intercourse by "coming to" (ityān), as preceded, so He said: ﴿so come to your tilth however you wish⁠﴾, meaning: approach them as you approach your fields which you wish to till, from whatever direction you wish, with no direction being prohibited to you over another. The meaning is: have intercourse with them from whatever direction you wish, and do not heed the words of the Jews. In singling out the tilth for mention there is a generalization to all the modes that lead to it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿It is a harm, so keep away from women﴾ [2:222] and ﴿from where Allah has commanded you﴾ [2:222] and ﴿so come to your tilth however you wish⁠﴾ are among the subtle allusions and the praiseworthy indirect expressions. These and their like in the speech of Allah are good manners, which the believers should learn, adopt, and strive to emulate in their dialogue and correspondence.

With regard to the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse, another narration has come, which Abu Dawud and al-Hakim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This clan of the Ansar, who were people of idolatry, were together with this clan of the Jews, who were people of the Book, and who considered that they had superiority over them in knowledge, so they [the Ansar] would follow much of their conduct. Among the practice of the People of the Book was that they did not approach women except in one manner, which is the most concealing for the woman. This clan of the Ansar had adopted that from their practice. And this clan of Quraysh (p. 565) would treat women in an objectionable manner, and would take pleasure from them facing forward, from behind, and lying on their backs. When the Emigrants came to Madinah, a man of them married a woman of the Ansar. He went to do that with her, and she rejected it and said: 'We were only approached in one manner, so do that, or else keep away from me,' until their affair spread. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish⁠﴾, meaning: facing forward, from behind, and lying on the back, meaning by that the place of the child."

Note:
What we have mentioned of these narrations is what the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) rely upon.

There are other narrations indicating that this verse was revealed as a concession (rukhṣah) for intercourse with women in their posteriors.

Al-Tahawi said: Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qasim, who said: "I did not encounter anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts that it is lawful"—meaning intercourse with a woman in her posterior—then he recited: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾, then said: "What is clearer than this?" This is the report of al-Tahawi, transmitted by Ibn Kathir.

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in his takhrij of the hadiths of al-Rafiʿi: Ibn al-Qasim said: "I did not encounter anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubts it, and the Medinans narrate concession in it from the Prophet (ﷺ)." He points by this to what was narrated from Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Saʿid.

As for the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, it has several chains. It was related from him by Nafiʿ, ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, Zayd ibn Aslam, Saʿid ibn Yasar, and others.

As for Nafiʿ, it is well known from him through very many chains, among them: the narration of Malik, Ayyub, ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmari, Ibn Abi Dhiʾb, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAwn, Hisham ibn Saʿd, ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, ʿAbd Allah ibn Nafiʿ, Aban ibn Salih, and Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Farwa.

Al-Daraqutni said, regarding the hadiths of Malik which he related outside the Muwatta: Abu Jaʿfar al-Aswani al-Maliki informed us in Egypt, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hammad informed us, Abu al-Harith Ahmad ibn Saʿid al-Fihri informed us, Abu Thabit (p. 566) Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed us: al-Darawardi related to us from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn Hafs, from Nafiʿ, who said: Ibn ʿUmar said to me: "Hold the mushaf for me, O Nafiʿ." So he recited until he came to this verse: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾. Then he said: "Do you know, O Nafiʿ, concerning whom this verse was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who had intercourse with his wife in her posterior. The people found that objectionable, so Allah revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾, the verse." Nafiʿ said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: "In her posterior, in her vagina?" He said: "No. Only in her posterior."

Abu Thabit said: al-Darawardi related this to me from Malik and Ibn Abi Dhiʾb, and in both of them, from Nafiʿ, the like of it.

In the tafsir of al-Baqarah in the Sahih of al-Bukhari: Ishaq related to us, al-Nadr related to us, Ibn ʿAwn related to us from Nafiʿ, who said: When Ibn ʿUmar recited the Qur'an he would not speak until he finished it. I took hold of him one day, and he recited Surah al-Baqarah until he reached a certain place, then said: "Do you know concerning what it was revealed?" I said: "No!" He said: "It was revealed concerning such and such." Then he went on.

And from ʿAbd al-Samad: my father—meaning ʿAbd al-Warith—related to me, Ayyub related to me from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾, he said: "He comes to her in..." He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid related it, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, thus it occurred in his version.

The first narration, in the tafsir of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, is like what was recited, but it specified the verse, which is: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾, and specified his saying "such and such." He said: "It was revealed concerning intercourse with women in their posteriors." Likewise al-Tabari related it through the chain of Ibn ʿUlayyah from Ibn ʿAwn. As for the narration of ʿAbd al-Samad, it is also in the tafsir of Ishaq from him, and he said in it: "He comes to her in the posterior."

As for the narration of Muhammad: al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat from ʿAli ibn Saʿid, from Abu Bakr al-Aʿyan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid, with the wording: "It was only revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾ as a concession for intercourse in the posterior." Al-Hakim related it in his Tarikh through the chain of ʿIsa ibn Mathrud from (p. 567) ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Qasim, and through the chain of Sahl ibn ʿAmmar from ʿAbd Allah ibn Nafiʿ. Al-Daraqutni related it in Gharaʾib Malik through the chain of Zakariyya al-Saji from Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Madani from Abu Musʿab. Al-Khatib related it in al-Ruwat from Malik through the chain of Ahmad ibn al-Hakam al-ʿAbdi. Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi related it in his tafsir, and al-Daraqutni also through the chain of Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Farawi. Abu Nuʿaym related it in Tarikh Asbahan through the chain of Muhammad ibn Sadaqa al-Fadaki, all of them from Malik. Al-Daraqutni said: "This is established from Malik."

As for Zayd ibn Aslam: al-Nasa'i and al-Tabari related through the chain of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from him, from Ibn ʿUmar: "A man came to his wife in her posterior during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he found from that a severe distress, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you⁠﴾, the verse." As for ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, al-Nasa'i related through the chain of Yazid ibn Ruman from him, that Ibn ʿUmar did not see any harm in it. This is a mawquf (companion's) report.

As for Saʿid ibn Yasar: al-Nasa'i, al-Tahawi, and al-Tabari related through the chain of ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Qasim who said: I said to Malik: "Among us in Egypt, al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrates from al-Harith ibn Yaʿqub, from Saʿid ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: 'We buy slave-girls and we make them lie (tuḥammiḍu)'—and the taḥmīḍ is intercourse in the posterior—so he said: 'Uff! Would a Muslim do this?'" Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik said to me: "I testify concerning Rabiʿah that he narrated to me from Saʿid ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn ʿUmar about it, and he said: 'There is no harm in it.'"

As for the hadith of Abu Saʿid: Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir, al-Tabari, and al-Tahawi related through several chains: from ʿAbd Allah ibn Nafiʿ, from Hisham ibn Saʿd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: that a man had intercourse with a woman in her posterior, so the people denounced that against him and said: "He has 'thafara' her!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish⁠﴾. Usamah ibn Ahmad al-Tujibi related it through the chain of Yahya ibn Ayyub from Hisham ibn Saʿd, and its wording is: "We used to come to women in their posteriors, and that is called ithfar, so Allah revealed the verse." He related it through the chain of Maʿn ibn ʿIsa from Hisham, without naming Abu Saʿid, who said: "There were men among the Ansar..."

(p. 568) This is so. Many reports have been transmitted prohibiting that, which the Hafiz Ibn Kathir in his tafsir and Ibn Hajar in his takhrij of the hadiths of al-Rafiʿi have quoted. All of them are defective (maʿlulah).

For this reason al-Bazzar said: "I know of no sound hadith in this chapter, neither in prohibition nor in permission, and everything that has been related in it from Khuzaymah ibn Thabit through a chain in it is not sound."

Likewise al-Hakim related from the Hafiz Abu ʿAli al-Nisaburi, and the like from al-Nasa'i, and al-Bukhari said it before them both.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam related from al-Shafiʿi that he said: "Nothing has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) either in its prohibition or in its permission. Analogy (qiyas) indicates that it is lawful."

Ahmad ibn Usamah al-Tujibi related through the chain of Maʿn ibn ʿIsa, who said: "I asked Malik about it, and he said: 'I know of no prohibition concerning it.'"

Ibn Rushd said in al-Bayan wa al-Tahsil fi Sharh al-ʿUtbiyyah: al-ʿUtbi related from Ibn al-Qasim from Malik that he said to him—when he asked him about it in private—"It is lawful, there is no harm in it."

Al-Hakim related from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam, who said: al-Shafiʿi said a statement which Muhammad ibn al-Hasan had discussed regarding the matter of intercourse with a woman in her posterior. He said: "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan asked me, and I said to him: 'If you want obstinacy and to authenticate narrations, even if they are not authentic, then you know best. But if you speak with impartiality, I will discuss with you.'" He said: "On impartiality." I said: "On what basis do you prohibit it?" He said: "By the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿So come to them from where Allah has commanded you⁠﴾ [2:222], and He said: ﴿so come to your tilth however you wish⁠﴾, and the tilth is only in the vagina." I said: "Does it then make unlawful anything other than that?" He said: "Yes." I said: "What do you say if he had intercourse with her between her thighs, or in her folds, or under her armpit, or if she took his penis in her hand? Is that a tilth...?" He said: "No!" (p. 569) I said: "Then is that prohibited?" He said: "No!" I said: "Then why do you argue with what has no proof in it?" He said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts⁠﴾ [23:5], the verse."

He said: I said to him: "Indeed, this is among the things they cite as evidence for permissibility, that God praised those who guard their private parts from anyone other than their wives and what their right hands possess." I said: "You guard yourself from his wife and what his right hand possesses."

Al-Hakim said: "Perhaps al-Shafi'i used to say this in his Old (al-Qadim) opinion. As for his New (al-Jadid) opinion, the well-known view is that he prohibited it. Al-Asamm narrated from al-Rabi', who said: al-Shafi'i said: 'He explicitly stated its prohibition in six of his books...'" And al-Hakim related from al-Asamm, from al-Rabi', who said: al-Shafi'i said: God said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth as you wish﴾. The verse admits two meanings. One: that the woman may be approached from wherever the husband wishes, since ﴿as you wish﴾ (anna shi'tum) comes in the sense of "where you wish." Two: that "tilth" refers only to the place where crops grow, and not to anything else. Our companions (ashab) differed over this. I think each of the two groups interpreted the possibility of the verse that I have described.

He said: "So we sought evidence from the Sunnah, and we found two conflicting hadiths. One of them is authentic: the hadith of Khuzaymah concerning prohibition." He said: "So we adopted it." 

Accordingly, al-Shafi'i would have retracted his Old opinion. The hadith of Khuzaymah was narrated by al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and Abu Nu'aym, through a chain going back to Khuzaymah ibn Thabit: "A man asked the Prophet ﷺ about having intercourse with women in their anuses, and he said: 'It is permitted.' When the man turned to leave, he called him back, or commanded that he be called back, and said: 'How did you put it? In which of the two holes? If it is from her posterior into her front, then yes; or from her posterior into her posterior, then no. Indeed God does not shy away from the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses.'"

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Talkhis al-Habir": In its chain is 'Amr ibn Uhayhah, whose state is unknown (majhul al-hal), and its chain has been disputed in many ways. Then al-Hafiz said: al-Shafi'i said: "Ibn 'Uyaynah erred in the chain of the hadith of Khuzaymah," meaning in how he narrated it. The statement of al-Bazzar has preceded: "Every report from Khuzaymah ibn Thabit through a route containing this is not authentic."

Al-Razi said in his Tafsir: Most scholars hold that the meaning of the verse is that a man is free to approach her from her front into her front, or to approach her from her back into her front. So God's words ﴿so go to your tilth as you wish﴾ are understood in this sense. Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar that he used to say: the meaning of the verse is the permissibility of approaching women in their anuses. This is the view of Malik, and it is the choice of al-Sayyid al-Murtada from the Shi'a. Al-Murtada related it from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, may God be pleased with him.

In sum, this is one of the battlefields of men and the arena of heroes. From what we have set forth, it is clear that whoever permits this holds to the wording of the verse, for God made "tilth" a term for the woman.

Some exegetes said: The Arabs call women "tilth." A poet said:
"When locusts eat the crops of a people, my tilth is the concern of the locusts' eating,"
meaning: my wife. Another said:
"Indeed the wombs are land, and we have cultivators (muhtaritat) [of them],
so we planted the seed in them, and upon God is the growth."

In that case, God's words ﴿so go to your tilth as you wish﴾ are general in permitting approach to them in all manners, and the point of dispute falls within it. The hadith of Ibn 'Umar, which al-Bukhari narrated, as mentioned earlier, is also relied upon as the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul). He also cited the narration of Jabir in the Sahih that was mentioned earlier, that the generality of a text revealed on a specific occasion (al-'amm 'ala sabab) does not restrict it to that occasion. He answered the suspicion of Ibn 'Abbas toward Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, as narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud, by saying that its chain does not meet al-Bukhari's conditions and therefore does not conflict with it, so the more authentic chain is given precedence. He considered that nothing authentic had been transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ on this subject.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "Fath al-Bari": A group of leading hadith scholars, such as al-Bukhari, al-Dhuhli, al-Bazzar, al-Nasa'i and Abu 'Ali al-Nisaburi, held that nothing authentic is established on this matter.

As for those who prohibit it, they interpreted the preceding verses as referring to a single restriction (simam wahid). They considered that the hadiths narrated through multiple routes that warn against engaging in it, even though they do not meet the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) for authenticity, nevertheless together are suitable to be used as evidence.

The hadith scholar al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi surveyed the hadiths related to this matter in a juz' (fascicle) he compiled on it. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir cited a number of them in his Tafsir, as did the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim in "Zad al-Ma'ad." He exaggerated greatly concerning this matter, may God have mercy on him. He said in that book, in discussing the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ regarding intercourse, the following text:

"As for the anus, it has never been permitted by the tongue of any of the prophets. Whoever attributes to some of the early generations (salaf) the permissibility of intercourse with a wife through her anus has made an error about them." Then he cited the reports forbidding it, and then said: "The verse indicates the prohibition of intercourse in her anus from two angles. One: that God only permitted approaching her in the tilth, which is the place of offspring, and not in the latrine (hashsh), which is the place of filth. The place of tilth is what is meant by His words: ﴿from where God has commanded you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222], and then ﴿so go to your tilth as you wish﴾. Approaching her from her posterior into her front is also derived from the verse, because He said ﴿as you wish﴾, that is, from wherever you wish: from in front or from behind. Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿so go to your tilth﴾ means the vagina (al-farj). If God prohibited intercourse in the vagina because of an incidental harm, what then is to be thought of the latrine, which is the place of inevitable harm, together with the added corruption of cutting off offspring and the close means (dhari'ah) from women's anuses to boys' anuses?

"Also, a woman has a right over her husband in intercourse, and intercourse in her anus defeats that right, does not satisfy her desire, and does not attain her intended purpose. Also, the anus was not prepared or created for this act; what was prepared for it is the vagina. Those who turn away from it to the anus have departed from God's wisdom and His law entirely. Also, this is harmful to the man, and for this reason wise physicians among the philosophers and others forbid it, because the vagina has a special property of drawing in retained semen and relieving the man of it, whereas intercourse in the anus does not help draw out all the retained semen, nor does all of it come out, since it opposes the natural order... Also, it harms in another respect: it compels him to very exhausting movements because it opposes nature. Also, it is a place of filth and excrement, so the man faces it with his face and is in contact with it. Also, it harms the woman greatly, for it is a strange and distant act, far from natural dispositions, and utterly repugnant to her. Also, it produces grief, anguish and aversion in both the doer and the one acted upon. Also, it blackens the face, darkens the chest, extinguishes the light of the heart, and covers the face with a desolation that becomes like a mark, which anyone with the least perception can recognize. Also, it necessarily produces aversion, intense hatred, and severance between the doer and the one acted upon. Also, it corrupts the condition of the doer and the one acted upon with a corruption from which goodness is hardly hoped for afterward, unless God wills through sincere repentance. Also, it takes away the good qualities of both and clothes them in their opposites, just as it removes the affection between them and replaces it with hatred and mutual cursing. Also, it is among the greatest causes of the loss of blessings and the descent of punishments, for it necessitates God's curse and wrath, and His turning away from its doer and not looking at him. So what good can one hope for after this? And what evil can one feel safe from? And how can the life of a servant be lived when God's curse and wrath have descended upon him, and He has turned His face away from him and does not look upon him?"

I say: Ibn al-Qayyim derived this from hadiths that came concerning the cursing of the one who does this and God's not looking at him, but they are weak.

Then Ibn al-Qayyim said: "Also, it entirely removes modesty (haya'), and modesty is the life of the hearts. When the heart lacks it, it considers the ugly to be good and the good to be ugly, and at that point its corruption is firmly established. Also, it turns natural dispositions away from what God has fashioned them to be, and takes a person out of his nature into a nature on which God has fashioned nothing of the animals; rather it is an inverted nature. When nature is inverted, the heart, the action and the guidance are inverted as well, so the person then finds pleasant the wicked among deeds, actions and states, and his condition, works and speech are corrupted without his choice. Also, it generates a shamelessness and boldness that nothing else generates. Also, it generates a baseness, lowliness and meanness that nothing else generates. Also, it clothes the servant in the garment of hatred and enmity, and of people's contempt for him, their disdain for him, and their belittling of him, which is witnessed by the senses. So may God's blessings and peace be upon the one in whose guidance and following of what he brought lies the happiness of this world and the next, and in opposition to whose guidance and what he brought lies the ruin of this world and the next." End of quotation.

Since this verse included permission for the fulfilment of desire, He drew attention to the fact that a person should not remain in the bonds of desire, but rather in the bonds of obedience. So He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And send forward for yourselves﴾, that is, what must be sent forward of righteous deeds, so that you may attain by it Paradise and honour, like His words: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾ [al-Baqarah: 197]. ﴿And fear God﴾, lest you be emboldened toward sins. ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, that is, that you will return to Him, so prepare yourselves for meeting Him. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ of reward. It was omitted because it is as if known, and so it is like His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from God a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47].

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[224] ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths, [preventing you] from being righteous and pious and reconciling between people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths, [preventing you] from being righteous and pious and reconciling between people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ Al-'Urdah (the obstacle), with a damma on the ʿayn, is on the pattern fu'lah in the sense of maf'ul, like al-qubdah (a handful) and al-ghurfah (a scoop). It is the name of what one places in front of a thing, from ʿarḍ al-ʿūd ʿala al-inā' (laying a stick across a vessel). Thus it stands in the way of the thing and becomes a barrier and a hindrance to it. One says: "So-and-so is an obstacle before good." A man would swear an oath concerning some good deed, such as maintaining family ties, reconciling between people, or doing a kindness to someone, and then say: "I fear Allah that I might break my oath." So he would leave the righteous act, intending to keep his oath. It was said to them: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾, meaning: a barrier against what you have sworn to do. The object of the oath is called "oath" because it is bound up with the oath, as in the hadith: "Whoever swears an oath concerning..." which will be mentioned later, meaning: concerning something of what he swears to. His words ﴿[preventing you] from being righteous and pious﴾ are an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to ﴿your oaths﴾ [al-Baqarah: 225], meaning: the matters sworn to, which are righteousness, piety and reconciling between people. This was stated by al-Zamakhshari.

According to this interpretation, the verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾ [al-Nur: 22]. The meaning mentioned above was agreed upon by the majority of the early scholars (salaf). ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Do not let Allah become an obstacle for your oath, that you do not do good; rather, expiate your oath and do good."

It is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, if Allah wills, I do not swear an oath and then see something other than it to be better, except that I do what is better and make expiation for my oath."

Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, let him expiate his oath and do what is better."

There is another aspect to the verse, mentioned by many exegetes: it is a prohibition against audacity toward Allah, Exalted is He, through excessive swearing by Him. This is because whoever mentions something frequently in any sense has made it an obstacle for it. A man says: "You have made me an obstacle for your blame." And the poet said:

*"And do not make me an obstacle for the blamers."*

Allah, Exalted is He, has censured the one who swears excessively, saying: ﴿And do not obey every contemptible swearer﴾ [al-Qalam: 10]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And guard your oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89]. The Arabs used to praise a man for swearing little, as Kuthayyir said:

*"Few in oaths, guarding his oath, and if an oath slips from him, he is pious (barra)."*

The wisdom in the command to reduce oaths is this: whoever swears by Allah concerning every small and large matter, his tongue becomes accustomed to it, and the oath no longer carries weight in his heart. Thus his boldness toward a false oath cannot be trusted, and the primary purpose of the oath is undermined. Also, the more a person magnifies Allah, Exalted is He, the more perfect he is in servanthood. Part of the perfection of magnification is that the mention of Allah, Exalted is He, be greater and higher in his sight than to call Him as witness for some worldly purpose. As for His saying, Exalted is He, after that: ﴿[preventing you] from being righteous and pious﴾, it is the cause (ʿillah) of the prohibition, meaning: lest you be prevented from being righteous, pious and reconciling, because the one who swears frequently is bold toward Allah and does not magnify Him; so he is not righteous or pious, and people do not trust him, so they do not admit him into their mediation and reconciliation between them. And Allah knows best.

(p-٥٧٧)The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[225] ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the idle (*laghw*) oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned. Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.﴾

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾, meaning: He will not punish you or obligate you for the oaths that come from you which are idle (*laghiyah*), when you did not intend to violate their sanctity. These are the oaths that the one swearing does not intend, but which pass over his tongue out of habit, without deliberate binding or intention to them. As His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿but He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have deliberately bound﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:89). This is what is meant by His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, meaning: what your hearts intended, so that the intention combined with the utterance. That is, the heart is bound to it, by neglecting the honouring of its matter and violating its sanctity through breaking a deliberate oath.

It was narrated from Aisha that she said: "This verse was revealed concerning a man's saying: 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!'" Narrated by al-Bukhari, Malik and Abu Dawud, and this is the wording of al-Bukhari.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted something similar from Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas and others among the Companions and the Successors. The wording of the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim from Aisha is: "The idle oath is only in jesting and levity, and it is the saying of a man: 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!' There is no expiation for that. The expiation is only for what the heart has bound itself to: that one does a thing and then does not do it."

(p-٥٧٨)It is also related in the explanation of idle oaths that it is when one swears about something he thinks to be true, and then the opposite becomes apparent. It is also related: that one swears while angry. Other interpretations have been related as well, as Ibn Kathir cited them with their chains of transmission.

It has become clear to the humble servant (al-faqir) that there is no contradiction between these narrations, because every oath with which the heart does not bind itself is idle (*laghw*), in whatever form it occurs and in whatever state it happens. So everything that has been related in the interpretation of the verse falls within what the idle oath includes. And Allah knows best.

The intended meaning of "holding accountable" (*mu'akhadhah*) is the imposition of expiation (*kaffarah*), as this was explained in the verse of al-Ma'idah: ﴿but He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have deliberately bound, so its expiation is...﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:89). ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾, meaning: to His servants regarding what they uttered as idle oaths, so He did not hold them accountable for it. ﴿Forbearing﴾, meaning: in not hastening the punishment of the people of disobedience, awaiting their repentance. This sentence is a concluding remark (*tadhyil*) for the two preceding rulings. Its benefit is the bestowal of favour upon the believers, and the comprehensiveness of His forgiveness and His kindness towards them.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[226–227] ﴿For those who take an oath to abstain from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they go back, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227].

﴿For those who take an oath to abstain from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they go back, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227] This verse contains the ruling on *ila'* (a vow of abstention from marital relations). Linguistically, *ila'* means refraining by means of an oath. In the usage of the Sharia, it is specialized to refraining from sexual intercourse with one's wife by means of an oath. For this reason the verb is followed by the particle *min* (from), with the sense of implication (*tadmin*): "they refrain from their wives." This is better than placing *min* in the position of *'ala* (upon). Glorified is He, Who gave husbands a period of four months during which they refrain from their wives through *ila'*. When it has elapsed, they either return (*fa'a*) or divorce.

(p-579) It is well known from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that *ila'* only occurs in a state of anger and not of contentment, as happened to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his wives. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an agrees with the majority. Muhammad ibn Sirin debated this question with another man. The man argued against Muhammad with the statement of 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, and Muhammad countered him with the verse, and he fell silent. The scholars (*a'imma*) agree that if the one who took the oath returns to continuing the marital relationship, he is obligated to pay the expiation of an oath (*kaffarat yamin*). It was omitted here only because it is known from another place in the Mighty Revelation. Thus the general obligation of expiation is established for the one who swears.

The scholar Siddiq Khan said in his *Tafsir*: Know that the people of every school have interpreted this verse in a way that accords with their school, and have strained themselves with meanings that the wording does not indicate and for which there is no other evidence. Its meaning is clear and evident, namely that Allah set the term for one who makes *ila'*, that is, who swears against his wife, as four months. Then He said, informing His servants of the ruling for this one who makes *ila'* after this period: ﴿If they go back﴾, that is, they return to the continuation of the marriage and the perpetuation of the wedlock; ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, He does not hold them accountable for that oath, but forgives them and shows them mercy; ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227], that is, the resolve and intention to it has arisen in them; ﴿then indeed Allah is Hearing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227] of that from them; ﴿Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227] of it. This is the meaning of the verse, about which there is no doubt or ambiguity. Whoever swears that he will not have intercourse with his wife, without specifying a term or specifying a term exceeding four months, it is incumbent upon us to give him four months' respite. When it has elapsed, he has the choice: either he returns to the marriage with his wife, and she is his wife after the period has passed just as she was his wife before it, or he divorces her, and he has the status of one who divorces his wife from the outset. But if he specified a term of less than four months, then if he wishes to (p-580) fulfil his oath, he withdraws from the wife concerning whom he swore until the term expires, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did when he made *ila'* against his wives for a month; he withdrew from them until the month had passed. If he intends to have intercourse with his wife before the passing of that term, which is less than four months, he breaks his oath and the expiation becomes obligatory upon him, and he is acting in compliance with what is authentically reported from him ﷺ: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else to be better than it, let him do what is better and let him make expiation for his oath."

Al-Harali said: In His words, exalted is He, ﴿then indeed Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 227], there is a warning concerning what occurs within souls and inner selves of harm and irritation between spouses in matters that the rulings do not grasp and that the judges cannot possibly come to know. Thus He made them trustees over themselves in what is hidden and what is manifest. For this reason the scholars held that divorce is a trust in the hands of men, just as the waiting period (*'idda*) and the purification period (*istibra'*) are a trust in the hands of women. Therefore the verse about the woman's waiting during her *'idda* is joined with the verse about the husband's waiting during his *ila'*.

The Imam Ibn Kathir said: The jurists and others have mentioned, regarding the reason for the four-month deferment for one who makes *ila'*, the report that Malik transmitted from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, who said: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab went out at night and heard a woman saying:

*The night has stretched on and its side has darkened,*
*and it keeps me awake, except for a friend I play with.*

*By Allah! Were it not for Allah, of whom I am mindful,*
*the sides of this couch would be shaken."*

So 'Umar asked his daughter Hafsa, may Allah be pleased with them both: "What is the longest a woman can endure away from her husband?" She said: "Six months, or four months." 'Umar said: "I will not hold back any of the soldiers for longer than that."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Sa'ib ibn Jubayr, the client of Ibn 'Abbas, who had met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "I kept hearing the report that 'Umar went out one night patrolling Medina, as he did often, when he passed by a woman from among the women of the Arabs, who had closed her door, saying:

*The night has stretched on and its side has grown dark,*
*and it keeps me awake, except for a companion I play with.*

*I play with him at times, and at times it is as if*
*a moon has appeared in the darkness of the night, its crescent.*

*He delights whoever plays with him in his nearness,*
*slender of waist, whom his relatives cannot contain.*

*By Allah! Were it not for Allah, there is nothing else,*
*the sides of this couch would be broken down.*

*But I fear a watchful guardian over our breaths,*
*whose scribe never tires, for all time.*

*Out of fear of my Lord, and shame holds me back,*
*and honouring my husband, from being reached by his mounts."*

Then he mentioned the rest of that, as was previously mentioned or similar to it. This has been related through several chains, and it is among the well-known reports.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[228] ﴿Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual cycles. It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation. And they [women] have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is reasonable. And the men have a degree over them. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾.

"﴿Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three [cycles]﴾": This is a command to divorced women to wait by themselves for three cycles, meaning that each of them remains after her husband divorces her for three cycles, and then she may marry if she wishes. By "divorced women" is meant those who have been consummated with and who have menstrual cycles, because the verses and reports indicate that the ruling for others is different from what is mentioned. As for the woman who has not been consummated, there is no waiting period (ʿiddah) for her, based on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period for them to count﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49]. As for the one who has not menstruated, her waiting period is three months, based on His saying: (p-582) ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and [likewise for] those who have not menstruated﴾ [al-Talaq: 4]. As for the pregnant woman, her waiting period is the delivery of the child, based on His saying: ﴿And for those with children, their term is that they deliver their burden﴾ [al-Talaq: 4].

Thus this verse is one of the general (ʿamm) rulings that has been specified (makhsus).

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, "What is the meaning of reporting about them as waiting?" I say: It is a statement in the sense of a command. The original wording is "let the divorced women wait," and expressing the command in the form of a statement is an emphasis of the command and an indication that it is something that must be received with haste in carrying it out. It is as if they had already complied with the command to wait, so He reports it as existing. A similar example is their saying in supplication, "May Allah have mercy on you," which is phrased as a statement out of confidence in being answered, as if mercy had already occurred, so He reports it. Building it on the subject (mubtada') also adds further emphasis. If it had been said, "and the divorced women wait," it would not have had that same force. If you ask, "Why not say 'they wait three cycles,' as it was said 'waiting four months,' and what is the meaning of mentioning the selves?" I say: Mentioning the selves stirs them to waiting and increases the impulse, because in it there is something they would find repugnant, which drives them to wait. That is because women's selves are inclined toward men, so they are commanded to restrain their selves, to subdue them from desire, and to compel them to wait.

And (al-qurʾ) [the word for "cycle"] is one of the words with opposite meanings (addad). It is applied to menstruation (ḥayḍ) and purity (ṭuhr). This is stated by leading philologists: Abu ʿUbaydah, al-Zajjaj, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, and others. The discussion of preferring one of them is lengthy, and the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim thoroughly covered it in "Zad al-Maʿad," so refer to it. For one who considers its lexical meaning, he may say: The waiting period ends after three periods of purity or three menstrual periods. Whichever of the two the woman who is observing the waiting period takes into account, she has discharged the obligation. And Allah knows best.

﴿And it is not lawful for them﴾, that is, the divorced women: ﴿to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾ (p-583) of menstruation or of a child, hastening the waiting period or nullifying the husband's right of return: ﴿if they believe in Allah﴾, that is, if they conduct themselves according to the requirement of belief in Him, the One whose majesty is feared: ﴿and the Last Day﴾, whose recompense is feared. This indicates that the determination in this matter rests with them, because it is a matter that cannot be known except from their side, and establishing evidence for it is impossible. So the matter is entrusted to them, and they are warned concerning it so that they do not report other than the truth. This verse indicates that whoever is made trustworthy in something and betrays it, his affair before Allah is grave.

﴿And their husbands﴾, that is, their spouses: ﴿have more right to take them back﴾, that is, to return them to marriage. The discussion concerns revocable divorce, as indicated by the following verse: ﴿in that [period]﴾, that is, during the time of waiting, which is the days of the cycles. As for when the waiting period has ended, she has more right over herself, and she is not lawful to him except by a new marriage contract with a guardian, witnesses, and a new dowry. There is no disagreement on this. ﴿If they desire﴾, that is, by return: ﴿reconciliation﴾ between them and themselves, and kindness toward them, and they do not intend to harm them. Otherwise, return is forbidden, based on His saying: ﴿And do not retain them to harm them, that you may transgress﴾ [al-Baqarah: 231].

﴿And they [women] have rights similar to those upon them according to what is reasonable﴾, that is, and they have over the men [rights] similar to what the men have over them. So each of them must fulfill to the other what is obligatory upon him according to what is reasonable. As established in "Sahih Muslim," from Jabir: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon at the Farewell Pilgrimage: 'Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful through the word of Allah. And it is yours that they should not allow anyone you dislike to tread upon your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a light strike that does not leave a mark. And for them is their provision and their clothing according to what is reasonable.'"

(p-584) And from Muʿawiyah ibn Haydah, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of one's wife over him?' He said: 'That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house.'" Narrated by Abu Dawud, who said: The meaning of "do not revile" is: do not say, "May Allah disfigure you."

And from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is not lawful for a woman to fast while her husband is present except with his permission, nor to permit anyone into his house except with his permission." Agreed upon.

And from Ibn ʿUmar: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler is a shepherd, and the man is a shepherd over his household, and the woman is a shepherd over her husband's house and his children. So each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock." Agreed upon.

And from Talq ibn ʿAli: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man calls his wife for his need, let her come to him, even if she is at the oven." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i.

(p-585) And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man calls his wife to his bed and she does not come to him, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning." Agreed upon.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "I love to adorn myself for the woman as I love her to adorn herself for me, because Allah says: ﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them according to what is reasonable﴾."

Note:

Ma'ruf (what is reasonable) is that which sound natures recognize and do not reject, which the intellect accepts, which agrees with nobility of soul, and which the Law affirms. Some jurists have said: It is not obligatory for her to serve her husband in kneading, baking, cooking, and the like, because what is contracted for is the benefit of intercourse, so he owns no other of her benefits..! But the implication of the verse refutes this and indicates the obligation of what is reasonable from a woman of her kind toward a man of his kind. Imam Ibn Taymiyyah issued a legal opinion accordingly, in agreement with the Malikis. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Ishaq al-Juzjani also held this view, and they relied on what was reported: "That the Prophet ﷺ decided that his daughter Fatimah should serve in the house and do what work was outside the house." Narrated by al-Juzjani through several chains.

The verse has also been cited as evidence for the obligation of providing her with a servant, if a woman of her station does not serve herself.

﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, that is, an increase in right and a superiority, as He said: ﴿Men are in charge of women by what Allah has given some of them over others, and by what they spend of their wealth﴾ [al-Nisa': 34].

(p-586) And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "If I were to command anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: A hasan sahih hadith. ﴿And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, that is, Dominant in His retribution against whoever disobeys Him, and Wise in His command and His law.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[229] ﴿The divorce is twice; then either keep (her) in an acceptable manner or release (her) with kindness. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up to be released. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah – it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿The divorce is twice⦆ "Divorce" (al-talaq) here means the act of divorcing (al-taṭlīq), just as "peace" (al-salam) means the act of greeting (al-taslīm). It is a subject (mubtada') with an elided modifier, whose predicate is what follows. That is: the number of divorces in which the husband is entitled to return (al-radd) and reconciliation (al-raj'a) is twice, i.e., two. The choice of the wording revealed in this noble verse is to indicate that their proper occurrence is one after another, not all at once, although the ruling of return is established then too.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse abrogates what was the situation at the beginning of Islam: that a man had the greater right to take back his wife even if he had divorced her a hundred times, as long as she was in the waiting period (al-'idda). Since this was harmful to wives, Allah the Exalted limited them to three divorces, permitted return at the second, and made separation complete at the third. So He said: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾, and so on.

(p-587) Imam Abu Dawud said in his "Sunan": Chapter on the abrogation of reconciliation after the three divorces. Then he traced, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse, that he said: A man, when he divorced his wife, had the greater right to her return, even if he had divorced her three times. That was abrogated, and He said: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾, and so on. It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i and others. al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'A'isha, she said: "People, and a man would divorce his wife as often as he wished, and she would still be his wife if he took her back while she was in the waiting period, even if he had divorced her a hundred times or more, until a man said to his wife: 'By Allah, I will not divorce you so that you become separated from me, nor will I shelter you ever again!' She said: 'How so?' He said: 'I will divorce you, and whenever your waiting period is about to end, I will take you back.' So the woman went and entered upon 'A'isha and informed her, and 'A'isha remained silent until the Prophet (ﷺ) came, and she informed him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent until the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾, and so on." 'A'isha said: "So the people began divorce anew, as a fresh start, for whoever had divorced and whoever had not divorced." Then he traced it from 'Urwa without mentioning 'A'isha, and said: This is more authentic.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿then either keep (her) in an acceptable manner or release (her) with kindness⦆ That is: the ruling, after a man divorces his wife with two divorces, is that he either keeps her in an acceptable manner, treating her companionship well; or releases her with kindness, not wronging her in any of her rights, not mentioning her after separation with evil, and not turning people away from her.

Al-Razi said: The wisdom in establishing the right of return is that as long as a person remains with his companion, he does not know whether separation from her will be hard upon him or not. When he separates from her, then it becomes clear. Had Allah made a single divorce a barrier to return, the hardship upon the person would have been great, given that love might appear after separation. Then, since complete trial cannot be attained with a single time, Allah the Exalted therefore established the right of reconciliation after separation twice. At that point the person has tested himself in that separation and known the state of his heart in that matter. (p-588) If keeping her is better, he returns to her and keeps her in kindness. And if releasing her is better for him, he releases her in the best manner. This gradation and ordering indicates the perfection of His mercy and compassion toward His servant.

﴿And it is not lawful for you⦆ – that is, O divorcers: ﴿to take anything of what you have given them⦆ – of the dower or otherwise –: ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah⦆ That is, regarding what is incumbent upon her of the rights of marriage –: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up to be released⦆ That is, she ransoms herself from his harm; that is, there is no sin upon the husband in taking what she has offered, nor upon her in giving it. This verse is the foundation of khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation).

Ibn Jarir mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays, whose wife could not bear him out of hatred. In the "Sahih of al-Bukhari" from Ibn 'Abbas: "The wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah! I do not blame him regarding character or religion, but I dislike disbelief in Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Will you return to him his garden?' She said: Yes! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Accept the garden and divorce her with one divorce.'" The Imam Ibn Kathir in his "Tafsir" has expounded the chains of this hadith together with the rulings of khul', and likewise Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim in "Zad al-Ma'ad"; so consult it there.

﴿These⦆ – that is, the great rulings previously mentioned concerning divorce, return, khul' and others… –: ﴿are the limits of Allah⦆ – His legislations –: ﴿so do not transgress them⦆ – by violation and rejection –: ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah – it is those who are the wrongdoers⦆ That is, wronging themselves by exposing themselves to the wrath of Allah the Exalted and His punishment. The following of the prohibition with the threat is for emphasis in warning.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 230 (part 1 of 3):

(p-589) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:
[230] ﴿And if he divorces her [a third time], then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband. And if he [the second husband] divorces her, there is no blame upon the two of them for returning to each other if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah. These are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.﴾

﴿And if he divorces her﴾ - i.e., after the two pronouncements of divorce - ﴿then she is not lawful to him﴾ - neither by reconciliation nor by a new marriage - ﴿after that﴾ - i.e., after this divorce - ﴿until she marries another husband﴾, i.e., until she tastes the intercourse of another husband, and this is the "'usaylah" (the sweetness of intimacy) which the Prophet (ﷺ) stated in a valid marriage. In making this a condition for lawfulness there is a deterrent for one who has a desire to divorce his wife three times, because every person of honour dislikes that another man should lie with his wife.

Important branches related to this verse:

The first: The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in "Zad al-Ma'ad": The ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning a woman divorced three times is that she is not lawful to the first husband until the second husband has intercourse with her.
