If someone owed a debt to a person and transferred it through his slave or servant, whose provision he is responsible for, the belief of the one paying the debt that the one receiving it is under his obligation would be foolishness and ignorance, for the one who does good to him is the one responsible for his provision. As for him, he is only settling what was binding upon him by buying what he loves, so he is striving for his own self, and so he has not conferred a favour on another. Whenever he knows the three meanings we mentioned before, or one of them, he does not see himself as doing good except to himself, either by giving his wealth to show love for God, or to purify his self from the vice of miserliness, or as thanks for the blessing of wealth, seeking more. However it is, there is no transaction between him and the poor man so that he sees himself as doing good to him. Whenever this ignorance occurs, so that he sees himself as doing good to him, there branches from it, outwardly, what was mentioned regarding the meaning of reproach, which is speaking of it, making it public, and seeking reward from the recipient [p. 698] by thanks and supplication, service, honour and reverence, fulfilling rights, precedence in gatherings, and following him in affairs. All of these are fruits of reproach. The meaning of reproach inwardly is what we have described. As for harm, its outward form is rebuke, reproach, harsh speech, frowning, exposing the veil by public disclosure, and various kinds of belittling. Its inward source has two matters: the first is his dislike of removing his hand from the wealth and the severity of that upon his self, for that inevitably constricts the character. The second is his seeing himself as better than the poor man, and that the poor man, because of his need, is baser than him. Both of these stem from ignorance. As for his dislike of handing over wealth, this is foolishness, for whoever dislikes giving a dirham in exchange for something worth a thousand is extremely foolish. It is well known that he gives wealth seeking the pleasure of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the reward in the Hereafter, and that is more noble than what he has given or gives to purify his self from the vice of miserliness, or to give thanks in seeking more. However it is supposed, the dislike has no basis. As for the second, it is also ignorance, for if he knew the excellence of poverty over wealth and knew the danger of the rich, he would not belittle the poor man, but rather would seek blessing through him and wish for his rank. The righteous rich enter Paradise five hundred years after the poor.

Al-Ghazali, may God have mercy on him, has extended this lofty discussion. So let it be consulted.

Section

On his guidance ﷺ regarding zakat and charity

Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim al-Dimashqi said in *Zad al-Ma'ad* (*Provision for the Hereafter*): His guidance ﷺ regarding zakat is the most perfect guidance in its timing, its measure, its nisab, those upon whom it is obligatory, and its recipients. Consideration is given to it for the interest of the owners of wealth and the interest of the needy. God, Glorified and Exalted, made it a purification for the wealth and for its owner, and He restricted the blessing in wealth for the rich by it. It has never removed the blessing from wealth of one who pays its zakat, rather it preserves it for him, increases it for him, repels calamities from him through it, and makes it a wall around him, a fortress for him, and a guard for him.

[p. 699] Then he said, regarding his guidance ﷺ in voluntary charity: He ﷺ was the greatest of people in charity from what his hand possessed. He never considered anything he gave for God as much, nor did he consider it little, and no one asked him for anything he had without his giving it, whether little or much. His giving was the giving of one who does not fear poverty. Giving and charity were the most beloved things to him. His joy and happiness in what he gave was greater than the joy of the recipient in what he received. He was the most generous of people with good; his hand was like a sent wind. Whenever a needy person came to him, he preferred him over himself, sometimes with his food and sometimes with his clothing. He varied the kinds of his giving and charity: sometimes by gift, sometimes by alms, sometimes by present, and sometimes by buying something, then he would give the seller the price and the goods together, as he did with Jabir. Sometimes he would borrow something and return more than it, better and greater. He would buy something and give more than its price. He would accept a present and reciprocate with more than it, or with multiples of it, showing kindness and variety in the forms of charity and goodness [p. 700] by every possible means. His charity and his goodness were with what he owned, with his state, and with his speech. He would bring out what he had, command charity, urge to it, and call to it, both by his state and his speech. When the miserly, stingy man saw him, his state called him to giving and bestowal. Whoever mixed with him, accompanied him, and saw his guidance could not restrain himself from generosity and bounty. His guidance ﷺ called to goodness, charity and kindness. For this reason he ﷺ was the most expansive of creatures in breast, the most pure of soul, and the most blessed of heart. Charity and the doing of good have a wondrous effect in expanding hearts. To this was added what God had specially granted him of expansion of his breast for prophethood and messengership, and their requirements and consequences, and the expansion of his breast physically, and the removal of the portion of Satan from it.

When the Exalted mentioned the righteous who spend their zakat and charities in all states and times, He proceeded to mention those who consume usury, the wealth of people by falsehood, and various kinds of doubtful dealings. He informed about their condition on the Day they rise from their graves, and their standing from them to their resurrection and gathering. He said:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[275] ﴿Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, "Trade is but like usury," while Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may keep what is past, and his affair is up to Allah. But whoever returns, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿Those who consume usury﴾: Riba is an excess of wealth, unmatched by any counter-value, in an exchange of wealth for wealth. Riba is written with a waw in the dialect of those who pronounce it with emphasis (tafkhim), just as al-salat and al-zakat are written, and an alif is added after it in imitation of the waw of the plural.

﴿will not stand﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection, as some of the Companions and the Successors (al-tabi'un) said.

﴿except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity﴾: In al-Qamus, "khabatahu" means he struck him severely, like "takhabbatahu" and "ikhtabatahu." In al-'Ubab: whoever strikes a person with his hand so that he falls down has "khabatahu" and "takhabbatahu" him. Its origin is touching (al-mass) with the hand, and then it was borrowed for madness, because Satan touches the person and drives him mad. The prepositional phrase may be connected either to "will not stand," meaning they will not stand up from the touch that is upon them except as the one struck down stands up from his madness; or to "stands," meaning as the one struck down stands up from his madness; or to "takhabbatahu," meaning from the direction of madness. The meaning is that they will rise on the Day of Resurrection deranged, like those struck down.

That is their mark by which they will be recognized at the place of standing, as a disgrace and an exposure for them.

Al-Harali said: In this unrestricted expression there is an indication of their state in this world, in the intermediate realm (al-barzakh), and in the Hereafter. Its announcement contains a notice that the one who consumes it will have his intellect taken away, and his remaining in this world will be with folly rather than with reason. He advances where he should retreat, and retreats where he should advance.

Al-Biqa'i said: This is confirmed by observation. We have never seen or heard of a consumer of riba who speaks with wisdom or is known for virtue. Rather, they are the lowest and most defiled of people.

Note:
Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: The "takhabbut" of Satan is among the fabrications (za'amat) of the Arabs. They claim that Satan strikes a person so that he falls down. "Al-mass" means madness, and a "mamsus" is one afflicted by it. This too is among their fabrications, that a jinn touches him so that his intellect is confused. Likewise, "junna al-rajul" means: the jinn struck him.

Al-Baydawi followed him in his statement: "That is: the takhabbut and the mass are in accordance with what they claim, etc."

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisar: The meaning of al-Zamakhshari's words, "from the fabrications of the Arabs," is their lies and embellishments that have no reality. This statement, taken literally, that Satan strikes with takhabbut, is from the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination), among their fabrications, which are rejected by the decisive texts of the Law. Then he cited what has been transmitted about this in hadiths and reports. He then said: The belief of the early generations (al-salaf) and of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) is that these are matters as they really are, occurring as the Law has reported about them. The Qadariyya are the opponents of what is manifest, and so they deny much of what they claim contradicts their principles. Among that is sorcery, Satan's striking, and most of the states of the jinn. Even if they acknowledge some of it, they do so in a manner other than that which the People of the Sunnah affirm and which the apparent sense of the Law indicates, in a long confusion of their own.

Shaykh Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani said in Sharh al-Maqasid: In sum, the affirmation of the existence of angels, jinn, and Satan is something on which the opinions of people have agreed, and which the Word of Allah and the words of the Prophets have affirmed.

He also said: The jinn are subtle, airy bodies that take on various forms, and strange states appear from them. The satans are fiery bodies whose nature is to cast people into corruption and error. Because air and fire are extremely subtle and penetrating, angels, jinn, and satans enter narrow openings, even into the inner bodies of humans, and they are not seen by ordinary sight unless they acquire something from mixed material forms.

Al-Biqa'i, after quoting what we have mentioned, said: Many hadiths have been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "Satan flows through a human being in the way the blood flows." It is also reported that he (ﷺ) expelled the jinn who was wrestling from the belly of the one afflicted, in the form of a dog, and similar things. In the earlier books of Allah, the Exalted, there are countless similar accounts. As for observing the one afflicted, who speaks of unseen matters while afflicted, who has lost sensation, and who is sometimes thrown into fire without being burned, or who sometimes rises into the air with no one lifting him, these are very many, and their witnesses cannot be counted. Besides these, there are other matters that make it certain that this is from the jinn or the satans. I will now mention to you from the hadiths of the Prophet (ﷺ) what is sufficient for whoever reflects upon it, and Allah is the Granter of success.

Al-Darimi narrated in the beginning of his Musnad, with a good chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a son of hers and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my son has madness, and it seizes him at our lunch and dinner, and he defiles us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wiped his chest and made supplication, and he vomited a vomiting, and something like a black pup came out of his chest and ran away.

(Thu'a'a: with a thaa' and a ha' [sic], meaning he vomited.)

Al-Darimi also, and 'Abd ibn Humayd with a good chain as well, narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey. We rode with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us as if birds were over our heads, shading us. A woman came to him with a child of hers and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! This son of mine is seized by Satan every day three times.' He took the boy and placed him between himself and the front of the saddle, then said: 'Begone, enemy of Allah! I am the Messenger of Allah,' three times, and then he gave him back to her."

Al-Tabarani narrated it through another route and clarified that the journey was the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa' and that this happened at Harrat Waqim. Jabir said: "When we had finished our journey and passed by that place, the woman came to us with her child, and with her were two rams which she was driving. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Accept my gift from me. By He who sent you with the truth, he has not returned to it since.' He said: 'Take one of them, and return the other to her.'"

It was also narrated by al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah from Ya'la ibn Murra, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then al-Biqa'i cited what came in the Gospel. He said: "And that is very much," meaning what occurred to the Messiah, peace be upon him, of driving out satans and evil spirits from those afflicted with that. After citing that, he said: "I have written this although what has been transmitted from our Prophet (ﷺ) is sufficient, because it cannot be denied that there is in it comfort for him and a confirmation that increases faith."

The Imam Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim has excelled in explaining the domination of evil spirits in Zad al-Ma'ad, and he mentioned the treatment for repelling them. He said, may God have mercy on him:

(p-704) Chapter:
On his guidance (ﷺ) in treating epilepsy (al-sar').

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported from the hadith of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas said to me: Shall I show you a woman of the people of Paradise? I said: Yes. He said: This is the black woman. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'I am afflicted with epilepsy, and I uncover myself, so pray to Allah for me.' He said: 'If you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise, or if you wish, I will pray to Allah that He cure you.' She said: 'I will be patient.' She said: 'I uncover myself, so pray to Allah that I not uncover myself.' So he prayed for her."

I say: Epilepsy (al-sar') is of two kinds: an epilepsy from evil earthly spirits, and an epilepsy from corrupt humors.

The second is what the physicians speak about regarding its cause and treatment. As for the epilepsy of spirits, their leaders and intelligent ones acknowledge it and do not deny it. They acknowledge that its treatment is by confronting the noble, good, heavenly spirits to those evil, wicked spirits, so that they repel its effects, oppose its actions, and nullify them. Hippocrates (Buqrat) stated this in some of his books. He mentioned some treatment for epilepsy and said: "This benefits only the epilepsy whose cause is humors and matter. As for the epilepsy that comes from spirits, this treatment is of no benefit." As for the ignorant, base, and lowly physicians, and those who consider heresy a virtue, they deny the epilepsy of spirits and do not admit that they affect the body of the afflicted. They have nothing but ignorance. Otherwise, there is nothing in the medical craft that repels this, and sense and experience bear witness to it. Their attribution of it to the domination of some humors is true in some of its divisions, but not in all. The early physicians used to call this epilepsy "the divine disease," and they said that it comes from spirits. As for Galen and others, they interpreted this name and said: They called it "the divine disease" only because this illness arises in the head and harms the divine, pure part whose dwelling is the brain. This interpretation arose from their ignorance of these spirits, their rulings, and their effects. (p-705) Then came the heretical physicians, who affirmed only epilepsy of humors alone. Whoever has intellect and knowledge of these spirits and their effects laughs at the ignorance of these physicians and the weakness of their minds. The treatment of this type occurs by two matters: one from the side of the afflicted, and one from the side of the healer.

That which is from the side of the afflicted occurs through the strength of his soul, the sincerity of his turning toward the Originator of these spirits and their Creator, and the correct seeking of refuge, when heart and tongue are in agreement. This is a form of combat, and the combatant cannot gain the victory over his enemy with a weapon except by two matters: that the weapon be sound and good in itself, and that the arm be strong. When either one is lacking, the weapon does not accomplish much. How much more so when both are absent, with the heart ruined by lack of tawhid, reliance, piety, and turning to God, and without any weapon.

The second, from the side of the healer, is that both of these matters should also be present in him, to the extent that some healers suffice with saying: "Come out of him," or "In the name of Allah," or "There is no power and no might except through Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Come out, enemy of Allah! I am the Messenger of Allah." I witnessed our shaykh (meaning Imam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah be pleased with him) send someone to the afflicted person who would address the spirit within him and say: "The Shaykh says to you: Come out, for this is not lawful for you." Then the afflicted person would recover. Sometimes he addressed it himself, and sometimes the spirit was defiant, so he would drive it out by striking, and the afflicted person would recover and feel no pain. We ourselves and others witnessed this from him many times. He often recited into the ear of the afflicted: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115]. He related to me that he once recited it into the ear of the afflicted, and the spirit said: "Yes," and he drew out his voice with it. He said: "I took a stick for him and struck him with it on the veins of his neck until my hands became blistered from the striking, and those present did not doubt that he would die from that striking. In the midst of the striking she said: 'I love him.' I said to her: 'He does not love you.' She said: 'I want to perform Hajj with him.' I said to her: 'He does not want to perform Hajj with you.' She said: 'I will leave him out of respect for you.' I said: 'No, but out of obedience to Allah and His Messenger.' She said: 'Then I will come out of him.'"

He (the one afflicted) sat up, looking to his right and left, and said, "What brought me to the presence of the Shaykh?" They said to him, "And all this beating?" He said, "And for what does the Shaykh beat me, when I have committed no sin?" He did not perceive that any beating had befallen him at all.

The shaykh would treat [the affliction] with Ayat al-Kursi, and he would order the afflicted person, and whoever treated him with it, to recite it frequently, along with the two Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs al-Falaq and al-Nas). In sum, this type of seizure (sar') and its treatment are not denied except by one who has little share of knowledge, intellect and understanding. Most of the domination of the evil spirits over their people comes from the weakness of their religion and the ruin of their hearts and tongues, [that is, from their neglect] of the realities of remembrance (dhikr), the protective incantations (ta'awidh), and the prophetic and faith-based fortifications. Thus the evil spirit encounters the man unarmed, with no weapon with him, and perhaps naked, so it affects him. Had the veil been lifted, you would have seen that most human souls are seized with these evil spirits, being in their captivity and grip, which drive them wherever they wish, and they cannot refrain from them or oppose them. In them is the greatest seizure, from which their possessor does not recover except at the time of separation (death) and direct witnessing, and then he will realize that he was in truth the one seized. And with God is the help sought.

The treatment of this seizure is the conjunction of sound reason with belief in what the messengers brought, and that Paradise and Hell be before his eyes and the focus of his heart. He should bring to mind the people of this world, the descent of punishments and calamities upon them, and their falling within their dwellings like the falling of rain, while they are seized and do not recover. How intense are the enemies of this seizure! But when the calamity became so widespread that none is seen but as one seized, it no longer became strange or disapproved; rather, due to the multitude of the seized, the opposite became the disapproved and strange thing. So when God wills good for a servant, he recovers from this seizure and looks at the sons of this world as seized around him, right and left, according to their different classes: some of them are overcome by madness; some recover briefly and return to their madness; and some recover once and go mad another time. When he recovers, he acts as the people of recovery and sound mind act; then the seizure returns to him, and he falls into confusion.

Then he said: As for the seizure of humours (sar' al-akhlat), it is an illness that prevents the psychic organs (al-a'da' al-nafsiyya) from acting, moving and standing upright, in a way that is not complete. Its cause is a thick, viscous humour that blocks the passages of the ventricles of the brain with an incomplete blockage, so that the passage of sensation and movement into it and into the organs is hindered to some degree, without being wholly cut off. It may also be due to other causes, such as thick wind trapped in the channels of the spirit, or foul vapour rising to it from some of the organs, or a corrosive quality, so that the brain contracts to repel the harmful thing, and a spasm follows in all the organs. The person cannot remain upright with it; rather he falls, and foam generally appears at his mouth. This illness counts among the acute diseases with respect to the time of the pain itself, and it may be counted among the chronic diseases with respect to its long duration and difficulty of cure, especially if the person is over twenty-five years old. This illness is in his brain, and especially in its substance, for the seizure of such people is permanent. Buqrat (Hippocrates) said: "The seizure remains in these people until they die."

Having established this, the woman mentioned in the hadith, who used to be seized and become uncovered, may have had a seizure of this kind. So the Prophet (ﷺ) promised her Paradise for her patience with this illness, and he prayed for her that she would not be uncovered; he gave her the choice between patience with Paradise and his supplicating for her healing without guarantee. She chose patience and Paradise. In this is evidence for the permissibility of abandoning treatment and medication, and that treatment of the spirits through supplications and turning to God accomplishes what the treatment of physicians cannot reach, and that its influence and effect, and the effect of nature upon it and its reaction, are greater than the influence of bodily medicines and the reaction of nature to them. We have tested this repeatedly, we and others. Judicious physicians acknowledge that in the action of the psychic powers and their reactions in curing illnesses there are wonders. Nothing is more harmful to the medical craft than the heretics of the people, their base ones and their ignorant ones. Apparently, this woman's seizure was of this type, though it may also have been from the spirits; and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave her the choice between patience over that together with Paradise, and supplicating for her healing; she chose patience and concealment. And God knows best.

﴿That﴾, i.e., the disordered standing, ﴿is because they said﴾, i.e., because of their saying: ﴿"Trade is only like usury"﴾, i.e., its equivalent in that each of them is an exchange (mu'awadah). If you say: Why was it not said, "Usury is only like trade," since the discussion concerns usury and not trade, and the permissibility of trade is agreed upon, so usury is analogized to it, and the proper form of analogy is to liken the disputed matter to the agreed matter? I answer: It was phrased this way as an exaggeration, for they had reached such a degree in their belief in the permissibility of usury that they made it a principle and a law of permissibility, to the point that they likened trade to it. Thus al-Zamakhshari answered.

Al-Nasir said in his Hawashi: "I have a different answer from what was mentioned. Whenever the aim is to equate the two cases in the establishment of a ruling, the speaker may equate them directly (tard). He says, for example: 'Usury is like trade,' and his purpose is to say: 'Trade is permissible, so usury is permissible.' He may also equate them in reverse ('aks), saying: 'Trade is like usury,' so that if usury were forbidden, trade would be forbidden, by necessity of equivalence. The conclusion that the force of the sentence indicates is: 'Since trade is permissible by agreement and not forbidden, it must be that usury is like it.' The first is by the method of direct analogy (qiyas al-tard), the second by the method of reverse (al-'aks). Both lead to one aim. So there is no need, on this formulation, to depart from the outward sense for the sake of exaggeration or otherwise. The purpose of all this is only to show what they imagined in the proper form of sound structure, even though it is a corrupt analogy in its foundation, because its use contradicts what is known of God's ruling in forbidding usury, permitting trade, and cutting off analogy between them. But if you use the two methods correctly, say in the first: 'Nabidh (date-wine) is like wine in the cause of prohibition, which is intoxication; wine is forbidden, so nabidh is forbidden.' And say in the second: 'Wine is only like nabidh; so if nabidh were permitted, wine would be permitted; but wine is not permitted by agreement, so nabidh is likewise, by necessity of the stated equivalence.' This interpretation is more fitting for the verse to be understood by. And God knows best."

His saying, ﴿"And God has permitted trade and forbidden usury"﴾, is a denial of their equating the two, for permission and prohibition are opposites. How can they be alike? It also indicates that analogy is overridden by the explicit text, for He made the proof of the invalidity of their analogy God's permitting and forbidding.

Al-Razi said: "The deniers of analogy (nufat al-qiyas) hold fast to this phrase. They say: 'If religion were by analogy, this objection would be binding; since it is refuted, we know that religion is by text, not by analogy.'" Al-Qaffal, may God have mercy on him, mentioned the difference between the two categories, saying: "Whoever sells a garment worth ten for twenty has made the garment itself equivalent to twenty. When mutual consent to this equivalence is reached, each becomes equivalent to the other in value in their view, and he has not taken anything from his companion without return. But if he sells ten for twenty, he has taken the extra ten without return. It cannot be said that its return is the delay of the term, because delay is not property or a thing pointed to, so as to make it a return for the extra ten. Thus the difference between the two cases is clear." Abu Nu'aym, in al-Hilya, reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that he was asked: "Why did God forbid usury?" He said: "So that people do not withhold kindness (ma'ruf)", i.e., the benevolence that is in lending; for if a dirham were permitted for two dirhams, no one would consent to give a dirham for a dirham.

﴿So whoever receives an admonition﴾, i.e., there reaches him exhortation and warning, such as the prohibition of usury, ﴿from his Lord﴾: this is connected to "received" (jā'ahu), or to something omitted that falls as a qualifier of "admonition." The mention of the title of Lordship together with the pronoun indicates that the coming of the admonition is for nurture. ﴿And desists﴾ is coordinated with "received", i.e., he takes heed without delay and follows the prohibition. ﴿Then to him is what has passed﴾, i.e., what he took before the prohibition, and it is not to be reclaimed from him. ﴿And his affair is with God﴾: if He wills, He will take it, since the distinction is clear; and if He wills, He will pardon him, for the distinction, though it is evident to people of reflection, may be hidden from the common folk. ﴿And whoever returns﴾, i.e., to the permitting of usury after the text, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾, because of their disbelief in the text, and their rejection of it by their corrupt analogy after its corruption has become evident. Whoever makes lawful what God, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden is a disbeliever, and therefore he deserves eternity [in the Fire]. By this it becomes clear that the Mu'tazilah have no connection to this verse regarding the eternal damnation of grave sinners, since they based their argument on the claim that what is threatened with eternity is only returning to the practice of usury. It is not hidden that the outward meaning on which they relied does not support them, for what the return refers to is what preceded: as if He said, "Whoever returns to what was previously mentioned, namely the practice of usury, the belief in its permissibility, and the argument for it by analogy to trade." Without doubt, whoever engages in usury transactions while considering them lawful, arrogantly denying their prohibition, attributing their permissibility to opposing God's clear signs with imaginations he fancies, has disbelieved and then increased in disbelief. In that case, the one promised eternity in the verse is one who is called a disbeliever, a denier, and not a believer, and this is not disputed. So there is no evidence for the Mu'tazilah in this verse for their doctrine. And God is the Granter of success. He pointed to this in al-Intisaf.

In Fath al-Bayan it is said: "Adopting this interpretation is obligatory, because of the mass-transmitted hadiths stating that monotheists will be brought out of the Fire."

(p-710) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[276] ﴿Allah destroys interest and gives increase for charities. And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner.﴾

﴿Allah destroys interest﴾ means: He removes its increase and erases its good, even though it is an increase outwardly; it does not benefit one in the Hereafter, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And what you give in interest to increase the wealth of people does not increase with Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 39], and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿and place the wicked one upon another and heap them all together and put them into Hell﴾ [al-Anfal: 37]. ﴿And gives increase for charities﴾ means: He multiplies them and causes them to grow, even though they appear to be a loss in the witnessed world.

Benefits:

The first: Al-Qashani said: Increase and decrease occur only in relation to the outcome and the benefit in both abodes. Wealth obtained from interest has no blessing, because it was acquired by opposing the truth, so its outcome is grievous, and its possessor commits all sorts of sins; for every food generates in its eater motives and actions of its own kind. If it is haram, it moves him toward forbidden actions; if it is disliked, toward disliked actions; if it is permissible, toward permissible ones; and if it is from surplus food, toward recommended acts, and he becomes one who gives voluntarily and bountifully in his actions. If it is only the amount of the obligatory rights, his actions are obligatory and necessary. If it is from excess and indulgences, his actions are likewise. So upon him is the sin of interest and the effects of his forbidden actions that arise from his eating, so his punishments and sins keep increasing forever, and Allah destroys his wealth in this world, so that his descendants and offspring do not benefit from it. He is thus among those who lost both this world and the Hereafter, and that is the total destruction. As for the one who gives charity, because his wealth is purified, Allah blesses its growth while preserving the principal, and whoever eats it can only be obedient in his actions, and his wealth remains beneficial for his descendants and offspring. And that (p-711) is increase in reality. Even if its increase were nothing but what is spent in obedience to Allah, that would suffice as an increase. And what increase is better than what remains with Allah?! Even if the loss of interest were nothing but its being obtained by opposing Allah and committing what He has forbidden, that would suffice as a loss. And what loss is more grievous than what becomes the cause of its possessor's veiling, his punishment, and the diminishing of his share with Allah?!

The second: Al-Qashani, may Allah have mercy on him, said before that: The eater of interest is in a worse state than all those who commit major sins, for every earner has a trust in what his earnings consist of, whether little or much, such as the merchant, the farmer, and the craftsman, since they did not fix their provisions by their own intellects, and they were not determined for them before earning, so they are in truth in unknown circumstances, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah refuses to provide for the believer except from where he does not know." As for the eater of interest, he has fixed for the taker his gain and his provision, whether the taker profits or loses; so he is veiled from his Lord by himself, and from his provision by his own determining it. He has no trust at all, so Allah entrusts him to himself and his intellect, and removes him from His protection and guardianship, so the jinn snatch him away and derange him, and he rises on the Day of Resurrection without any bond between him and Allah, unlike the rest of people who are bound to Him by trust, so he is like the one struck down whom Satan has touched, so he staggers, not guided to any goal.

The third: Some of the scholars of civilization (al-'Umrani) said: For the lawful pursuit of wealth it is required that it be from a legitimate source, such as in exchange for labour or a transaction, and that wealth not exceed the amount needed by much. For this reason all the heavenly religions have prohibited the eating of interest, and likewise political, moral, and civilizational wisdom, with the intent of preserving equality and closeness among people in financial strength, because interest is gain without material counter-value, so it has the meaning of usurpation; and it is without labour, so it involves habituation to idleness which corrupts morals; and without exposure to natural losses, such as trade, agriculture, and property; and from the evidence: through interest wealth swells and equality among people is disturbed.

Then he said: Economists and financial thinkers have examined the matter of interest and said: Moderate interest is beneficial (p-712) and indeed necessary. First: for the sake of sustaining large transactions. Second: because existing money does not suffice for circulation, how much more so when hoarders withhold a portion of it? Third: because many of the wealthy do not know the ways of profit-making, or are unable to pursue them, while many who know them do not find capital or partners in a joint venture.

This view is correct from the standpoint of increasing the wealth of individuals and nations. But political and moral thinkers look at the harm to the masses of nations as greater than its benefit, because these individual fortunes enable internal tyranny, making people into two classes: slaves and masters; and they strengthen external tyranny, facilitating aggression upon the freedom and independence of weak nations in wealth and means; and these are corrupt aims in the view of wisdom and justice. For this reason the religions have prohibited interest with severe prohibition. End.

The fourth: Al-Razi said: When Exalted Allah had exaggerated in warning against interest, and had exaggerated in the preceding verses in commanding charities, He mentioned here what serves as an incitement to abandoning charities and engaging in interest, and He exposed its corruption. This is because the motive for engaging in interest is obtaining more goods, while what diverts from charities is avoiding the loss of goods. So Exalted Allah clarified that interest, although it is an increase in wealth, is in reality a loss, and that charity, although it appears to be a loss in form, is an increase in meaning. Since this is the case, it befits the intelligent person not to heed what the nature and the senses dictate of motives and deterrents, but to rely on what the Law has urged him toward of them.

Al-Qaffal said: The parallel to His saying ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾ is the parable He struck earlier of a smooth rock with dust upon it, which a heavy rain struck and left bare. The parallel to His saying ﴿and gives increase for charities﴾ is the parable He struck of a single grain that produced seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains.

﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾: the two forms are intensives derived from disbelief (kufr) and sin (ithm), because the one who deems interest lawful and the one who eats it persist in both and continue in that. In the verse there is an emphasis on the matter of interest and an announcement that it is an act of the disbelievers, not an act of the Muslims.

(p-713)The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[277] ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾ in Allah, His Messenger, His books, and the prohibition of riba. Their faith outweighed the command of Allah to spend, over their accumulation of wealth. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ between themselves and their Lord, among which is generosity and abandoning riba. ﴿And establish prayer﴾, which forbids indecency and wrongdoing, such as stinginess and riba. ﴿And give zakah﴾: they gave the zakah of their wealth, which is among the greatest causes of the excellence of generosity. ﴿Their reward is with their Lord﴾: their complete recompense, ﴿with their Lord﴾ in Paradise. ﴿And no fear will there be concerning them﴾ on the Day of the Greatest Terror.

﴿Nor will they grieve﴾ because they rejoice in what their Lord has given them and has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[278] ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you should be believers.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾, i.e., be mindful of Allah regarding interest (ribā), because in it lies the nullification of His wisdom, exalted is He, in creating wealth. ﴿And give up what remains of interest﴾, i.e., leave off what remains owed to you of interest from the debtors. ﴿If you should be believers﴾ in truth, for that necessarily entails compliance with what you have been commanded, absolutely.

Al-Harrali (al-Ḥarālī) said: He made clear that interest (ribā) and faith (īmān) do not come together.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[279] ﴿But if you do not do it, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, you may have your principal. You do not wrong, nor are you wronged.﴾

﴿But if you do not do it﴾, i.e., if you do not abandon what remains; ﴿then be informed﴾, i.e., know; ﴿of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾ (p-714). Al-Mahayimi said: That is, if you do not abandon what remains, you have been treating His command lightly, and whoever treats the command of a king lightly has made war upon him.

War is the opposite of peace (silm), and whoever is at war with Allah and His Messenger will never prosper. In this there is an allusion to a bad end for one who persists in taking usury. ﴿And if you repent﴾ of usury: ﴿then you may have your principal﴾, i.e., your capital: ﴿You do not wrong﴾ by seeking an increase; ﴿nor are you wronged﴾ by a reduction or procrastination. Rather, you have what you paid, without any addition to it or deduction from it. Then the Exalted commanded patience toward the debtor who cannot find repayment, saying:

The commentary on His saying, the Exalted:

[280] ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease. And that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

﴿And if the debtor is in hardship﴾, meaning in full or in part. ﴿Then let there be postponement﴾, meaning it is obligatory to grant respite by the amount of his hardship, ﴿until a time of ease﴾, meaning until he is at ease to that extent. This is not like the practice of the people of the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), where a creditor would say to his debtor when the debt fell due: "Either you pay, or you increase the interest." Then the Exalted encouraged remitting the debt of the one in hardship and promised good and abundant reward for it, saying: ﴿And that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ That is, that you leave the hardship-stricken debtor the amount of his hardship by releasing him from it, because the repayment may not be obtained immediately, so he would take in the Hereafter what is equivalent to it. Charity is multiplied by the multiples mentioned.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i related from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man used to lend money to people, and he would say to his servant: 'If you come to someone in hardship, overlook it, perhaps Allah will overlook us.' So he met Allah and He overlooked him." Muslim and al-Tirmidhi related something similar from Abu Mas'ud al-Badri, may Allah be pleased with him.

(p-715) And from Abu Qatadah al-Harith ibn Ribi al-Ansari, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever relieves his debtor or wipes away the debt for him, he will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.'" Related by Imam Ahmad and Muslim. And from Buraydah, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity equal to it for each day.' Then I heard him say: 'Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity twice that for each day.'" I asked him about that, and he ﷺ said: "For him is a charity for each day before the debt falls due. But when the debt falls due and he grants him respite, for him is a charity twice that for each day." And from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship or remits it for him, Allah will shield him from the heat of Hell." Both were related by Imam Ahmad. Then the Exalted said, admonishing His servants and reminding them of the passing away of the world and the perishing of what is in it of wealth and other things, of the coming of the Hereafter and the return to Him, the Exalted, and of His, the Exalted, reckoning His creation for what they did, and His recompense for them for what they earned of good and evil, warning them of His punishment, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 281:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[281] ﴿And guard yourselves against a Day on which you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And guard yourselves against a Day﴾ meaning: fear the punishment of a Day ﴿on which you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾, that is, what it did of good or evil.

Al-Mahayimi said: If the creditor collects his right by pressing the debtor, Allah collects from him His rights by pressing him; and if he forgives him, then Allah is more deserving of forgiveness. As for the debtor, if he does not repay the creditor's right while able to pay, Allah collects His right from him. As for one who is unable, it is hoped that Allah will pardon him and that his creditor will be satisfied with a recompense from Him. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: their good deeds will not be diminished, nor will their evil deeds be increased.

Admonition:

Whoever reflects on these verses and what they contain of the punishment of the people of riba (usury) and those who consider it lawful, will realize the magnitude of their sin and crime. There follows from it their being raised on the Day of Gathering deranged, their eternal abiding in the Fire, their being branded with disbelief, and war from Allah and His Messenger, and the curse. Likewise there follows blame, hatred, loss of uprightness, loss of trustworthiness, their being named with corruption, harshness and coarseness, and the supplication of one wronged over the taking of his wealth by his oppressor. This is a cause for the disappearance of goodness and blessing. How ugly is this disobedience and how much greater its indecency! And how great are the punishments that follow from it! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained what these verses left implicit, through explicit statement, of the punishments and vile consequences befalling the people of riba, in many hadiths. Among them is what al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins," i.e., the ruinous ones. They said: "O Messenger of Allah! What are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming riba, consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unwary women."

Al-Bukhari narrated from Samurah ibn Jundub, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Last night I saw two men who came to me and took me out to a sacred land. We went on until we came upon a river of blood, in which there was a man standing, and on the bank of the river there was a man with stones before him. The man in the river approached, and whenever he tried to come out, the other threw a stone into his mouth and sent him back to where he was. Every time he came to get out, he would throw a stone into his mouth, and he would return as he was." I said: "What is this that I saw in the river?" He said: "The consumer of riba."

Muslim narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the consumer of riba, its agent, its scribe, and its two witnesses." And he said: "They are all equal."

Al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud narrated from Abu Juhayfah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, and the consumer of riba and its agent."

There are abundant reports which al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur.

[p. 719]

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[282] ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt with one another for a specified term, write it down. Let a scribe write it down between you justly. No scribe should refuse to write as Allah has taught him; so let him write. Let the one who owes the debt dictate, let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything of it. But if the one who owes the debt is feeble-minded, or weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate justly. And call upon two witnesses from among your men. If there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, the other may remind her. The witnesses should not refuse when they are called. And do not be averse to writing it down, whether it is small or large, along with its term. That is more just in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt among you, unless it is a present trade that you conduct among yourselves. Then there is no blame on you if you do not write it down. But take witnesses when you trade with one another. Let neither scribe nor witness be harmed. If you do so, it is indeed a transgression on your part. Fear Allah; Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt with one another for a specified term, write it down﴾: This is an instruction from Him, exalted is He, to His believing servants: when they deal with one another in transactions involving deferred payment, they should write them down, so that this is more preserving of their amount and their due time, and more precise for the witness regarding them. He drew attention to this at the end of the verse when He said: ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt﴾. In His words ﴿tadayantum﴾ (you contract a debt with one another) is evidence for the permissibility of *salam* (a sale in which the price is paid in advance and the goods are delivered later), because *al-mudayana* (the mutual contracting of debt) is an action of two parties, and it is *salam* itself, since it is a debt from both sides together. On this, (p. 720) it is narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I testify that *al-salaf* (advance payment) guaranteed for a specified term is something Allah, exalted is He, has made lawful and permitted. Then he recited: ﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt with one another…﴾ to the end of the verse." Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Others said: His words ﴿when you contract a debt﴾ refer to the sale of any debt for a specified term, and so it is called *al-tadayun* (mutual debt-contracting), just as the seller and the buyer are called *al-mutabayi'ayn* (the two who sell to one another), because each of them is a seller in one respect. Accordingly, *al-mudayana* means *al-tadayun*. The reason we were not commanded to write in the sale of specific goods (*bay' al-a'yan*) is that in debt transactions, one of the two parties obtains his need by receiving the capital, while the other has not yet obtained his. Thus this may lead the latter to deny the debt and reject it. But when he recalls that it was written down and witnessed against him, he refrains from denial and rejection, out of fear of his lie being exposed and his disgrace before people. This is not the case with "item for item" exchange, because each of the two parties obtains his need only through what the other obtains, so there is no meaning of denial there. There is another aspect: it is possible that one may forget and deny it, or forget part of it and remember part, so He commanded writing so that the right of the other party would not be lost by abandoning writing. This is not so in the sale of item for item, so they differ. Thus says al-Maturidi in *al-Ta'wilat*.

﴿Let a scribe write it down between you justly﴾: *bi-l-'adl* (justly) is a prepositional phrase that is either connected to the verb, meaning "let him write with the truth," or connected to a deleted element as a description of *kateb* (scribe), meaning: let the one who undertakes the writing be such that he writes impartially, without leaning toward either side, neither adding nor subtracting. This is also an instruction to the contracting parties to choose a scribe who is a jurist and pious, so that his writing is trustworthy and approved by the Sharia.

﴿No scribe should refuse﴾: i.e., should not abstain, ﴿to write as Allah has taught him﴾: i.e., as He has explained it in His words: ﴿justly﴾. Or it means: he should not refuse to benefit people by his writing, just as Allah has benefited him by teaching him writing, as in His words: ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 77]. And in a hadith: "Indeed, among charity is that you help a craftsman or make something for one who is unskilled." (p. 721) And in another hadith: "Whoever conceals knowledge that he possesses will be bridled with a bridle of fire."

Al-Razi said: The apparent meaning of these words is a prohibition on every scribe from refraining from writing, and an obligation upon everyone who is a scribe. ﴿So let him write﴾: i.e., that taught writing. He commanded it after the prohibition against refusing it, to emphasize it. ﴿Let the one who owes the debt dictate﴾: *al-imlal* (dictation) is the same as *al-imla'* (dictation). These are two dialects, both of which the Qur'an has uttered. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿so it is dictated to him﴾ [al-Furqan: 5]. I.e., let the dictator to the scribe be the debtor, who is the one who owes the debt, because he is the one acknowledging it and the one against whom testimony is given. ﴿And let him fear﴾: i.e., let the dictator fear ﴿Allah, his Lord﴾: He combined the Noble Name with the beautiful attribute for the sake of emphasis in warning. ﴿And not diminish﴾: i.e., not reduce ﴿anything of it﴾: i.e., of what is owed ﴿anything﴾ of the debt upon him. ﴿But if the one who owes the debt﴾: i.e., the debtor, ﴿is feeble-minded﴾: i.e., of light judgment, or ignorant of dictation, unable to do it well; ﴿or weak﴾: a child or an old man who is decrepit; ﴿or unable to dictate himself﴾: i.e., or not able to dictate by himself, due to muteness, dumbness, or a foreign tongue. The word *huwa* (himself) here is an emphasis of the implied subject. The majority read it with a *damma* on the *ha'* because it is a separate word, not connected to what precedes it, so it begins with it. It was also read with a *sukun* on it, as if the separate pronoun were treated like a connected one after *wa-* (and), *fa-* (so), or *li-* (for), as in *wa-huwa*, *fa-huwa*, *la-hu*. This was said by Abu al-Baqa'.

﴿then let his guardian dictate﴾: meaning the one who manages his affairs, whether a trustee, an agent, or an interpreter; ﴿justly﴾: without deficiency or excess. ﴿And call upon two witnesses from among your men﴾ (p. 722): i.e., seek them, so that they bear witness to the debt. ﴿But if they are not two men﴾: i.e., the two witnesses, ﴿then a man and two women from among those you accept﴾: i.e., in justice, ﴿as witnesses﴾. Since He stipulated for standing in place of one man, a number of women, He gave a reason which points to a deficiency of memory in them, saying: ﴿so that if one of them errs﴾: i.e., the testimony escapes her; ﴿the other may remind her﴾ of what she forgot. ﴿The witnesses should not refuse when they are called﴾: i.e., to perform the testimony they have borne, or to bear it. Calling them "witnesses" before they bear testimony is treating the one who is about to do something as if he has done it.

﴿And do not be averse to writing it down﴾: i.e., the debt; ﴿whether it is small or large, along with its term﴾; ﴿that﴾: i.e., what has been mentioned of writing; ﴿is more just﴾: i.e., more equitable; ﴿in the sight of Allah, and more upright for testimony﴾: i.e., more helpful in establishing it, for through it reliance on memory is completed; ﴿and closer﴾: i.e., nearer; ﴿to preventing doubt﴾: i.e., so that you do not doubt the kind of debt, its amount, or its term, through one of the contracting parties raising doubts. ﴿Unless it is a present trade﴾: i.e., immediate; ﴿that you conduct among yourselves﴾: i.e., you frequently conduct; ﴿so writing it becomes difficult for you, while the need for it is small﴾; ﴿then there is no blame on you if you do not write it down﴾, because it is settled on the spot, so disputes and forgetting are unlikely in it.

Abu al-Baqa' said: *tijarah* (trade) is read in the nominative, so that it is the complete verb, and *hadirah* (present) is its description. It is also permissible that it be the incomplete verb, with *tijarah* as its subject, *hadirah* as its description, and *tudirunaha* as the predicate. It is also read in the accusative, so that the active participle is implied in it, its estimate being: "unless the transaction is a trade."

﴿And take witnesses when you trade with one another﴾: this is a command to take witnesses for trade in general, whether immediate or deferred, because it is more cautious and further from what disagreement might arise. It is also permissible to intend: "take witnesses when you trade in this trade," meaning the present trade, in that witnessing is sufficient for it without writing. From al-Dahhak: "It is a firm ordinance from Allah, even for a bunch of herbs." Thus says al-Zamakhshari in *al-Kashshaf*. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Jabir ibn Zayd that he bought a whip and took witnesses, and said: "Allah said: ﴿And take witnesses when you trade with one another.﴾"

Abu al-Qasim ibn Salama said in his book *al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh* (abrogating and abrogated): A group of the Successors (p. 723) held that they should call witnesses in every sale and purchase. Among them were al-Sha'bi and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. They used to say: "We see that we should call witnesses even for a bunch of herbs."

﴿Let neither scribe nor witness be harmed﴾: this admits of being read in the active or passive voice, and what indicates this is that it was read as *wa-la yudarir* with a kasra and with a fatha. The meaning is a prohibition on the scribe and the witness from refusing to respond to what is requested of them, and from distortion, addition, or reduction; or a prohibition on harming them by causing them to hurry away from something important. Al-Harrali said: In this, there is an indirect encouragement to kindness toward the witness and scribe, so that he responds to the request and assists him in complying with his command, by avoiding harm, which is his being idle or being employed in some matter of his worldly affairs. Thus in this indirect expression is a permission for what the scribe takes, and for one who claims a need for help in this respect from those who present themselves for something which harms him if he abandons it.

﴿If you do so﴾: i.e., what you have been forbidden of harm; ﴿then it is indeed a transgression on your part﴾: i.e., a departure by you from the Sharia that Allah has laid out for you. Al-Harrali said: In the form *fu'ul* (fusuq) there is emphasis and intensification in the warning.

﴿And fear Allah﴾: that He punish you by departing from His obedience; ﴿and Allah teaches you﴾ His rulings, which contain your welfare; ﴿and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ Since the implied meaning was: "this applies when you are present, when it is easy for you to bring the scribe and the witness," he followed it with His words:

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[283] ﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand. And if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted fulfil his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾

﴿And if you are on a journey﴾ means: travelling, and you contract a debt for a specified term. ﴿And you do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand﴾ (p. 724): that is, what is used to secure the debt is a pledge taken in hand, which the creditor takes as a guarantee for his debt. This applies when some of them do not trust one another without a guarantee. ﴿And if one of you trusts another﴾ because of his good opinion of him, and he dispenses with taking a pledge because of his trustworthiness. ﴿Then let the one who is trusted﴾, who is the debtor. He expressed him with this title only because it is the clear means of identifying him and because it compels him to pay. ﴿Fulfil his trust﴾, that is, his debt. It was called a trust (amanah) only because the creditor entrusted him with it by leaving off taking a pledge. ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾ in observing the rights of the trust. In combining the title of divinity (al-Uluhiyyah) with the attribute of lordship (al-Rububiyyah) there is emphasis and warning that is not hidden. ﴿And do not conceal﴾, O witnesses, ﴿the testimony. And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why did He not restrict Himself to saying "for he is sinful"? And what is the benefit of mentioning the heart when the sinful act is the whole person and not the heart alone? I say: concealing testimony is to conceal it within oneself and not speak it. Since it is a sin committed by the heart, it is attributed to the heart, because attributing an act to the limb through which it is done is more emphatic. Do you not see that when you wish to emphasise, you say: "This is something my eye has seen, and something my ear has heard, and something my heart has known." Also, the heart is the chief of the organs, the lump of flesh which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. So it is as if it were said: sin has taken firm hold of the root of his self and has possessed the noblest place in it. And lest it be thought that concealing testimony is among the sins connected only with the tongue, and so that it may be known that the heart is the root of what is connected to it and the source of its commission, while the tongue is its interpreter; and because the acts of the hearts are greater than the acts of the other limbs, and they are to them like the roots from which they branch out. Do you not see that the root of good and evil deeds is faith and disbelief, and both are acts of the heart? So when He made concealing testimony one of the sins of the heart, He thereby testified that it is among the greatest of sins.

It is also read ﴿qalbahu﴾ (his heart) in the accusative, as in His saying: "he has befooled himself" (safiha nafsahu). Ibn Abi ʿAblah recited: ﴿athima qalbuhu﴾, meaning: he made it sinful. ﴿And Allah is of what you do﴾, that is, of your hearts, your tongues and your limbs, ﴿Knowing﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[284] ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you show﴾, meaning you make apparent, ﴿what is in your souls﴾ of voluntary actions, by the tongue or by the limbs, ﴿or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it.﴾ Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: When He, exalted is He, said at the end of the preceding verse, ﴿And Allah is Knower of what you do﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283], He followed it with what functions as a rational proof, saying, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ The meaning of this ownership is that these things, since they are originated, have come into being by His creating, forming and originating them. Whoever is the doer of these firmly wrought, perfected, wondrous and marvelous acts, which contain abundant wisdoms and great benefits, must necessarily be knowing of them, for it is impossible that a firm and perfected act proceed from one ignorant of it. Thus it is as though Allah, exalted is He, argued by His creation of the heavens and the earth, together with the aspects of firmness and perfection in them, that He is knowing of them and encompasses their parts and particulars.

Al-Sha'bi said: When He, exalted is He, forbade concealing testimony and threatened for it, He made clear that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so He will requite concealment and disclosure. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir (p. 726) and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if you show﴾ etc., was revealed concerning the concealing of testimony and its establishment.

Imam Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, who said: «When this verse was revealed, ﴿And if you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, he said: something entered their hearts from it such as nothing had entered their hearts before. So the Prophet ﷺ said: "Say: We hear and we obey and we submit." He said: So Allah cast faith into their hearts, and Allah revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned, and it bears what it earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. He said: "I have done." ﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed on those before us.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. He said: "I have done." ﴿And forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. He said: "I have done."» In the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn Humayd and al-Tabarani, Ibn 'Abbas said: This whispering was of a kind no one among the Muslims had the capacity to bear, and the matter came to the point that Allah decreed that for the soul is what it earned and against it is what it has merited, of speech and deed.

I say: What has been reported, that the verse terrified whoever among the Companions was terrified, arose only from its generality and from His saying ﴿will call you to account﴾, since he took the reckoning to mean the taking to task. As for its generality, its composition clearly indicates it, though it primarily and specifically concerns testimony and its concealment, and secondarily and incidentally other matters. As for taking the reckoning to mean taking to task and retribution, if this is according to common usage or linguistic usage, then concealment here means a concealment whose prohibition is agreed upon, such as hypocrisy and doubt in religion, and there is no difficulty in the verse. This is perhaps supported by the mention of faith after it, and the closing of the sura with disclosure and concealment serves as a return of the final part to the beginning (radd al-'ajz 'ala al-sadr), corresponding to the opening of the sura with the believers and the disbelievers and what belongs to each of them. If the reckoning is not literal in what has been mentioned, but rather its meaning is His, exalted is He, causing the servant to stand before his deed, whether good or evil, and showing him its outcome, the good or the bad, which is what appears, then there is also no difficulty. What was reported from some of the Companions, may Allah's good pleasure be upon them, has its source in the strength of certainty and the intensity of fear of the terror of the place of appearing, together with the occurrence of reckoning in many verses in the context of the dangers of the Resurrection, which rightly makes the heart of every believer tremble (p. 727). Do not forget what we have previously stated in the introduction and elsewhere, that when they say "it was revealed concerning such and such," it may mean that such and such is among what the wording of the verse includes by its generality, both for it and for other than it. So also here: although the context of the verse concerns testimony and its concealment, it includes other things by its generality, and for this reason whispering and the imagining of what is imagined entered within it. His saying in the narration, "Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾" [al-Baqarah: 286], does not imply any delay between what entered their hearts and the revelation of it. Rather, the intent, as we stated regarding the occasion of revelation, is that the wording ﴿Allah does not burden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286] etc., which was revealed with it, makes clear that there is no blame for such whispering and the like. Understand this, for it is extremely precious, and by it is removed from you what many dispute concerning this verse and regard as among its difficulties. And success is from Allah.

Furthermore, in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Allah, exalted is He, has overlooked for me in regard to my community what their souls whisper, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it.» And in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Allah, mighty and majestic, said: When My servant intends an evil deed, do not record it against him; if he does it, record it as one evil deed. When he intends a good deed and does not do it, record it as a good deed; if he does it, record it as ten.»

﴿Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.﴾ It is also read with the two verbs in the nominative, as a resumptive construction (isti'naf), meaning: so He forgives, etc. And with both in the jussive, coordinated upon the answer of the conditional (jawab al-shart). In placing forgiveness before punishment there is an indication that His mercy precedes His wrath. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ Al-Razi said: By His saying ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ He has made clear that He possesses complete dominion and sovereignty, and by His saying ﴿Whether you show﴾ etc., that He possesses complete knowledge and encompassment. Then by His saying ﴿and Allah is over all things competent﴾ He has made clear that He possesses complete power, prevailing over all possibilities by subjugation, capability, bringing into being and annihilation. There is no perfection higher or greater than the attainment of perfection in these attributes, and the one described with these perfections must be, for every rational person, a servant submissive to Him, obedient to His commands and prohibitions, and cautious of incurring His displeasure. And success is from Allah.

(p-728) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[285] ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers too. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say: "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; and to You is the final destination."﴾

﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾ — meaning: he affirmed it by accepting it and adopting its character, as 'A'isha said: "His character was the Qur'an," and by advancing in its meanings and realizing them. ﴿And the believers﴾ — meaning: they likewise believed.

Al-Zajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in this surah the obligation of prayer (salah), zakah, fasting, hajj, divorce, menstruation, ila' (oath of abstinence), jihad, the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, and usury and debt, He concluded it with His words: ﴿The Messenger believes﴾, to glorify him and to affirm his Prophet ﷺ, and the believers affirm all of that mentioned before it and other things, so that it would be a confirmation of it and a summation (fadhlaka).

A subtle point:

His words "and the believers" (wa-l-mu'minun) may be a subject (mubtada'), with the sentence after it as its predicate (khabar), namely "each one believed" (kullun amana). The pronoun returning to the subject is the tanwin (nunation) standing in for the pronoun in "kullun," since the tanwin that stands in for a pronoun is among what returns to the subject. Or it may be conjoined (ma'tuf) to "the Messenger," so the tanwin refers to "the Messenger and the believers." Many have chosen the first view, among them the scholar Abu al-Su'ud, and he lengthened in explaining it. In my view, the better option is the second, (p-729) because the context is enumerating what is believed in, and this is shared by the Messenger and his followers, although the essential nature of the Messenger's faith is not shared by anyone else; the context is not one of exclusivity. And Allah knows best.

﴿Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. "We make no distinction﴾ — meaning: they say, "We make no distinction﴾ ﴿between any of His messengers﴾ — meaning: by rejecting some and accepting others; and we have no doubt that they are upon the truth and with the truth. ﴿And they say: "We hear"﴾ — meaning: your words, and we have understood them; ﴿and we obey﴾ — meaning: we carry out your command, we act upon it, and we remain steadfast in it. And since they knew that they are not free from shortcoming, and that the Lord forgives whom He wills, they said: ﴿Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾ — meaning: forgive us, Your forgiveness; or we ask You for Your forgiveness of our sins. The mention of hearing and obedience before the request for forgiveness is because mentioning the means before the one asked is more conducive to being answered and accepted. ﴿And to You is the final destination﴾ — meaning: the return by death and resurrection, to no one other than You. This is a concluding statement (tadhyil) for what precedes it, establishing the need for forgiveness, since return is for reckoning and recompense.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 1 of 3):**

The discussion on the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[286] ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It shall have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it shall bear [the consequence of] what it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes. Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.﴾

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ means: He does not load it except with what it can bear and is able to do, and in which it is not incapable.

Al-Razi said: It is possible that this is an initial statement from Allah, and it is possible that it is a report of the Messenger and the believers saying it, in the sequence of the speech in His statement: ﴿And they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], and they said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾.

What supports this is what follows it, His statement: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us﴾. It is as though He, exalted is He, related their way of holding fast to faith and righteous action (p. 730), and related of them, as part of that, that they described their Lord as one who does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.

Then al-Razi said, regarding the structure of the composition (al-nazm): If we say that this is from the speech of the believers, then the link of the composition is that when they said, ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], it was as though they said: How could we not hear and obey, when He, exalted is He, does not burden us except with what is within our capacity and ability? So if He, exalted is He, by the judgment of divine mercy, does not demand of us except what is easy and light, then likewise we, by the judgment of servanthood, must be hearing and obeying. And if we say that this is from the speech of Allah, exalted is He, then the link of the composition is that when they said, ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], and then after it they said, ﴿Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], this indicates that their saying ﴿Your forgiveness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285] is a request for forgiveness for the shortcomings that proceed from them deliberately. So when their saying "Your forgiveness" was a request for forgiveness for that shortcoming, Allah, exalted is He, certainly lightened that for them and said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. The meaning is: when you hear and obey, and you do not deliberately fall short, then if some kind of shortcoming occurs from you through inadvertence and heedlessness, do not be fearful of it, for Allah, exalted is He, ﴿does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. In sum, this is a response to them in their supplication in their saying: "Your forgiveness, our Lord."

Zayn al-'Abidin Bir Muhammad Durra said in *al-Madhah al-Kubra*: And on the possibility that His statement ﴿Allah does not burden﴾ and so on is a report, it is from the type of conjunction without a conjunctive particle ('atf bila 'atif), or the speech is with the assumption of "they said." Some of them said: You may make ﴿Allah does not burden﴾ and so on within the scope of the saying, and that it is a report of the scattered statements, not conjoined to one another, of the believers, and it is a praise of them, that they are thankful to Allah, exalted is He, for His imposition, since they see that it has not gone beyond their capacity, and that they see that Allah, exalted is He, does not benefit from their good deeds, rather it is for their benefit, and is not harmed by their evil deeds, rather it is against them.

Al-Biqa'i said: This statement is part of their supplication in the manner of praise, seeking the fulfillment of what the Messenger ﷺ informed them of from Him, glorified is He, concerning that, out of fear that they might be charged with what Allah, exalted is He, might charge them with, namely being held accountable for whisperings, since these are among what souls conceal, and there is no capacity to repel them.

(p. 731) Perhaps the shift from direct address to the third person, by mentioning the Greatest Name, is a form of ingratiation, that He has among the attributes of greatness what calls for pardoning their weakness, and among the attributes of forbearance and mercy what eases them. It is possible that this is from the speech of Allah, exalted is He, as a reward for them for their saying ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], and so on. Thus He informed them by this that He does not hold them accountable for the promptings of the soul, and so what had burdened them from His statement ﴿And if you show what is in your souls﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284], and so on, is removed. This is unlike what the saying of the Children of Israel conveyed to them: "We hear and we disobey," in terms of burdens in this world and the Hereafter. Then it would be a resumed statement, answering someone who, as it were, said: Has He answered their supplication? And this possibility is supported by His following the ruling on what is within capacity with the resumed or inferred statement: ﴿It shall have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it shall bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾.

Al-'Allama Abu al-Su'ud said: His statement, exalted is He, ﴿It shall have [the reward of] what it has earned﴾ and so on is to encourage preserving the obligations of the duty and to warn against neglecting them, by explaining that the imposition on every soul, together with its accompanying blessing of lightening and facilitation, includes in observing it an additional benefit, and that this benefit returns to it and not to others, and neglecting it entails a harm that befalls it and not others. For the restriction of the benefit of an act to its doer is among the strongest motives to performing it, and the restriction of its harm to him is among the most powerful deterrents from committing it.
