That is: it has the reward of what it has earned of good, which it was charged to do, not for others; and it bears the punishment of what it has earned of evil, which it was charged to abandon, not that of others. And the mention of "earning" (iktisab) in the case of evil is because in it there is an effort arising from the soul's concern with obtaining evil and its striving to seek it.

Al-Harali said: The form (fa'ala) in its bare state indicates the lowest level of earning (kasb). Therefore, whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is written down for him.

A subtle point:

Al-Jarbardi said in *Sharh al-Shafiyah*: The meaning of kasb (earning) is obtaining a thing in whatever manner it may be, while iktisab (acquiring) is exaggeration and effort in it. Among this is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿It shall have [the reward of] what it has earned, and it shall bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾. In it there is an alert to Allah's gentleness toward His creation, for He affirmed for them the reward of the act in whatever manner it was done, and He did not affirm the punishment of the act upon them except in the manner of exaggeration and effort in it.

(p. 732) Al-Zamakhshari said: Since evil is something the soul desires, and it is drawn toward it and commands it, it is more active and diligent in obtaining it, so it was described for that reason as "acquired" (muktasaba) in it. And since it is not so in the matter of good, due to its sluggishness in obtaining it, it was described with what does not indicate effort and exertion. End of quote.

Al-'Allama Ibn Jama'a said in his *Hawashi*: His distinction between kasb and iktisab is what al-Zamakhshari and others said, and Sibawayh explicitly stated it. Al-Halabi said: This is the more evident. And a group said: There is no difference. They said: The Qur'an has come with kasb and iktisab in a single context. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38]; ﴿And no soul earns [evil] except against itself﴾ [al-An'am: 164]; ﴿Rather, whoever earns an evil deed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 81]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Without what they have acquired﴾ [al-Ahzab: 58], thus using kasb and iktisab for evil. Al-Wahidi said: The correct view among the people of lexicography is that kasb and iktisab are one and the same. In *al-Qamus*: kasabahu yaksibuhu kasban, and takassaba and iktasaba: sought sustenance; or kasaba: attained; and iktasaba: exerted himself and strove. Then Ibn Jama'a said: What he (al-Zamakhshari) mentioned about the verse's alerting to Allah's gentleness toward His creatures, to the end, was said by Ibn al-Hajib in his commentary on *al-Mufassal*. And a similar statement by some of them: In the verse there is an indication that even the least of good deeds is for the human being an act of generosity from Allah toward His servant, unlike punishment, for He does not hold anyone accountable for it except one who exerts himself in it and strives. And close to this is another statement: The soul has whatever reward results, in whatever way it comes about, whether by mere attainment or by acquisition; and it bears what it has acquired and striven for, not what comes about without choice (p. 733) and effort. He, exalted is He, pointed out that the reward is available to it whether it came through its effort and choice or not. As for punishment, it does not fall upon it except through its intention and acquisition.

What they said regarding the distinction needs verification. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7]; ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 8], meaning: will see its recompense. And He said: ﴿And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. Given that the attainment of reward from what comes about without effort and choice, if it is for engaging in its cause while heedless of it, then punishment is likewise. Whoever commits an evil deed bears its sin and the sin of those who act upon it. And if it is pictured as attainment at the first moment of inattention, there is no barrier to punishment being similar to it, and whoever claims otherwise must provide proof. Yes, persistence is a condition, because repentance erases it, but it is an additional matter beyond the act itself. In sum, what the Jar Allah (al-Zamakhshari) said is good, and al-Baydawi also mentioned it. In al-Halabi's *I'rab* (grammatical analysis): What appears in this is that good deeds are things acquired without strain, since the one who acquires them is on the path of Allah's command and the design of His law; and evil deeds are acquired with strain, since the one who acquires them strains in their matter to break through the barrier of Allah's prohibition and oversteps toward them. So the use of both verbal forms in the verse is fitting, to secure this meaning, and Allah knows best. Then Ibn Jama'a said: "Mubalagha" (exaggeration) is from balagha mubalaghatan, meaning exerted himself and did not fall short; and "i'timal" (exertion) is from i'tamala, meaning: worked by himself and applied his opinion and his tool. End of quote.

Al-Biqa'i said: When He gave them this good news, He made known to them the points of His blessings, through a supplication arranged in order from the lightest to the heaviest, by way of ascending, to inform them that He did not hold them accountable for what they had committed through forgetfulness, nor for what they had perpetrated through error, nor did He place upon them a heavy burden; rather He made their law a upright, tolerant religion, and did not charge them beyond their capacity, even though He had all of that power. And that He pardoned them from punishment, then concealed them and did not shame them by mentioning their evil deeds, then showed them mercy by placing them in a station of nearness and making them worthy of succession. Thus it became clear that He would elevate their affair above every affair and make their religion manifest over every religion, since He, glorified is He, is the one who is invoked on their behalf. And so that the entire supplication would be borne by the attainment (of its aim) and encompassed by the answering, He said: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us﴾, that is: do not punish us, ﴿if we forget﴾ Your command and Your prohibition, ﴿or make mistakes﴾ (p. 734), that is: we commit what is contrary to the right, through negligence and the like.

Many exegetes have been eager here to investigate the question: forgetting and error are pardoned, so what is the benefit of asking for pardon for them? They answered this with various responses. The most subtle answer I have seen is the statement of al-'Allama Bir Muhammad in *al-Madhah al-Kubra*: Since those who seek pardon are the Messenger, the Helpers, and the Emigrants, and those of their likeness, it is as though they count forgetting among disobedience and error among sin, like His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60].

It has also been said regarding the meaning of the verse: Do not punish us if we abandon Your command or commit a sin, on the basis that forgetting here means abandoning, and error means sin. And according to this there is no objection, and Allah knows best.

﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden (isran)﴾, that is: a covenant that is heavy upon us.

Al-Harali said: The isran is a heavy covenant, in bearing which there is the greatest hardship: ﴿like that which You laid upon those before us﴾, and it is what the Children of Israel were charged with, which would crush the pillars. There is no harm in pointing to some of the burdens they bore, which we convey from their books, to affirm what leads to gratitude for lightening this from us, and to magnify His favor, exalted is He. So to Allah belongs all praise. We say: In the Book of Exodus, in chapter twelve:

15 * Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day you shall put away leaven out of your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that person shall be cut off from Israel.

And this entire chapter is heavy burdens.

And in the said book, in chapter twenty-one:

15 * And whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

16 * And whoever kidnaps a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

17 * And whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

27 * And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or the tooth of his female servant, he shall let him go free for his tooth.

[p-735] Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 2 of 3):

28. If an ox gores a man or a woman and they die, the ox is to be stoned and its flesh is not to be eaten. As for the owner of the ox, he is innocent.

29. But if it was a goring ox previously, and its owner was warned about it but did not restrain it, and it kills a man or a woman, then the ox is to be stoned and its owner is also to be put to death.

[p-735] In the aforementioned book, in chapter 23:

10. And for six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

This is a brief selection of the burdens that were upon the Israelites, which our Lord, in His grace and generosity, did not prescribe for us. So to Him be praise, for He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.

﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾: that is, from the afflictions of this world and the Hereafter. The first supplication concerns the removal of the hardships of obligation (taklif), and this one concerns the removal of the hardships of afflictions. It is said that it is a repetition of the first, and a depiction of the burden in the form of what cannot be borne, as an intensification. ﴿And pardon us﴾: that is, overlook our sins and do not punish us. ﴿And forgive us﴾: that is, cover over our sins and pardon them. ﴿And have mercy upon us﴾: that is, show us favor with mercy, even though we are negligent and sinful. ﴿You are our Protector﴾: that is, our guardian and our helper. ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾, for it is the right of the Protector to grant victory to His servant and to those who take charge of his affairs over their enemies.

In this there is an indication that raising the word of Allah and striving (jihad) in His way, Exalted is He, as He commanded throughout this noble surah, is the ultimate aim of their pursuit.

Al-Biqa'i said: Thus this includes the obligation of fighting the disbelievers, and that they are the most hostile of enemies. And His saying ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ [al-Baqarah: 256] is not a prohibition against that; rather, it is an indication that the religion has become so clear that no compulsion can be imagined in it. Indeed, it is fitting for every sensible person to enter it with the utmost desire, let alone the need for intimidation. Whoever counsels his own soul enters it by what his intellect indicates, and whoever refuses enters it by force, through the admonition of Allah, which is the striking with the sword and the piercing of arrows.

It has been transmitted in Sahih Muslim from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah, Exalted is He, said after each of these supplications: 'I have done it.'"

[p-739] Al-Bukhari and the group (of compilers) narrated from Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the two verses at the end of Surat al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah from a treasure house beneath the Throne, which no prophet before me was given."

Muslim narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he was brought to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), which is in the seventh heaven; to it ascends what rises from the earth, and it is taken from there, and to it descends what comes down from above, and it is taken from there. [Ibn Mas'ud] said: ﴿When there covered the lote tree that which covered﴾ [an-Najm: 16]. He said: "A flock of golden moths." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given three things: the five prayers were given to him, the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah were given to him, and whoever among his community did not associate anything with Allah was forgiven the grave sins (al-muqhamat)."

From Ibn Abbas, who said: "While Jibril was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), he heard a creaking from above him, so he raised his head and said: 'This is a gate of heaven that has been opened today; it has never been opened except today.' Then an angel descended from it and said: 'This is an angel who has descended to the earth; he has never descended except today.' He greeted (the Prophet) and said: 'Rejoice in two lights that have been given to you, which no prophet before you was given: the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah) and the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah. You will not recite a letter of either of them except that it will be given to you.'" Narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, and this is the wording of Muslim.

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Darimi and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah wrote a Book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and from it He sent down two verses with which He concluded Surat al-Baqarah. They shall not be recited in a house for three nights, but a devil will come near it."

Abd ibn Humayd in his Musnad narrated from al-Hasan that when he recited the end of al-Baqarah he would say: "O what a blessing! O what a blessing!"

This, and many hadiths have been related concerning the virtue of Surat al-Baqarah... Among them is what Muslim and al-Tirmidhi transmitted from the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The Qur'an will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and its people who acted upon it, preceded by Surat al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck three examples for the two, which I have not forgotten since: "They are like two clouds or two dark shades with a radiance between them, or like two flocks of birds in ranks, pleading on behalf of their companion."

Ahmad, al-Hakim and al-Darimi narrated from Buraydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Learn Surat al-Baqarah, for taking it up is a blessing, leaving it is a regret, and the idle cannot master it. Learn al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, for they are the two shining ones, coming on the Day of Resurrection like two clouds or two shades or like two groups of birds in ranks, pleading on behalf of their companion."

Al-Bukhari's and Muslim's... no, correcting myself: this passage is as follows.

Ahmad, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi related from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not make your houses graveyards. Indeed, Satan flees from the house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited." The wording of al-Tirmidhi is: "Indeed, the house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited, Satan does not enter it."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything has a summit, and the summit of the Qur'an is Surat al-Baqarah. In it is a verse which is the chief of the verses of the Qur'an: the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)."

Benefit:

Ibn al-Qayyim said: Reflect upon the address of the Qur'an and you will find a King who possesses all sovereignty and all praise; the reins of all affairs are in His hand, their origin is from Him and their return is to Him. He is established upon the Throne, nothing hidden from Him in any corner of His kingdom, knowing what is in the souls of His servants, aware of their secrets and their open conduct, alone in managing the kingdom. He hears and sees, gives and withholds, rewards and punishes, honours and humiliates, creates and provides, causes to die and gives life, decrees, judges and manages. Affairs descend from Him, the minute and the great, and ascend to Him; not a speck moves except by His permission, and not a leaf falls except by His knowledge. So reflect how you find Him praising Himself, glorifying Himself, and commending Himself; advising His servants, guiding them to what brings their happiness and success, encouraging them towards it, and warning them against what brings their destruction; making Himself known to them through His names and attributes, and endearing Himself to them through His blessings and favours! He reminds them of His blessings upon them, commands them to what makes those blessings complete for them, warns them of His vengeance, reminds them of the honour He has prepared for them if they obey Him and the punishment He has prepared for them if they disobey Him; He informs them of His doings with His allies and His enemies, and how the end of these and those turned out; He praises His allies for their righteous deeds and best qualities, and dispraises His enemies for their evil deeds and ugly qualities; He strikes parables, varies proofs and evidences, and answers the doubts of His enemies with the best answers; He confirms the truthful and refutes the liar, speaks the truth, and guides to the right path; He calls to the Abode of Peace and describes its attributes, its beauty and its bliss, and warns against the Abode of Ruin, describing its torment, its ugliness and its pains; He reminds His servants of their poverty before Him and their dire need of Him in every respect, and that they have no independence from Him for the blink of an eye; He reminds them of His self-sufficiency from them and from all existing things, that He is Self-Sufficient in His own essence above all else, and that everything else is needy of Him; and that no one attains a speck of good or anything above it except by His bounty and mercy, nor a speck of evil or anything above it except by His justice and wisdom. And you witness in His address His rebuke of His beloved ones, the gentlest of rebukes.

Yet with all this, He is the One who sets right their stumbles, forgives their lapses, accepts their excuses, rectifies their corruption, repels harm from them, protects them, helps them, takes responsibility for their interests, rescues them from every distress, and fulfils His promise to them.

He is their Protector besides whom they have no protector; He is their true Master, and He grants them victory over their enemy. How excellent a Master and how excellent a Helper!

When hearts witness in the Qur'an a King who is great, generous, merciful and beautiful, with such qualities, how could they not love Him, vie with one another in drawing near to Him, and spend their breaths in seeking His affection? He would be dearer to them than everything else, and His pleasure more precious to them than the pleasure of anyone besides Him. How could they not cling to His remembrance, making their love of Him, their longing for Him and their intimacy with Him their nourishment, their strength and their cure, such that if they lose this they are corrupted and destroyed, and do not benefit from their lives?!

O Allah, make the Qur'an the spring of our hearts, the light of our breasts, the removal of our sorrow, and help us to complete what we have intended by Your grace. O Most Merciful of the merciful.
